entries.new: The Government of Canada says credit cards are widely accepted in major urban and tourist centres, but you may have difficulty making credit card cash withdrawals, and while there are ATMs in major cities, some do not accept international cards. The UK Foreign Office adds that most major banks allow Visa and Mastercard cash withdrawals.
entries.note: Claims about tuk-tuks, guesthouses and rural areas running on cash are not in any official source read; text now limited to what Canada and the UK say.

entries.old: Duty-free allowance includes 2 bottles of wine and 1.5 liters of spirits per adult; cigarettes are not part of the duty-free allowance and attract high duty.
entries.new: (deleted)
entries.note: Duty-free quantities (2 bottles of wine, 1.5 l spirits, no cigarettes) are not stated by any official source read; replaced with the FCDO declaration rule.

entries.old: No arrival card is currently required for air arrivals — passenger details are captured through the ETA.
entries.new: (deleted)
entries.note: Contradicted: the Government of Canada says you will also need to fill out an online arrival card, which can be completed 3 days before arriving.

entries.old: Apply only at the official eta.gov.lk. Lookalike ETA websites rank high in search results and charge double or triple the official fee, or sell authorisations that never arrive.
entries.new: Apply only at the official eta.gov.lk.
entries.note: The claims about lookalike sites and their fees are not stated by any official source read.

entries.old: The banking system has largely broken down during the war — international cards and ATMs do not work for foreign visitors, so US dollars in cash are essential. Exchange rates vary widely between official and market channels.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says foreign debit and credit cards are not accepted, ATMs serve only local accounts, and international flights and hotel bills must be paid in cash, so bring enough US dollars for your stay. The UK government adds that only US dollar notes dated 2006 or later may be exchanged.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed; unsupported claims removed.

entries.old: November to February is the cooler dry season — in normal times the window for Nile valley trips and the Meroë pyramids, though tourism is suspended by the war.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the rainy season runs from July to September, when flooding regularly makes roads impassable, and that sandstorms occur particularly from July to October.
entries.note: Replaced with the climate statement the cited source supports.

entries.old: Alcohol may not be brought into Sudan. | Photographing bridges, airports, military sites and infrastructure can lead to detention.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says it is prohibited to import or consume alcohol, even in private. | Australia's Smartraveller says you need a permit for photography of any kind, and that even with one you may not photograph military areas, infrastructure or slums.
entries.note: Only what an official source states is kept, attributed; unsupported claims removed.

entries.old: Sudan is in active civil war — governments advise against all travel. Khartoum airport and much of the capital have been battlegrounds, land routes are dangerous, and no meaningful consular assistance is available in-country.
entries.new: Sudan is in armed conflict and governments advise against all travel. Canada's travel advice says drone attacks occur frequently nationwide and that the airports at Port Sudan and Khartoum may close without notice.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: Travelers who do enter must register with the Aliens Department of the Ministry of Interior within three days of arrival (some larger hotels do it for you), and need a travel permit, applied for in the country, to leave the Red Sea State.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says foreigners must register with the Ministry of the Interior's Aliens' Registration Office within 3 days of arrival (some larger hotels do it for a fee), and the UK government says you need a travel permit, applied for in the country, to leave the Red Sea State.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: Evidence of travel to Israel in your passport can lead to refusal of a visa or entry.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the authorities will automatically deny you entry if your passport contains an Israeli stamp.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: Effectively no. Since fighting broke out in April 2023 the country has been in civil war — tourism has stopped, scheduled flights are minimal, and Western governments advise against all travel.
entries.new: Effectively no. Canada's travel advice says heavy fighting has continued across the country since April 2023 and drone attacks occur frequently, and Western governments advise against all travel.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: ["Dutch", "Sranan Tongo"]
entries.new: ["Dutch"]
entries.note: Sranan Tongo is widely spoken but is not an official language. No official source we could read was found for the language field, so it carries no citation.

entries.old: Yes
entries.new: No
entries.note: No official source we could read says tap water in Suriname is safe to drink.

entries.old: Cards are accepted in Paramaribo's larger hotels, supermarkets and a few restaurants, but foreign cards are often declined and ATMs do not always accept them. Bring US dollars or euros in cash to change at a bank or licensed cambio, and carry Surinamese dollars for the interior, where there is no banking at all.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says Suriname's economy is primarily cash-based and only major hotels and some restaurants accept credit cards, and that exchanging money on the street is illegal — use hotels, banks or official exchanges (cambios). The UK government says some cash machines in Paramaribo accept international cards, and to bring US dollars or euros.
entries.note: Rewritten to the Canadian and UK advice; 'no banking at all in the interior' had no source.
Canada gives the rainy seasons as May–August and November–February, so February, August and November were removed.

entries.old: Suriname has two dry seasons — a short one in February and March and a long one from August to November. The long dry season is best for river trips, jungle lodges and the sea-turtle beaches at Galibi.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the rainy seasons run from May to August and from November to February, when flooding can make roads impassable. No official source names a best season; the months shown fall between the two.
entries.note: The river-trip and turtle-beach claims had no official source.

entries.old: Gold cannot simply be carried out of the country — exports are controlled and require documentation. | Wildlife products, including caiman and jaguar items and untreated feathers, are prohibited under CITES rules. | Fresh food, plants and seeds are restricted; declare anything agricultural rather than risk a penalty.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: None of the three notes (gold export controls, CITES wildlife products, fresh-food restrictions) could be confirmed on an official page.

entries.old: Dutch is the official language and the one used on signs and paperwork, with Sranan Tongo as the everyday lingua franca. English is widely understood in Paramaribo's tourism trade but much less so in the interior.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source supports this tip.

entries.old: Carry cash. The Surinamese dollar has been through heavy devaluations, foreign cards are often refused, and prices for tours are frequently quoted in US dollars or euros. Bring clean, undamaged notes to change at a bank or cambio.
entries.new: Carry cash: Canada's travel advice says the economy is primarily cash-based and only major hotels and some restaurants take credit cards. Change US dollars or euros only at hotels, banks or official cambios — street exchange is illegal.
entries.note: The devaluation and tour-pricing claims had no source.

entries.old: The rainforest interior — Bigi Pan, the Upper Suriname river villages, Raleighvallen — is reached by shared taxi and dugout canoe or by a small plane, and effectively has to be booked as a package. Allow a spare day either side of an international flight.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source supports this tip.

entries.old: Suriname drives on the left, a legacy it shares with neighboring Guyana, and the road east into French Guiana ends at a ferry across the Marowijne river. If you plan to drive on, check the ferry timetable and the French border requirements in advance.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says traffic in Suriname drives on the left and that driving conditions may be hazardous during the rainy season.
entries.note: The Guyana and Marowijne-ferry claims had no source.

entries.old: true
entries.new: false
entries.note: No official source on an allowed host states that Swedish tap water is safe to drink; withdrawn under the rule that unconfirmed values are not published.

entries.old: Sweden is close to cashless. Cards and the Swish app are accepted virtually everywhere, and many cafés, buses and attractions no longer take cash at all. There is little reason to change money.
entries.new: The UK government's travel advice says many shops, cafes and restaurants do not accept cash, so make sure you have a debit or credit card with you. Canada's travel advice also says many shops and restaurants no longer accept cash.
entries.note: Rewritten to the UK and Canadian advice; Swish, buses and attractions were not mentioned by an official source.

entries.old: May–September brings long days, archipelago trips and midsummer festivities; December is atmospheric for Christmas markets, and the far north offers northern lights through the winter.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Sweden.
entries.note: No official seasonal guidance found.

entries.old: ["Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, 1 liter of spirits, goods up to €430 arriving by air or sea.", "No limits on goods for personal use when arriving from another EU country; note that strong alcohol is sold only through the state monopoly inside Sweden."]
entries.new: ["Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal lists the duty-free allowance as 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits over 22% (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine), 200 cigarettes in countries applying the higher tobacco limit, and other goods worth up to €430 for air and sea travellers (€300 otherwise).", "Between EU countries no further tax is due on goods for your own use, but each country may set guideline quantities, which may not be lower than 800 cigarettes, 10 litres of spirits, 90 litres of wine and 110 litres of beer (EU Your Europe). Under Sweden's Alcohol Act, retail sale of spirits, wine and strong beer is reserved for a state-owned company."]
entries.note: Allowances restated from the EU's Your Europe page; 'no limits' within the EU was wrong — the EU sets minimum guideline quantities.

entries.old: ... close early on Saturdays and all day Sunday; the minimum purchase age there is 20.
entries.new: State retail monopoly and purchase age 20 per the Alcohol Act
entries.note: Opening hours were not confirmed by an official source; the Act also allows farm sales.

entries.old: hike, forage and wild-camp on most open land for a night or two
entries.new: Canada: camping on public land, not within 70 m of a dwelling or cultivated land
entries.note: Restated from Canada's advice.

entries.old: polar night and serious cold from December to February
entries.new: Winter road conditions and winter-tyre rule (UK advice)
entries.note: Climate claims were not confirmed by an official source.

entries.old: True
entries.new: False
entries.note: No official source we could read says the tap water is safe to drink.

entries.old: widely/low
entries.new: limited/low
entries.note: Card-acceptance and euro claims are not described by any official source we could read; set to the conservative value.
Seasonal recommendation withdrawn; text now states FCDO alpine and wildfire hazards.

entries.old: Swiss Franc (CHF)
entries.new: Swiss franc (CHF)
entries.note: Corrected to the issuing authority.

entries.old: Switzerland is outside the EU customs union: allowances apply even when arriving from EU neighbors — 250 cigarettes, 5 liters of alcohol up to 18% and 1 liter above 18% per adult per day.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source we could read supports this; withdrawn.

entries.old: Goods worth more than CHF 150 per person per day are subject to Swiss VAT on the full value.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source we could read supports this; withdrawn.

entries.old: Switzerland is one of the world's most expensive destinations. Budget roughly double what you would spend in neighboring countries; a simple lunch can cost CHF 20–30.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source we could read supports this; withdrawn.

entries.old: police: 112 · ambulance: 110
entries.new: police: 112 · ambulance: 110 · fire: 113
entries.note: Police 112 and ambulance 110 confirmed by Canada, which also lists fire 113.

entries.old: Satellite phones, drones and professional camera equipment can be confiscated or require permits — journalists need prior accreditation.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says security forces may confiscate phones, cameras and other recording equipment, and that foreign journalists should check Syrian requirements with the authorities before entering.
entries.note: Rewritten to UK FCDO advice; the permit and "any evidence leads to refusal" claims overstate it.

entries.old: Any evidence of travel to Israel in your passport or belongings leads to refused entry.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says Israeli and Iranian citizens cannot enter Syria, and that you may be refused entry if your passport shows previous travel to Israel.
entries.note: Rewritten to UK FCDO advice; the permit and "any evidence leads to refusal" claims overstate it.

entries.old: Most governments still advise against all travel to Syria — if you go anyway, use an experienced local guide, share your itinerary with someone at home and register with your embassy where possible.
entries.new: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Syria because of unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks. It warns that landmines and other unexploded weapons remain in less populated and rural areas: do not step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
entries.note: Rewritten to UK FCDO advice.

entries.old: Travelers with Israeli stamps, visas or any other evidence of travel to Israel are refused entry. Use a clean passport.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says you may be refused entry if your passport shows previous travel to Israel, and that Israeli citizens cannot enter Syria.
entries.note: Rewritten to UK FCDO advice, which says entry "may" be refused.

entries.old: Bring US dollars or euros in cash for the entire trip — foreign cards and ATMs do not work, and crisp, undamaged notes get the best rates.
entries.new: Bring US dollars or euros in cash: Canada says credit cards are not widely accepted, ATMs are not always reliable and sanctions may stop foreign cards working. Exchange money only at banks or official exchange counters — street exchange is illegal.
entries.note: Rewritten to Canadian travel advice.

entries.old: Expect frequent checkpoints between cities. Carry your passport, visa and any permits at all times, and never photograph military or government sites.
entries.new: Canada says roadblocks and checkpoints are common, including on the highways linking Damascus with Aleppo, Jordan and Beirut. The UK FCDO says you must carry copies of your passport photo page and visa, and Canada says photographing military or government installations is prohibited.
entries.note: Rewritten to official travel advice.

entries.old: No — most governments advise against all travel. Damascus, Aleppo and the coast are calmer than during the war years, and organized tours do run, but unexploded ordnance, sporadic fighting, terrorism and detention risks remain real, and consular support is minimal. Anyone going should use experienced local guides and follow conditions daily.
entries.new: No. The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Syria because of unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks, and says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks. It also warns of unexploded weapons in less populated and rural areas and of the risk of detention for journalists and other foreign nationals.
entries.note: Claims about calmer cities and organised tours are not stated by an official source.

entries.old: Cash only. Bring US dollars or euros for your whole stay — international cards and ATMs do not work for visitors — and exchange into Syrian pounds in small amounts as needed. Clean, recent-series banknotes are strongly preferred.
entries.new: Cash. Canada's travel advice says the economy is primarily cash-based, credit cards are not widely accepted and you should carry enough US dollars or euros; ATMs in major cities are not always reliable. Exchange only at banks or official exchange counters.
entries.note: Rewritten to Canadian travel advice.

entries.old: Cards and mobile payments widely accepted in cities; EasyCard for transport and shops
entries.new: No official description of card acceptance
entries.note: The card and EasyCard claims had no official source and were withdrawn.

entries.old: Summer typhoon risk from July to September
entries.new: Typhoons usually May to November (Government of Canada, UK FCDO)
entries.note: Both official sources give a typhoon season of May to November, not July to September.

entries.old: Bringing in meat products is banned under African swine fever controls — undeclared pork products carry very heavy fines. | Duty-free allowances for adults are 1 liter of alcohol and 200 cigarettes. | Fresh fruit and plants may not be brought in without quarantine clearance.
entries.new: Do not bring animal products into Taiwan without authorisation: the UK FCDO says you may face a heavy fine, and customs have increased inspections because of African swine fever in pork products.
entries.note: The alcohol and tobacco allowances and the fresh-produce note could not be confirmed from an official source we could read.

entries.old: Buy an EasyCard at any metro station or convenience store. It works on the Taipei and Kaohsiung metros, buses, trains and in shops, and makes getting around effortless.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source we read describes the EasyCard’s coverage.

entries.old: Submit … within 7 days before you arrive
entries.new: Submit … within three days before you arrive
entries.note: The tip contradicted the sourced arrival-card rule (three days) and the UK FCDO.

entries.old: Tajik, Russian
entries.new: Tajik
entries.note: The CIA World Factbook marks Tajik as the official language and notes that Russian is widely used in government and business.

entries.old: Drones may not be brought in without prior permission. They are routinely confiscated at the border.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official page we could read supports this.

entries.old: Carry a doctor's letter for strong prescription painkillers; some codeine- and tramadol-based medicines are controlled substances.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official page we could read supports this.

entries.old: not safe
entries.new: not stated
entries.note: No official source we could read states whether tap water is safe to drink; now shown as not stated rather than unsafe.

entries.old: Cards are accepted at safari lodges, larger hotels and city supermarkets, but day-to-day Tanzania runs on cash and mobile money. Carry shillings for markets and transport, plus clean, recent US dollar notes for visas, park fees and tips.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says Tanzanian shillings or US dollars are the preferred method of payment and credit cards are not widely accepted in rural areas; ATMs in the main cities occasionally run out of cash. The UK Foreign Office says US dollars are widely accepted in tourist areas.
entries.note: Rewritten to what Canada and the FCDO state; the lodge and mobile-money claims had no official source.
Months now exclude October, which the FCDO places in the short rains; January–February kept as the other dry window. The safari and migration claims had no official source.

entries.old: June to October — the long dry season — is prime time for safaris, Kilimanjaro treks and Zanzibar beaches, with Serengeti river crossings roughly July to September; January and February make a good second window.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Tanzania. The UK Foreign Office says the rainy seasons generally run from the end of March to May and from October to mid-December; Canada gives March to May and November to December on the mainland.
entries.note: Months now exclude October, which the FCDO places in the short rains; January–February kept as the other dry window. The safari and migration claims had no official source.

entries.old: ["Plastic carrier bags are banned in Tanzania — remove them from your luggage before arrival (resealable ziplock bags for toiletries are tolerated).", "Drones require a permit from the Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority, arranged before travel.", "Exporting unlicensed wildlife products, including some shells and corals sold on beaches, is prohibited."]
entries.new: ["The UK Foreign Office says plastic bags are banned: if you arrive by air you will be asked to hand them over, although zip-lock bags used for airline security are not included.", "Canada's travel advice says you must obtain a permit from the Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority to import a drone.", "The UK Foreign Office says exporting wildlife items, including horns and seashells, without a certified export permit from the Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism is illegal, and advises against bringing animal-skin accessories into the country."]
entries.note: Attributed to the FCDO and Canada and aligned with their wording.

entries.old: … travelers have been fined at entry points.
entries.new: FCDO plastic-bag rule
entries.note: Rewritten to the FCDO's wording; the fines claim had no official source.

entries.old: Cards are accepted in hotels, malls and larger restaurants; markets, street food and taxis are cash-first. QR payments (PromptPay) dominate locally but usually require a Thai bank account.
entries.new: No official source we could read describes card acceptance in Thailand.
entries.note: Withdrawn: no official source we could read describes card acceptance.
Months that fall in the rainy season named by the cited source were removed.

entries.old: November to February is the cool, dry season — the most comfortable time across most of the country.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the rainy (monsoon) season runs from June to November and that typhoons usually occur from April to November.
entries.note: Rewritten to the climate statement the cited source makes.

entries.old: Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and 1 liter of alcohol per adult.
entries.new: (removed or rewritten)
entries.note: Not stated by an official source we could read; removed or replaced with what the source says.

entries.old: E-cigarettes and vaping devices are prohibited — possession can lead to fines or arrest.
entries.new: (removed or rewritten)
entries.note: Not stated by an official source we could read; removed or replaced with what the source says.

entries.old: Overstaying costs 500 THB per day (capped at 20,000 THB); overstays of 90+ days trigger multi-year re-entry bans.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says overstaying costs 500 baht a day, up to 20,000 baht, and that you risk detention, deportation at your own expense and a re-entry ban of up to 10 years.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: E-cigarettes are illegal to bring into or use in Thailand.
entries.new: Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal to possess or use in Thailand — the UK Foreign Office says there are no exceptions for tourists or for personal use.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: Thailand has strict lèse-majesté laws — never comment disrespectfully on the monarchy, online or offline.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says criticising the Thai monarchy (lèse-majesté) is illegal, that the law can be interpreted broadly and carries a long prison sentence, and that people have been charged over comments and shared articles online.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: {"general": "112"}
entries.new: {"police": "112", "ambulance": "110", "fire": "115"}
entries.note: 112 is the police number, not a general one: the FCDO lists ambulance 110, fire 115 and police 112 (the Government of Canada lists the same three), and notes emergency numbers are unreliable in Timor-Leste.

entries.old: Duty-free allowances are modest (roughly 200 cigarettes and a small quantity of alcohol per adult). Declare anything beyond personal use.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules about goods you can take into or out of Timor-Leste, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
entries.note: The duty-free figures ("roughly 200 cigarettes") are not stated by any official source read.

entries.old: Malaria and dengue occur year-round. Use repellent and consider prophylaxis for rural stays. Bring any medication you need; pharmacies outside Dili are very limited.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office lists dengue, chikungunya, typhoid, hepatitis and rabies (in Oecusse, Bobonaro and Covalima, and possibly elsewhere) among the health risks, and says medical services are limited, particularly outside Dili; a medical emergency is likely to mean evacuation to Australia or Singapore.
entries.note: "Malaria … year-round" removed: the FCDO health risks for Timor-Leste do not include malaria. The pharmacy claim is unsourced.

entries.old: Atauro Island, a short boat ride from Dili, sits on some of the world's most biodiverse reefs…
entries.new: (deleted)
entries.note: No official source read supports the reef and homestay claims.

entries.old: The US dollar is the official currency (with local centavo coins). Bring cash. Cards work only in a few Dili establishments, and ATMs are unreliable. Small, clean bills are the most practical.
entries.new: The US dollar, according to the Government of Canada, which also says the economy is primarily cash based and credit cards are not widely accepted. Older notes can be refused: Canada says many places will not accept bills issued before 2007, and the UK Foreign Office says notes printed before 2009 are usually rejected but can be changed at the Central Bank in Dili.
entries.note: Centavo-coin and ATM claims replaced with what Canada and the UK state.

entries.old: Cash dominates. Cards are accepted only at larger hotels and supermarkets in Lomé, and ATMs are unreliable outside the capital. Mobile-money services are widely used locally; carry CFA francs for everyday spending.
entries.new: The UK government says Togo is a cash-based society: credit cards are not widely accepted, card machines at the hotels and restaurants that do take cards are unreliable, and some ATMs in Lomé accept international cards.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed; unsupported claims removed.

entries.old: November to February is the main dry season — the best window for the beaches around Lomé, the Koutammakou landscape and hiking in the Plateaux region, though the harmattan can bring hazy skies.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the rainy season runs from April to November, and that the harmattan, a dusty wind from the Sahara, blows from December to March.
entries.note: Replaced with the climate statement the cited source supports.

entries.old: Large amounts of cash should be declared on arrival. Confirm current thresholds with Togolese customs before carrying significant sums.
entries.new: (none)
entries.note: Only what an official source states is kept, attributed; unsupported claims removed.

entries.old: Avoid the Savanes region along the Burkina Faso border — foreign governments warn of a real terrorism risk there; the rest of the country is far calmer.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all travel within 5 km of the border with Burkina Faso and against all but essential travel to the rest of the Savanes region, and says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Togo.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: Keep your yellow fever certificate with your passport. It is checked on arrival and sometimes at land borders.
entries.new: Keep your yellow fever certificate with your passport: the UK government says you must have one to enter Togo.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: Withdraw or exchange CFA francs in Lomé before traveling upcountry. The same currency is used in Benin, Burkina Faso and other WAEMU neighbors, so leftover notes stay useful.
entries.new: Withdraw or exchange CFA francs in Lomé before travelling upcountry. The UK government says Togo is a cash-based society and that some ATMs in Lomé accept international cards.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: Lomé, the coast and the central Plateaux are generally safe, with petty theft the main concern. The exception is the far-northern Savanes region near Burkina Faso, where governments advise against travel due to terrorism risk. Check current advisories before planning a route north.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all travel within 5 km of the Burkina Faso border and against all but essential travel to the rest of the far-northern Savanes region, and says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Togo. Check current advisories before planning a route north.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: Yes. The coastal crossings at Aflao (Ghana) and Hillacondji (Benin) are busy and straightforward for ECOWAS citizens. Other nationalities who need a visa must arrive with an approved eVisa, since visas on arrival are suspended.
entries.new: ECOWAS citizens can cross freely. Other nationalities who need a visa must arrive with an approved eVisa, since visas on arrival are suspended.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: {"general": "911", "police": "922"}
entries.new: {"general": "911", "police": "922", "ambulance": "933", "fire": "999"}
entries.note: Added the ambulance (933) and fire (999) numbers listed by the UK government.

entries.old: Resorts, larger hotels and some restaurants in Nuku'alofa and Neiafu take cards, often with a surcharge. ATMs are limited to Tongatapu, Vava'u and Ha'apai, so carry paʻanga in cash for markets, taxis, boats and outer islands.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says most major hotels and some restaurants and stores accept credit cards, that ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and that foreign currency exchange may be limited on the other islands.
entries.note: Rewritten to Canada's advice; the surcharge and Vava'u/Ha'apai ATM claims had no source.
The UK puts May in the November–May cyclone season.

entries.old: May to October is dry, cooler and outside the cyclone season; humpback whales are in Tongan waters roughly July to October, which is the peak reason most visitors come.
entries.new: The UK government says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May (Canada says November to April), though cyclones can happen at any time, and that whales frequent Tongan waters between June and November. No official source names a best season.
entries.note: Aligned with the UK cyclone and whale seasons.

entries.old: Quarantine rules are strict: fresh fruit, vegetables, meat, seeds, plants and unprocessed wooden items must be declared and are often confiscated. | Firearms, ammunition and offensive weapons require prior police authorization; drugs offenses carry severe penalties. | Taking whale products, turtle shell, coral or protected shells out of Tonga is prohibited.
entries.new: You must declare personal valuables worth 500 pa'anga or more (UK government). | The UK government says the maximum penalty for importing or exporting illegal drugs is 30 years' hard labour and fines of several hundred thousand US dollars.
entries.note: The quarantine, firearm and wildlife-export notes had no official source; replaced with what the UK advice says.

entries.old: Sunday is constitutionally protected as a day of rest: shops, restaurants, flights and most tours stop, and commerce is prohibited. Buy food on Saturday, and expect only resorts and church services to be open.
entries.new: The UK government says Tongan people strictly observe the Sabbath, and that on Sundays recreational activities may be considered disrespectful, except at island resorts. Plan shopping and activities around it.
entries.note: The claims that Sunday rest is constitutional and that flights and commerce stop had no source.

entries.old: Tonga is conservative and Christian — cover shoulders and knees away from resorts, keep swimwear to the beach and pool, and dress up for church, where visitors are genuinely welcome.
entries.new: The UK government says topless sunbathing and public nudity are illegal, with fines of up to 100 pa'anga, and that swimwear is acceptable on the beach or by streams and waterfalls but likely to attract negative attention elsewhere.
entries.note: Rewritten to the UK advice.

entries.old: Swimming with humpback whales is allowed only with a licensed operator and a set number of swimmers in the water. Book a licensed Vava'u or Ha'apai operator well ahead for the July–October season.
entries.new: The UK government says it is illegal to swim or kayak with whales unless you are on a licensed boat with a certified guide, with fines of up to 5,000 pa'anga or 18 months in prison. Whales are in Tongan waters between June and November.
entries.note: Added the penalties and season from the UK advice; the swimmer-number limit had no source.

entries.old: The cyclone season normally runs November to May, and Tonga also sits on an active volcanic arc. Check advisories before traveling in those months and make sure your insurance covers disruption.
entries.new: The UK government says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May but cyclones can happen at any time, and that Tonga lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where earthquakes and volcanic eruptions can trigger tsunamis. Make sure your insurance covers disruption.
entries.note: Attributed to the UK government.

entries.old: There are no ATMs on most outer islands and boat schedules change with the weather. Carry enough paʻanga in small notes and leave a buffer day before your international flight.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and that currency exchange may be limited on other islands. Carry enough pa'anga before you head to the outer islands.
entries.note: The boat-schedule claim had no source.

entries.old: Almost. Sunday trading is restricted by the constitution, so shops, most restaurants, tours and domestic flights do not operate. Resorts feed their guests and church services are a highlight, but plan arrivals, departures and shopping around it.
entries.new: The UK government says Tongan people strictly observe the Sabbath and that recreational activities on Sundays may be seen as disrespectful, except at island resorts; Canada says such activity outside resorts may be seen as provocative. Plan arrivals, shopping and activities around it.
entries.note: The constitutional and closure claims had no source.

entries.old: Only in resorts, larger hotels and some Nuku'alofa and Neiafu businesses, usually with a surcharge. ATMs exist on Tongatapu, Vava'u and Ha'apai but not on smaller islands, so bring Tongan paʻanga in cash for day-to-day spending.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says most major hotels and some restaurants and stores accept credit cards, ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and foreign currency exchange may be limited on other islands. Carry pa'anga cash for the outer islands.
entries.note: The surcharge and Vava'u/Ha'apai ATM claims had no source.

entries.old: Cards work in supermarkets, malls, hotels and larger restaurants in Port of Spain, San Fernando and Crown Point, and ATMs are plentiful in town. Maxi-taxis, route taxis, doubles vendors, beach bars and rural shops are cash only. Keep small TT dollar notes on you.
entries.new: Tobago's official visitor site says Visa and Mastercard credit cards are widely accepted at businesses and ATMs, and that foreign currency can be changed at local banks. The UK government's travel advice says to use well-lit ATMs, withdraw small amounts and preferably do so in daylight.
entries.note: Rewritten to the Tobago House of Assembly's visitor information and the UK advice; claims about cash-only maxi-taxis and vendors were not stated by an official source.

entries.old: January to May is the dry season and covers Carnival, the country's defining event, in February or March. The wet season runs June to December; Trinidad and Tobago sit at the southern edge of the hurricane belt and are rarely hit directly, but heavy rain and flooding are common.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the Atlantic hurricane season runs from early June to the end of November. Hurricanes rarely hit Trinidad and Tobago directly, but storms passing to the north can bring heavy rain, severe flooding and landslides.
entries.note: Dry/wet season and Carnival claims were not confirmed by an official source; replaced with Canada's hurricane-season statement.

entries.new: The UK FCDO says it is illegal to insult the Turkish nation or flag, and a criminal offence to insult the President or Atatürk — including online, wherever and whenever you posted. It also advises not photographing military or official installations, and says you must always carry photo ID such as your passport.
entries.note: Rewritten to UK FCDO advice.

entries.new: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are accepted only by major hotels, airlines and some car rental agencies, and that there are foreign exchange bureaus at most border crossings and in major cities.

entries.old: The two dry seasons — December to February and June to August — are best for gorilla trekking and savannah safaris; rains peak around March–May and October–November, when forest trails get slippery.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Uganda. The CIA World Factbook describes a tropical, generally rainy climate with two dry seasons, December to February and June to August; the UK Foreign Office says flooding and landslides are common in the rainy seasons from March to May and October to November.
entries.note: Withdrawn: the gorilla-trekking and trail claims had no official source; kept the dry seasons the Factbook states.

entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says ATMs are available and credit cards are widely used in cities, but that because of Russia's invasion ATMs might not be refilled with cash, some bank cards might not be accepted, and ATMs and card terminals may not work during power cuts.

entries.new: (removed or rewritten)

entries.old: Ukrainian airspace is closed to civil aviation — enter overland or by rail, most reliably on the trains from Przemyśl (Poland) to Lviv and Kyiv, or via Slovakia, Hungary, Romania or Moldova.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says Ukraine's airspace is closed, so entry is overland or by rail through a neighbouring country; check the travel advice for every country you cross.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: Install an air-raid alert app (such as Air Alert), take alerts seriously and know your nearest shelter — metro stations in Kyiv and Kharkiv double as deep shelters.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says to identify shelter locations in advance and take shelter immediately when an air alert is announced; several air raid alert apps exist, including "Air Alert".
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: Martial law means nightly curfews (roughly midnight to 05:00, varying by region) and military checkpoints. Carry your passport at all times and never photograph checkpoints or military sites.
entries.new: Martial law can bring curfews, more document checks and transport restrictions. Canada's travel advice says to follow local authorities' instructions at all times, including air raid sirens, curfews and evacuation orders. Carry your passport.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: Ukraine treats dual nationals as Ukrainian citizens: men aged 18–60 with Ukrainian citizenship are generally barred from leaving the country under martial law. Ordinary foreign visitors are not affected by exit restrictions.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says Ukrainian and dual-national men aged 23 to 60 are prohibited from leaving Ukraine, and that the authorities may treat you as Ukrainian — for example if you have a Ukrainian parent or were born in Ukraine. Ordinary foreign visitors are not affected by the exit restriction.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: Civilian airspace has been closed since February 2022, so all entry is by land or rail. The most used routes are the direct trains from Przemyśl in Poland to Lviv and Kyiv, plus road and rail crossings from Slovakia, Hungary, Romania and Moldova.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says Ukraine's airspace is closed, so all entry is by land or rail from a neighbouring country. Check the travel advice for each country you travel through.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources say, attributed.

entries.old: No. The country is at war, missile and drone attacks reach cities far from the front line, and most governments advise against all travel. Western regions are calmer than the east and south, but nowhere is risk-free. If you must travel, prepare seriously: alerts app, shelters, insurance that covers war zones, and embassy registration.
entries.new: No. The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to most of Ukraine, and against all but essential travel to some western regions. If you must travel, prepare seriously: identify shelters, install an air raid alert app, and buy insurance that explicitly covers Ukraine.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources say, attributed.

entries.old: No. Exit restrictions apply to Ukrainian citizens — chiefly men aged 18–60 — not to foreign tourists. The important exception is dual nationals: if you also hold Ukrainian citizenship, Ukraine treats you as Ukrainian and the restrictions can apply to you.
entries.new: No. The UK Foreign Office says the exit ban applies to Ukrainian and dual-national men aged 23 to 60, not to foreign tourists. The important exception is dual nationals: if you also hold Ukrainian citizenship, Ukraine may treat you as Ukrainian and the restriction can apply to you.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources say, attributed.

entries.old: Cards work well in cities and contactless payment is widespread, but carry some hryvnia — power cuts and strikes occasionally take terminals offline, and small towns still prefer cash. Declare amounts of €10,000 or more at the border.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says credit cards are widely used in cities, but ATMs might not be refilled, some bank cards might not be accepted, and card terminals may not work during power cuts — so carry some hryvnia as well. Cash of €10,000 or more must be declared in writing when entering or leaving Ukraine.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources say, attributed.

entries.old: Mount Yasur on Tanna and Ambrym's craters are active and their alert levels change at short notice. Go with a licensed guide and check the current level with the Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-hazards Department before booking.
entries.new: The UK FCDO lists active volcanoes on Ambae, Ambrym, Epi, Gaua, Lopevi, Tanna and Vanua Lava, and says alert levels can change unexpectedly and may stop access to an island. Check current levels with the Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-hazards Department and the latest advice with the Vanuatu Tourism Office before you go.
entries.note: Rewritten to UK FCDO advice.

entries.old: Land, beaches and sites such as waterfalls, blue holes and land-diving towers are customary property. Expect a modest fee in vatu paid to the landowner, and always ask before photographing people or ceremonies.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says local customs are strictly observed and should be respected, that beachwear should not be worn away from beaches and hotels, and that some kava bars (nakamals), particularly outside Port Vila, do not welcome women. Ask before photographing people or ceremonies.
entries.note: Customary-fee claims are not stated by an official source; rewritten to UK FCDO advice.

entries.old: A passport valid for more than 6 months on the date you arrive, a confirmed onward or return ticket, proof of accommodation and funds, and a completed arrival and customs card. Biosecurity checks on food, seeds and used outdoor equipment are taken seriously.
entries.new: A passport valid for more than 6 months on the date you arrive, a confirmed onward or return ticket, proof of accommodation and funds, and a completed arrival and customs card.
entries.note: Biosecurity claim is not stated by an official source.

entries.old: Unusually for the Pacific, Vanuatu drives on the right — a legacy of the Anglo-French condominium. Take extra care if you have arrived from Australia, New Zealand or Fiji.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source we could read states which side traffic keeps to in Vanuatu; the historical claim is also unsourced.

entries.old: General: 112
entries.new: Police: 112; Ambulance: 118; Fire: 115
entries.note: The UK FCDO’s Italy advice, which also covers Vatican City, lists 112 for police, 118 for ambulance and 115 for fire.

entries.old: Safe to drink
entries.new: Not confirmed safe
entries.note: No official source we read states that tap water in Vatican City is safe to drink.

entries.old: Museum, post office and shop registers all take cards
entries.new: No official description of card acceptance
entries.note: The card-acceptance claims had no official source and were withdrawn.

entries.old: There are no customs checks between Rome and Vatican City. The boundary is an open square. | Airport-style security screening applies to enter St Peter's Basilica and the Vatican Museums.
entries.new: (none)
entries.note: The notes on the open boundary and on security screening had no official source we could read.

entries.old: There is no passport control between Rome and the Vatican — you cross an invisible line on St Peter's Square. Carry ID anyway, and expect airport-style security to enter the basilica and museums.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source on a host we can cite confirms this tip.

entries.old: The dress code is enforced: shoulders and knees must be covered to enter St Peter's Basilica, the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel — visitors in shorts or sleeveless tops are turned away.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source on a host we can cite confirms this tip.

entries.old: The Pope's general audience is held most Wednesday mornings in St Peter's Square — tickets are free but must be requested in advance through the Prefecture of the Papal Household.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source on a host we can cite confirms this tip.

entries.old: Send a postcard from the Vatican post office. The state has its own stamps and postal system, a small tradition of a visit.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source on a host we can cite confirms this tip.

entries.old: No. There are no tourist hotels inside the walls; accommodation inside is reserved for clergy and official guests. Visitors stay in Rome, where the Borgo and Prati districts put you a few minutes' walk from St Peter's Square.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official source we read describes accommodation inside Vatican City.

entries.old: general 911, police 171, fire 171, ambulance 171
entries.new: general 911
entries.note: The UK and Canada both give 911 for ambulance, fire and police; neither lists 171.

entries.old: Drone equipment, satellite phones and professional camera gear draw scrutiny; journalists have been detained for filming without accreditation.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official page we could read supports this.

entries.old: Airport departure taxes and fees are sometimes demanded in cash at the counter even when they are supposed to be included in the ticket.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: No official page we could read supports this.

entries.old: Do not photograph airports, military installations, police or protests — cameras and phones have been confiscated.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says photographing sensitive installations, including the presidential palace, military sites, government buildings and airports, is prohibited.

entries.old: not safe
entries.new: not stated
entries.note: No official source we could read states whether tap water is safe to drink; now shown as not stated rather than unsafe.

entries.old: Cards work in hotels, malls and upscale restaurants, but street food, markets, taxis and most small businesses are cash-first. Local QR payments are booming but generally need a Vietnamese bank account.
entries.new: No official source we could read describes card acceptance in Vietnam. The UK Foreign Office says to change money only at official exchange counters with a clear sign; changing money elsewhere is illegal.
entries.note: Withdrawn: the card, cash-first and QR-payment claims had no official source.

entries.old: Vietnam spans several climate zones: roughly November to April is driest in the south, while the north is best from October to April; central beaches shine from February to July.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Vietnam. The UK Foreign Office says the rain season runs from June to September in the north and south and from October to December in central Vietnam, and that the tropical cyclone season normally runs from May to November.
entries.note: Rewritten to the FCDO's seasons; the 'best' and beach claims had no official source.

entries.old: ["Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and 1.5 liters of spirits (or 2 liters of alcohol under 20%) per adult.", "No arrival card is required; customs declaration forms are needed only if you carry declarable goods or cash."]
entries.new: ["The UK Foreign Office says to carry prescription medication in your hand luggage with a copy of the prescription, and to declare it at customs if its total import value is over 100 US dollars.", "The UK Foreign Office says vapes and related products are banned and cannot be brought into Vietnam.", "Canada's travel advice says exporting antiques requires permits from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the General Department of Customs; without the paperwork, items may be confiscated."]
entries.note: Removed the unsourced 200-cigarette / 1.5-litre allowance; 'no arrival card is required' is out of date (the FCDO says a digital arrival card is encouraged at Tan Son Nhat). Added FCDO and Canada rules.

entries.new: Canada / FCDO licence rules (they differ)
entries.note: Rewritten to Canada and the FCDO, which state different licence requirements; the insurance claim had no official source.

entries.new: police: 199 / 194 · ambulance: 191 · fire: 191

entries.old: Yemen is a cash economy — international cards are almost unusable and ATMs unreliable, so bring US dollars in cash to exchange. Two rival central banks mean exchange rates differ sharply between Sana'a- and Aden-controlled areas.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says Yemen's economy is primarily cash-based, credit cards are accepted only in some major hotels, and ATMs may only be available in major cities.
entries.note: Rewritten to what the cited official source says.
Months that fall in the rainy season named by the cited source were removed.

entries.old: October to April is the most temperate window and the main Socotra season. The island is largely cut off by monsoon winds from June to September.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the monsoon season runs from April to September, when seasonal flooding can slow overland travel.
entries.note: Rewritten to the climate statement the cited source makes.

entries.old: Alcohol may not be brought into Yemen. It is prohibited and will be confiscated.
entries.new: (removed or rewritten)
entries.note: Not stated by an official source we could read; removed or replaced with what the source says.

entries.old: Drones and professional camera gear attract heavy scrutiny; photographing checkpoints, military sites or infrastructure can lead to detention.
entries.new: (removed or rewritten)
entries.note: Not stated by an official source we could read; removed or replaced with what the source says.

entries.old: Virtually all governments advise against all travel to Yemen because of the armed conflict, kidnapping and terrorism risk; embassies of most countries are closed and cannot help you. Any travel requires professional security arrangements.
entries.new: The UK and Canadian governments both advise against all travel to Yemen, including Socotra; Canada cites armed conflict, terrorist attacks and kidnapping. Any travel requires professional security arrangements.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: Yemen is split between rival administrations — paperwork issued for Sana'a-controlled areas may not be honored in Aden-controlled areas and vice versa, so your sponsor or operator must match your point of entry.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: Withdrawn: no official source we could read supports it.

entries.old: Bring everything you plan to spend as cash — US dollars are the most exchangeable; cards and international ATMs do not work.
entries.new: Bring what you plan to spend as cash. The UK Foreign Office says there are not many ATMs outside Sana'a and US dollars in cash are the most easily convertible currency; Canada says credit cards are accepted only in some major hotels.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed.

entries.old: No. Yemen is in active armed conflict and Western governments uniformly advise against all travel, citing airstrikes, kidnapping, terrorism and landmines. Consular assistance is effectively unavailable inside the country.
entries.new: No. The UK and Canadian governments both advise against all travel to Yemen, and the UK Foreign Office says emergency services have severely limited capacity because of the conflict.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources say, attributed.

entries.old: No — Israeli passport holders are not admitted, and evidence of travel to Israel in any passport can also lead to refusal of entry.
entries.new: Possibly not. Canada's travel advice says you could be denied entry if your passport bears an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian border stamp issued at a crossing with Israel.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources say, attributed.

entries.note: 999 is not listed by any official source read. The FCDO lists police 991, ambulance 992 and fire 993; the Government of Canada lists police 991, medical assistance 991 or 995, and firefighters 993.

entries.note: Article 258 names English as the only official language; Bemba and Nyanja are widely spoken but not official, and were removed.

entries.old: Cards work in Lusaka and Livingstone hotels, supermarkets and fuel stations; markets and rural areas are cash-only. US dollars are widely accepted for safaris and visas, but bring newer-series notes in good condition.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says major credit and debit cards are accepted in larger supermarkets, restaurants, stores and hotels in large urban centres, ATMs are available in main cities, and you should carry local currency when travelling to rural locations. US dollars, British pounds and South African rand can be exchanged at any exchange bureau.
entries.note: "US dollars are widely accepted for safaris and visas" and the newer-notes advice are not in an official source read.

entries.old: May to October is the dry season — prime safari time, hot from September. Victoria Falls thunders fullest from about February to May; by late October the Zambian side can run nearly dry, when the Zimbabwean side keeps more water.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says the rainy season usually runs from December to April, when seasonal flooding can hamper overland travel and rural roads may become impassable; the UK Foreign Office dates it from November to April.
entries.note: Victoria Falls flow-by-month claims are not in an official source read; replaced with the rainy-season dates Canada and the UK give.

entries.old: Drones require prior authorization from the Zambia Civil Aviation Authority. Bring the permit or expect the drone to be held at customs.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says you must obtain authorization from the Zambia Civil Aviation Authority to fly a drone in Zambia.
entries.note: "Expect the drone to be held at customs" is not stated by an official source read.

entries.old: …usually cheaper than separate visas.
entries.new: (sentence removed)
entries.note: The price comparison is not stated by an official source; the rest is now attributed to the FCDO.

entries.old: Victoria Falls is seasonal: spectacular spray February–May, while by October–November the Zambian side can be a trickle…
entries.new: (deleted)
entries.note: No official source read supports the flow-by-month or Devil's Pool claims.

entries.new: general 999
entries.note: Numbers not stated by the cited official source were removed.

entries.old: The gold-backed ZiG (ZWG) is the official currency, but US dollars are legal tender and remain the practical currency for visitors. Bring small-denomination USD notes in good condition, as torn or old bills are often refused. Cards work in larger hotels and supermarkets, but networks are unreliable; cash is essential outside the cities.
entries.new: The UK government says Zimbabwe has a multi-currency system: Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) replaced the Zimbabwean dollar in April 2024, the US dollar remains legal tender and can be used for most transactions, and most suppliers prefer US dollars in cash. There is a shortage of physical US dollars, so withdrawals with an international card are not always possible, change is rarely available, and some businesses do not accept credit or debit cards.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official travel advice says, attributed; unsupported claims removed.

entries.old: The dry season from May to October brings the best game viewing and comfortable temperatures. Victoria Falls is at its thundering fullest from about February to May and at its lowest around November.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the rainy season runs from November to March, when flooding can make roads impassable and cyclones occur, and that veld fires are common in the dry season from April to October.
entries.note: Replaced with the climate statement the cited source supports.

entries.old: Zimbabwe gold (ZiG)
entries.new: Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG)
entries.note: Name as Canada's travel advice and ISO 4217 give it.

entries.old: It is illegal to photograph government buildings, airports, military sites, police and the presidential motorcade. | Camouflage-pattern clothing is prohibited for civilians in Zimbabwe. | Drones may not be flown without prior authorization from the Civil Aviation Authority of Zimbabwe.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says photographing airports, military establishments, government offices, the President's residence and security forces is illegal, as is photographing demonstrations and protests. | Canada's travel advice says it is illegal for civilians to wear any clothing made from camouflage material.
entries.note: Only what an official source states is kept, attributed; unsupported claims removed.

entries.old: Bring enough US dollars in cash: visa-on-arrival fees are payable only in USD, ATMs and card terminals are unreliable, and worn or older-series notes are frequently refused.
entries.new: Bring enough US dollars in cash, in small notes. The UK government says it is not always possible to withdraw cash with an international card, change is rarely available, and you should not accept torn or damaged notes in change.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: Do not photograph government buildings, airports, bridges, military sites or police — arrests over "sensitive" photography do happen. Camouflage clothing is also illegal for civilians.
entries.new: Do not photograph airports, military establishments, government offices, the President's residence, security forces or demonstrations — Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal — and Canada's travel advice says camouflage clothing is illegal for civilians.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.old: US dollars in cash. The gold-backed ZiG is the official currency, but USD is legal tender and is what hotels, parks and border posts actually quote. Bring clean, small-denomination notes and expect change to be scarce.
entries.new: US dollars in cash. The UK government says Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) replaced the Zimbabwean dollar in April 2024, but the US dollar remains legal tender, can be used for most transactions and is what most suppliers prefer. Bring small-denomination notes, as change is rarely available.
entries.note: Rewritten to what official sources state, attributed.

entries.new: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to Afghanistan.
entries.note: Consistency: 197 passport rows still said 'nearly every government' advises against all travel; narrowed to the three governments whose advice we read, as the FAQ and tips already say.

entries.old: Andorra does not require a visa. Travelers who need a Schengen visa to reach Andorra through France or Spain must hold the travel medical insurance the visa requires (minimum EUR 30,000 cover); winter-sports cover is strongly recommended for ski trips.
entries.new: Andorra does not require a visa. Travelers who need a Schengen visa to reach Andorra through France or Spain must hold the travel medical insurance the visa requires (minimum EUR 30,000 cover). The UK government says the EHIC and GHIC are not valid in Andorra and advises comprehensive travel and medical insurance that covers your planned activities.
entries.note: Consistency: 'winter-sports cover is strongly recommended for ski trips' was stated by no source (the cited EU Visa Code does not mention it). Replaced with the FCDO's own advice: 'The European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) and Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) are not valid in Andorra. Take out comprehensive travel and medical insurance before travelling' and 'Insurance should cover your itinerary, planned activities'.

entries.old: Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for more than 100 nationalities
entries.new: Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for about 90 nationalities
entries.note: Consistency: the passport table lists 92 visa-free nationalities (plus 11 CARICOM free-movement), not more than 100 besides CARICOM.

entries.old: Argentina requires your passport to be valid for the duration of your stay; there is no formal 6-month rule, though airlines sometimes apply their own stricter checks.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for the proposed duration of your stay in Argentina; it sets no 6-month rule.
entries.note: Consistency: the FCDO says 'your passport must be valid for the proposed duration of your stay'; the unsourced line about airlines applying stricter checks was dropped.

entries.old: Not a formal requirement, but airlines and immigration officers may ask for proof of return or onward travel and where you will stay.
entries.new: Not a formal requirement, but Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask you to show a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay.
entries.note: Consistency: Canada says 'Customs officials may ask you to show them a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay'; 'airlines' and 'where you will stay' were not stated.

entries.old: No fixed amount is set, but officers may ask about your means of support and travel plans when granting entry.
entries.new: No fixed amount is published, but Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask for proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay.
entries.note: Consistency: aligned to Canada's wording ('proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay'); 'means of support and travel plans' was not stated.

entries.old: Argentina is one of the safer countries in Latin America. The main risk is petty theft — pickpocketing, bag-snatching and phone theft in Buenos Aires tourist areas such as La Boca, Retiro and on public transport. Avoid displaying phones and jewellery on the street.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says thieves and pickpockets operate on public transport and at bus and train terminals, and can snatch a mobile phone while you are using it on the street. In Buenos Aires it advises particular caution in areas including La Boca, Palermo, San Telmo and Retiro.
entries.note: Consistency: 'one of the safer countries in Latin America' is not stated by the FCDO; rewritten to its crime section ('Thieves and pickpockets operate on public transport and at bus and train terminals'; caution in La Boca, Palermo, San Telmo, Retiro).

entries.old: Yes — e-Visa-eligible nationalities can obtain a visitor visa on arrival at Zvartnots Airport and at open land crossings: AMD 3,000 for 21 days or AMD 15,000 for 120 days. Applying online in advance at evisa.mfa.am avoids any line.
entries.new: For some nationalities. Around 20 — including Canada, Mexico, South Africa, Thailand and Türkiye — can get a visitor visa on arrival at Zvartnots Airport and open land crossings outright: AMD 3,000 for 21 days or AMD 15,000 for 120 days. Most other e-Visa nationalities qualify on arrival only if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from the EU or Schengen states, the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia or Japan, or a residence permit from a Gulf state; Taiwanese passports cannot get one. Applying online in advance at evisa.mfa.am works for all of them.
entries.note: Consistency: said every e-Visa-eligible nationality can get a visa on arrival, but the row notes (from the MFA) give it outright to only 20 nationalities; for 46 others it is available 'only if you hold a valid visa or residence permit from the EU or Schengen states, the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia or Japan, or a residence permit from a Gulf state', and Taiwan has none.

entries.new: (none)
entries.note: Consistency: the months shown as best (May, June, September, October) include three months the text itself, from Canada, puts in the rainy season ('from March to June and from October to November'); no official source names a best season, so the months are cleared.

entries.old: Use SPF 50+, a hat and sunglasses, and swim only between the red-and-yellow flags at patrolled beaches.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says riptides are common on Australia's coast and several drownings occur each year: avoid unsupervised beaches, follow lifeguards' instructions and respect the beach flag warning system. The UK's says rip currents can happen at any beach.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. The 3 October rewrite was logged as 'rewritten to what official sources state, attributed' but cites nothing; SPF 50+, hat and sunglasses and 'red-and-yellow flags' appear in neither Canada's nor the FCDO's advice. Rewritten to Canada ('Riptides are common and can be dangerous. Several drownings occur each year ... Respect the flag warning system') and the FCDO ('They can happen at any beach').

entries.old: Distances are vast. Fly between regions, plan fuel and water for outback drives, and avoid driving rural roads at dawn or dusk.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says outback settlements are far apart and isolated: plan your overland route carefully, carry sufficient fuel, water and food, and take care driving in rural areas at night, when roaming animals and road trains are hazards.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH. 'Fly between regions' and 'avoid driving rural roads at dawn or dusk' are not stated by Canada or the FCDO, and the tip cited no source. Rewritten to Canada: 'Exercise caution when driving in rural areas at night ... Roaming animals and road trains pose further hazards ... plan your overland route carefully ... carry sufficient fuel, water, and food supplies'.

entries.old: Australia is a very safe destination with low crime. The real risks are natural: extreme UV, rip currents at beaches (swim between the flags), remote-area driving, and seasonal bushfires and floods. Check local warnings.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says violent crime is low, while petty crime occurs mostly in larger cities and vehicle break-ins are common. The main hazards the Canadian and UK governments describe are natural: rip currents at beaches, remote outback driving, and seasonal bushfires, floods and cyclones. Check local warnings.
entries.note: Consistency: 'extreme UV' was still asserted although no official source we read states it (the sun-uv tip was corrected for the same reason). Rewritten from Canada ('Violent crime is low. Petty crime ... occurs mostly in larger cities. Vehicle break-ins are common.') and the FCDO's natural-hazard sections.

entries.old: Mar · Apr · May · Sep · Oct · Nov
entries.new: May · Jun · Jul · Aug · Sep
entries.note: Consistency: the months shown included March, April, October and November, which the text (Canada: 'The rainy season extends from November to April'; 'Bush and forest fires are common between October and April') puts in the rainy or fire season. The months are now those outside both windows.

entries.old: Goods for your own use bought in another EU country carry no further duty. Above the EU guide levels (for example 800 cigarettes or 10 litres of spirits), customs may ask you to show they are for personal use.
entries.new: Goods for your own use bought in another EU country carry no further duty. Above the guide levels each EU country sets, which may not be lower than 800 cigarettes or 10 litres of spirits, customs may ask you to show they are for your own use.
entries.note: Audit: OVERREACH narrowed. 800 cigarettes / 10 litres are the EU floor, not Austria's level: Your Europe says "each EU country can set their own guideline values ... These guideline values may not be lower than the following: Cigarettes 800 ... Spirits 10 litres".

entries.old: Azerbaijan refuses entry to citizens of Armenia. Travelers of Armenian descent or with evidence of visits to Nagorno-Karabakh also face refusal or removal.
entries.new: Azerbaijan refuses entry to citizens of Armenia. The UK government's travel advice adds that anyone who has visited certain areas in south-western Azerbaijan, including the town of Khankendi, without the Azerbaijani authorities' permission could be denied entry.
entries.note: Consistency: the claim that travelers of Armenian descent face refusal was withdrawn from the tips and FAQ on 3 Oct as unsourced but was still asserted in this row; replaced with the FCDO statement: 'Anyone who has previously visited certain areas in south-western Azerbaijan, including the town of Khankendi, without the permission of the Azerbaijani authorities could be denied entry'.

entries.old: Baku is safe with low street crime. Keep well away from the border with Armenia and do not enter the Karabakh region or other restricted zones without government authorization — landmines and closed military areas remain.
entries.new: The UK government's travel advice says crime levels in Baku are generally low. It advises against all travel within 5 km of the closed border with Armenia (Nakhchivan excepted) and against all but essential travel to some areas in south-western Azerbaijan, in and around the former Nagorno-Karabakh region, because of mines and unexploded weapons; entering certain areas there without the authorities' permission is illegal.
entries.note: Consistency: 'Baku is safe' narrowed to the FCDO's words ('Crime levels in Baku are generally low') and the restricted-area warning restated as the FCDO gives it.

entries.old: If you are eligible for both, the visa on arrival is quickest. It is issued at the airport or the King Fahd Causeway in minutes. The eVisa (evisa.gov.bh) is worth getting in advance if you prefer certainty before boarding, want a longer or multi-entry option, or are only eligible for the eVisa and not for the visa on arrival.
entries.new: If you are eligible for both, the visa on arrival needs no application in advance: it is issued at Bahrain International Airport or the King Fahd Causeway, and the passport officer may ask for a confirmed return ticket. The eVisa (evisa.gov.bh) is worth getting in advance if you prefer certainty before boarding, want a longer or multi-entry option, or are only eligible for the eVisa and not for the visa on arrival.
entries.note: Consistency: 'issued ... in minutes' is stated by no official source (the visa-on-arrival type has no processing time). Replaced with what the data holds: issued at the airport or the King Fahd Causeway (as the passport rows state), with NPRA's confirmed-return-ticket condition from the onward-ticket block.

entries.old: Citizens of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the countries of Europe, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states can obtain a 30-day visa on arrival (US$50 plus processing fees) at Dhaka and other international airports, while other nationalities — including Indian citizens — must arrange a visa through a Bangladeshi mission, starting on the official portal visa.gov.bd, before traveling. Maldivian citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, and the immigration police say citizens of Barbados, Bhutan, Fiji, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago need no visa for stays of up to 90 days.
entries.new: Citizens of the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the countries of Europe, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states can obtain a 30-day visa on arrival (US$50 plus processing fees) at Dhaka and other international airports, while other nationalities — including Indian citizens — must arrange a visa through a Bangladeshi mission, starting on the official portal visa.gov.bd, before traveling. Maldivian citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, and the immigration police say citizens of Barbados, Bhutan, Fiji, Ghana, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago need no visa for stays of up to 90 days.
entries.note: Consistency: the summary listed the nationalities the immigration police checker exempts for 90 days but left out Ghana, whose row in the data is visa-free for 90 days on that checker.

entries.old: Almost everyone needs one, but many tourists get it at the airport: citizens of the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the countries of Europe, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states can obtain a 30-day visa on arrival for US$50 plus processing fees. Other nationalities apply through a Bangladeshi mission, starting online at visa.gov.bd, where the fee schedule lists the fee for each nationality. Maldivian citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, and the immigration police say citizens of Barbados, Bhutan, Fiji, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago need no visa for stays of up to 90 days.
entries.new: Almost everyone needs one, but many tourists get it at the airport: citizens of the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the countries of Europe, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states can obtain a 30-day visa on arrival for US$50 plus processing fees. Other nationalities apply through a Bangladeshi mission, starting online at visa.gov.bd, where the fee schedule lists the fee for each nationality. Maldivian citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, and the immigration police say citizens of Barbados, Bhutan, Fiji, Ghana, Grenada, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Trinidad and Tobago need no visa for stays of up to 90 days.
entries.note: Consistency: Ghana added to the 90-day visa-free list, matching its row.

entries.old: The main tourist areas — the cayes, Placencia, San Ignacio — are generally safe. Belize City has a high rate of gang-related violent crime concentrated on its south side; avoid walking there after dark and use licensed taxis (green plates).
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says Belize has one of the highest per capita murder rates in the world, with serious gang-related violence most frequent in Belize City south of the Haulover Creek (Southside); tourists are not normally the targets but anyone nearby could be affected. It says tourists are vulnerable to theft, including in San Pedro, Caye Caulker, Placencia and San Ignacio. Canada advises against non-essential travel to Southside Belize City.
entries.note: Consistency: 'The main tourist areas — the cayes, Placencia, San Ignacio — are generally safe' contradicts the FCDO ('Tourists ... are vulnerable to theft ... including in ... San Pedro, Caye Caulker, Placencia and San Ignacio'); the green-plate taxi detail had no source read. Restated per the FCDO and Canada.
