entries.old: It depends on your passport. Citizens of 38 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia and the European microstates — enter visa-free for up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, and no more than 90 days in a calendar year) at any international road or rail crossing until December 31, 2026, and CIS citizens and a list of bilateral partners are visa-free too. 76 nationalities (Canada, Japan, Australia and more) get 30 days visa-free only when flying in and out through Minsk National Airport or five regional airports. US, Bolivian and Paraguayan citizens can apply online for a 30-day e-visa. Everyone else needs a visa from a Belarusian embassy.

entries.field: FAQ: do I need a visa
entries.old: Yes, unless you hold an Indian passport (Indian nationals need an entry permit instead). Bangladeshi and Maldivian citizens can get the visa on arrival, though applying online beforehand is recommended. Everyone else applies online at immi.gov.bt — directly or through a licensed tour operator — paying a US$40 visa fee plus the Sustainable Development Fee, and the visa is issued for your exact travel dates before arrival.
entries.new: Yes, unless you hold an Indian passport (Indian nationals need an entry permit instead). Bangladeshi and Maldivian citizens can get the visa on arrival, though the Department of Tourism recommends arranging it beforehand. Everyone else applies online at immi.gov.bt — directly or through a tour operator — paying a US$40 visa fee plus the Sustainable Development Fee, before travel. A tourist may stay for the actual duration of the trip, up to 90 days.
entries.note: "Issued for your exact travel dates" replaced by the Immigration Rules 2023 (rule 56): actual duration of stay or 90 days, whichever is less.

entries.old: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival. Bolivian officials are strict about damaged passports and about visa pages being intact.
entries.new: Bolivia's Migration Directorate asks for a passport valid for at least 6 months with a tourist visa or stay application. The UK Foreign Office says a British visitor's passport should be valid for at least 6 months after the date of arrival, with at least two blank pages.
entries.note: "Officials are strict about damaged passports and visa pages" rests on no official page; the 6-month rule is now attributed to DIGEMIG and the FCDO, which state it.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from or have transited a country with risk of transmission. Bolivia's Migration Directorate also lists a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate among the requirements for a tourist visa or stay permit if you will visit high-risk endemic areas. Vaccination is strongly recommended — and sometimes checked on domestic flights — before traveling to the lowland departments of Santa Cruz, Beni, Pando, Tarija or the Yungas.
entries.new: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from a country with risk of transmission. Bolivia's Migration Directorate also lists a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate among the requirements for a tourist visa or stay permit if you will visit high-risk endemic areas. WHO recommends yellow fever vaccination for travelers aged 9 months or over going to areas east of the Andes below 2,300 m, including the whole departments of Beni, Pando and Santa Cruz and designated areas of Chuquisaca, Cochabamba, La Paz and Tarija.
entries.note: "Or have transited", "strongly recommended" and "sometimes checked on domestic flights" are not on an official page; replaced by the WHO recommendation as WHO words it.

entries.old: Group 2 tourist-visa applicants must show a travel itinerary or return ticket, an invitation from a person legally resident in Bolivia registered with the Migration Directorate, or a hotel booking. Airlines may also check for an onward ticket at check-in.
entries.new: Group 2 tourist-visa applicants must show a travel itinerary or return ticket, an invitation from a person legally resident in Bolivia registered with the Migration Directorate, or a hotel booking.
entries.note: "Airlines may also check for an onward ticket at check-in" rests on no official page.

entries.old: Group 2 tourist-visa applicants must prove economic solvency with a sworn declaration backed by documents, such as recent bank statements. No minimum sum is published, and none is set for visa-free visitors.
entries.new: Group 2 tourist-visa applicants must prove economic solvency with a sworn declaration backed by documents. No minimum sum is published.
entries.note: "Such as recent bank statements" and "none is set for visa-free visitors" are not on the official page.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export any item the Bolivian government considers a national treasure (patrimonio cultural) — including pre-Columbian artifacts, historical paintings, colonial-era items, native textiles, flora, fauna and fossils — without written permission from the Ministry of Culture. | Canada's travel advice notes that it is illegal to import coca leaves and related products into Canada; check the rules of your next destination before carrying any.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export any item the Bolivian government considers a national treasure (patrimonio cultural) — including pre-Columbian artifacts, historical paintings, colonial-era items, native textiles, flora, fauna and fossils — without written permission from the Ministry of Culture. | Canada's travel advice notes that it is illegal to import coca leaves and related products into Canada.
entries.note: "Check the rules of your next destination before carrying any" is advice not on the Canadian page.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says Canadian dollars are hard to exchange in Bolivia and to bring US dollars if you need to exchange cash. Migration fees are set in UFV and paid at Banco Unión, not in cash at the counter.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says Canadian dollars are hard to exchange in Bolivia and to bring US dollars if you need to exchange cash. Migration fees are set in UFV and paid into the government's fiscal account at Banco Unión.
entries.note: "Not in cash at the counter" is not stated; DIGEMIG says payment goes into the fiscal account at Banco Unión.

entries.old: The visa-free allowance is 90 days within a calendar year, not per entry. Leaving and coming back does not reset it, and overstays are fined per day on departure.
entries.new: Bolivia's Migration Directorate puts the maximum stay for tourists at 90 calendar days per year.
entries.note: "Leaving and coming back does not reset it" and "overstays are fined per day on departure" rest on no official page.

entries.old: Ninety days within a calendar year for visa-free visitors. Entry stamps often give 30 days initially. Check what you were granted and request more time, up to the 90-day annual cap, at a Dirección General de Migración office in any major city; the Directorate lists a fee of 250 UFV per period of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Bolivia's Migration Directorate puts the maximum stay for tourists at 90 calendar days per year. The UK Foreign Office says border officials issue 30-day stamps but that you can stay 90 days without any new stamp; Australia's Smartraveller says the stay permitted on entry is 30 days and can be extended to 90. Group 2 tourist-visa holders can apply to the Directorate for up to two further periods of up to 30 days, at 250 UFV each.
entries.note: The FCDO says Group 1 visitors need no new stamp to stay 90 days, and DIGEMIG's 250-UFV procedure requires a tourist or visit visa; the old answer sent every visitor to a migration office. The two foreign advices differ and are both shown, attributed.

entries.old: Group 2 nationalities can, at La Paz (El Alto), Santa Cruz (Viru Viru) and the main land borders. Bring a passport valid for at least six months, a recent 4x4 cm photo on a white background, a travel itinerary or return ticket (or a registered invitation letter or hotel booking), documents backing a sworn statement of your funds, a yellow fever certificate if you will visit high-risk areas, and the fee of 300 UFV, paid at Banco Unión once the officer authorizes it. Processing takes up to 10 minutes at border and airport posts, and up to 30 minutes at a migration office. Applying at a consulate first is slower but avoids surprises at a remote border post.
entries.new: Group 2 nationalities can, at land-border and airport migration posts. Bring a passport valid for at least six months, a recent 4x4 cm photo on a white background, a travel itinerary or return ticket (or a registered invitation letter or hotel booking), documents backing a sworn statement of your funds, a yellow fever certificate if you will visit high-risk areas, and the fee of 300 UFV, paid at Banco Unión once the officer authorizes it. Processing takes up to 10 minutes at border and airport posts, and up to 30 minutes at a migration office.
entries.note: DIGEMIG names land-border and airport control posts generally, not specific airports; "applying at a consulate first… avoids surprises" is not on an official page.

entries.old: Group 3 is the list of nationalities that, according to Bolivia's migration authority (DIGEMIG), need a consular visa to enter. No official source we could read states the fee, how long a consulate takes or the permitted stay, so ask a Bolivian consulate well before you plan to travel. Group lists are revised by decree.
entries.new: Group 3 is the list of nationalities that, according to Bolivia's migration authority (DIGEMIG), need a consular visa to enter. No official source we could read states the fee, how long a consulate takes or the permitted stay.
entries.note: "Ask a Bolivian consulate well before you plan to travel" and "group lists are revised by decree" are not on an official page.

entries.old: It is required if you arrive from or have transited a yellow fever risk country, and Bolivia's Migration Directorate asks for a valid certificate with a tourist visa or stay application if you will visit high-risk endemic areas. Even if you are exempt, vaccination is strongly recommended before visiting the lowlands — Santa Cruz, Beni, Pando, Tarija and the Yungas — and is occasionally checked on domestic flights.
entries.new: It is required if you arrive from a yellow fever risk country, and Bolivia's Migration Directorate asks for a valid certificate with a tourist visa or stay application if you will visit high-risk endemic areas. WHO recommends yellow fever vaccination for travelers aged 9 months or over going to areas east of the Andes below 2,300 m, including the whole departments of Beni, Pando and Santa Cruz and designated areas of Chuquisaca, Cochabamba, La Paz and Tarija.
entries.note: "Or have transited", "strongly recommended" and "occasionally checked on domestic flights" are not on an official page; replaced by the WHO recommendation.

entries.old: Bolivia needs care with altitude, road travel and protests: a State of Emergency is in force over roadblocks, which can close highways at short notice, and the UK advises against all but essential travel to the Chapare region of Cochabamba. Express kidnapping and criminals posing as police are a risk, and taxi robberies have risen in Santa Cruz, La Paz and Rurrenabaque — order radio taxis by phone.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office advises against all but essential travel to the Chapare region of Cochabamba and says a State of Emergency gives police and armed forces powers to remove roadblocks. It says tourists are at risk of express kidnapping, that thieves impersonate police officers, and that robberies from people taking taxis have increased in Santa Cruz, La Paz and Rurrenabaque; it advises ordering radio taxis by phone.
entries.note: The FCDO text is now attributed by name; "Bolivia needs care with altitude, road travel and protests" rests on no official page.

entries.old: Group 3 nationality: Bolivia's migration authority (DIGEMIG) lists it among the countries that need a consular visa to enter. No official source we could read states the fee, processing time or permitted stay, so ask a Bolivian consulate.
entries.new: Group 3 nationality: Bolivia's migration authority (DIGEMIG) lists it among the countries that need a consular visa to enter. No official source we could read states the fee, processing time or permitted stay.
entries.note: "So ask a Bolivian consulate" is advice, not on an official page.

entries.old: Group 1 nationality. No visa needed for tourism, up to 90 days within a calendar year. Entry stamps are often issued for 30 days; more time up to the annual limit is requested at a migration office, which lists a fee of 250 UFV per period of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Group 1 nationality. No visa needed for tourism, up to 90 days per year. The UK Foreign Office says border officials issue 30-day stamps but that you can stay 90 days without any new stamp.
entries.note: DIGEMIG's 250-UFV stay procedure requires a tourist or visit visa; for visa-free visitors the FCDO says no new stamp is needed for 90 days.

entries.old: Chinese citizens are treated as Group 2 and pay for a tourist visa, though Bolivia has periodically eased terms for Chinese tourists. Confirm the current rule with a Bolivian consulate before booking.
entries.new: Chinese citizens are in Group 2 and pay for a tourist visa, obtainable on arrival or at a consulate; it costs 300 UFV.
entries.note: "Periodically eased terms" and the advice to confirm rest on no official page.

entries.old: Bolivia does not recognize Kosovo, so Kosovan passports are not covered by the visa-free group. Apply through a Bolivian consulate, and travel on a second nationality if you hold one.
entries.new: No official source we could read states the rule for Kosovo passports; DIGEMIG's country list does not name Kosovo.
entries.note: Non-recognition and the advice are not on an official page we read.

entries.old: Bolivia recognizes the People's Republic of China and has no Taiwanese mission; Taiwanese passport holders should expect to apply for a consular visa. Confirm current handling with a Bolivian consulate before booking.
entries.new: No official source we could read states the rule for Taiwanese passports; DIGEMIG's country list does not name Taiwan.
entries.note: "No Taiwanese mission", "should expect to apply for a consular visa" and the advice are not on an official page.

entries.old: Bosnia and Herzegovina lets citizens of the EU, EEA and most countries on the EU visa-free list — plus Russia, Turkey, China, Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE — visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180 (30 days for Russians and Ukrainians), while other travelers need a short-stay visa from a Bosnian embassy or can enter for up to 30 days with a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa.
entries.new: Bosnia and Herzegovina lets citizens of the EU, the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and many other countries, including Russia, Turkey, China, Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE, visit visa-free for up to 90 days (30 days for Russians and Ukrainians), while other travelers need a short-stay visa from a Bosnian embassy or can enter for up to 30 days with a valid multiple-entry Schengen, EU or US visa or residence permit.
entries.note: "EEA and most countries on the EU visa-free list" and "90 days in any 180" are not what the Ministry states: most country entries say up to 90 days within six months of first entry.

entries.old: Consular fee for a type C visa. Missions may charge the equivalent in local currency: the embassy in Oslo charges NOK 679. Supporting documents include proof of accommodation, travel insurance covering EUR 30,000, and an invitation or itinerary.
entries.new: Consular fee for a type C visa, as published by the Embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Qatar. Its document list includes a copy of a return air ticket, travel insurance covering EUR 30,000 or USD 50,000 and, for tourists, proof of a paid trip or paid accommodation.
entries.note: The Oslo NOK 679 figure and "missions may charge the equivalent in local currency" rest on no page we read; the document list now matches the Qatar embassy page.

entries.old: Consular fee for a type D visa as published by the Embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Doha; other missions may charge the equivalent in local currency.
entries.new: Consular fee for a type D visa as published by the Embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Doha.
entries.note: Global rule: sentences no official source confirms were deleted; what remains is stated by the cited official page.

entries.old: Your passport should be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from Bosnia and Herzegovina. Carry extra margin to be safe.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must have an expiry date at least 90 days after the date you plan to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina, and a date of issue less than 10 years before the date you arrive. The Government of Canada says it must be valid for at least 3 months beyond the date you expect to leave.
entries.note: Foreign-government advice attributed by name; "carry extra margin to be safe" removed; the FCDO 10-year issue rule added as it states it.

entries.old: Foreigners must be able to show at least KM 150, or the equivalent in a convertible foreign currency, for each day of the intended stay if a Border Police officer asks. Cash or payment cards accepted by Bosnian banks both count, and a certified letter of invitation can serve as proof of means.
entries.new: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina says the minimum means of subsistence for a foreigner's stay is KM 150, or the equivalent in a freely convertible foreign currency, for each day of the intended stay.
entries.note: The cited Service for Foreigners' Affairs page shows only a menu; the KM 150 rule is on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs page, now cited. Border-officer request, cards and invitation-letter details are on no page we read.

entries.old: Foreigners staying longer than three days must have their address registered with the Service for Foreigners' Affairs or the police within 48 hours of entry. Hotels and registered accommodation do this automatically — if staying privately, your host must register you at the local field office.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says that if you visit for 3 or more days you must register with the local police within 48 hours of arrival; hotel staff register their guests, and otherwise you fill in the registration form at the nearest police station. The UK Foreign Office says all foreign nationals must register with the police within 72 hours of arrival.
entries.note: The cited Service for Foreigners' Affairs page shows only a menu; the rule is now attributed to Canada and the UK, which state it.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain from the 1992–1995 war, mainly in less populated and rural areas. Do not step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain from the 1992–1995 war, mainly in less populated and rural areas, and advises not to step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
entries.note: The second sentence is the FCDO's advice and is now attributed to it.

entries.old: Foreign visitors must register with the police soon after arrival — within 72 hours according to the UK FCDO, or within 48 hours for stays of 3 days or more according to the Government of Canada. Hotels usually register their guests; otherwise go to the nearest office of the Service for Foreigners' Affairs.
entries.new: Foreign visitors must register with the police soon after arrival — within 72 hours according to the UK FCDO, or within 48 hours for stays of 3 days or more according to the Government of Canada. The FCDO says hotels and some hostels usually register their guests; otherwise contact the nearest field centre of the Service for Foreigners' Affairs.
entries.note: The hotel sentence is the FCDO's and is now attributed to it.

entries.old: Carry convertible marks in cash outside the main cities: the Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs are limited in rural areas.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs are limited in rural areas.
entries.note: Global rule: sentences no official source confirms were deleted; what remains is stated by the cited official page.

entries.old: If you hold a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa, you can enter Bosnia and Herzegovina without a Bosnian visa for up to 30 days — a common route for visa-required nationalities touring the Balkans.
entries.new: If you hold a valid multiple-entry visa or a residence permit from a Schengen state, an EU member state or the United States, you can enter Bosnia and Herzegovina without a Bosnian visa for up to 30 days at a time.
entries.note: Global rule: sentences no official source confirms were deleted; what remains is stated by the cited official page.

entries.old: Bosnia and Herzegovina is not in the EU or Schengen, so days spent there do not count against your Schengen 90/180 allowance — useful when combining it with Croatia.
entries.new: (tip removed)
entries.note: No official page we read states how days in Bosnia and Herzegovina relate to the Schengen allowance.

entries.field: FAQ: do I need a visa
entries.old: Most Western travelers do not: citizens of the EU, EEA, US, UK, Canada, Australia and the other countries on the EU visa-free list can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and EU/EEA citizens can enter with just an ID card. Russia and Ukraine get 30 days per visit; Turkey, China, Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE get 90 days. Everyone else needs a short-stay visa from a Bosnian mission.
entries.new: Citizens of the EU, the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and many other countries can stay visa-free for up to 90 days, and citizens of EU and Schengen states, Andorra, Montenegro, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Serbia, the Holy See, Switzerland, North Macedonia and Albania can enter with a valid identity card. Russian and Ukrainian citizens get 30 days; Turkey, China, Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE get 90 days. Everyone else needs a short-stay visa from a Bosnian mission, unless they hold a valid multiple-entry visa or residence permit from a Schengen state, an EU member state or the US.
entries.note: "Most Western travelers", "the EU visa-free list" and "90 days in any 180" are not on the Ministry page; the ID-card list is now the Ministry's own.

entries.old: Yes — holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa (or an EU or US one, or a residence permit from any of those) can enter visa-free for up to 30 days at a time, and 90 days in any 180, within the visa's validity, without applying for a Bosnian visa. Single-entry visas do not qualify; confirm details with a Bosnian mission before travel.
entries.new: Yes — holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa (or an EU or US one, or a residence permit from any of those) can enter visa-free for up to 30 days at a time, and 90 days in any 180, within the visa's validity, without applying for a Bosnian visa.
entries.note: Global rule: sentences no official source confirms were deleted; what remains is stated by the cited official page.

entries.old: The convertible mark (BAM, written KM). The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs are limited in rural areas, so carry cash outside the cities.
entries.new: The convertible mark (BAM, written KM). The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs are limited in rural areas.

entries.old: The UK FCDO warns of pickpockets and bag-snatchers in the tourist areas of Sarajevo and other cities, and says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain from the 1992–1995 war in less populated and rural areas. Do not step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
entries.new: The UK FCDO warns of pickpockets and bag-snatchers in the tourist areas of Sarajevo and other cities, and says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain from the 1992–1995 war in less populated and rural areas. It advises not to step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
entries.note: Advice now attributed to the FCDO.

entries.old: Do days in Bosnia count against the Schengen 90/180 limit? — No. Bosnia and Herzegovina is outside the EU and Schengen, so time spent there does not use up your Schengen allowance.
entries.new: (question removed)
entries.note: No official page we read states how days in Bosnia and Herzegovina relate to the Schengen allowance.

entries.old: Bosnia and Herzegovina is safe for visitors, with low violent crime. The serious residual risk is landmines from the 1990s war in remote rural areas. Stay on paved roads and marked trails and heed warning signs. Petty theft occurs in Sarajevo's tourist areas.
entries.new: The UK FCDO warns of pickpockets and bag-snatchers on public transport and in the tourist areas of Sarajevo and other cities, and says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain from the 1992–1995 war in less populated and rural areas; it advises not to step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
entries.note: "Safe for visitors, with low violent crime" is not on the FCDO page; the text is now what the FCDO says, attributed.

entries.old: No official seasonal guidance. The UK FCDO notes that winter tyres and snow chains are required from November to April, and that wildfires are possible from April to October.
entries.new: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Bosnia and Herzegovina. The UK FCDO says that between November and April vehicles must have winter tyres and carry snow chains, and that wildfires are possible from April to October.
entries.note: Global rule: sentences no official source confirms were deleted; what remains is stated by the cited official page.

entries.old: The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based, ATMs are limited in rural areas and credit card payment is not always accepted. Australia's Smartraveller says ATMs are found in major centres and card use is increasing, but you may still need cash in some areas.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based, ATMs are limited in rural areas and credit card payment is not always accepted.
entries.note: The Smartraveller page we read does not carry the ATM and card statement.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period; citizens of neighboring Balkan states can generally also cross with a national ID card.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days, per the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which also lets citizens of this country enter with a valid identity card instead of a passport.
entries.note: The Ministry names Montenegro, Serbia, North Macedonia and Albania as ID-card countries; "generally" removed; the stay window varies by country entry.

entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days, per the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

entries.new: Holders of travel documents from Kosovo need a visa: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina says its embassies in Skopje, Podgorica and Belgrade issue it on a separate sheet of paper.

entries.old: Botswana is one of Africa’s easiest destinations to enter — citizens of some 100 countries, including the EU, US, UK, most of the Commonwealth and most SADC states, get up to 90 visa-free days, while the remaining nationalities apply through the official eVisa portal or a Botswana mission before traveling.
entries.new: Citizens of some 100 countries, including the EU, US, UK, most of the Commonwealth and most SADC states, enter Botswana visa-free for up to 90 days, while the remaining nationalities apply through the official eVisa portal, an immigration office or a Botswana mission before travelling.

entries.old: BWP 300 for a single-entry tourist visa of up to one month; BWP 500 for multiple entries over up to three months.
entries.new: BWP 300 for a single-entry visa for a period of up to three months; BWP 500 for multiple entries over up to three months.
entries.note: The eVisa terms give BWP 300 for a single entry for up to 3 months, not one month.

entries.old: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months, with at least three unused pages — more if you are combining Botswana with neighboring countries.
entries.new: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months, with at least three unused pages.

entries.old: Insurance is not an entry condition, but private clinics expect payment up front and safari areas are remote — cover including medical evacuation is strongly advisable.
entries.new: Insurance is not among the documents Botswana's tourism visa application requires, and no official source we could read states an insurance requirement for visitors.

entries.old: Cash of BWP 10,000 or more, in pula or foreign currency, must be declared when you enter Botswana; failing to declare can lead to prosecution.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says cash of BWP 10,000 or more, in pula or foreign currency, must be declared when you enter Botswana, and that failing to declare can lead to prosecution.

entries.old: Attacks on tourists are rare, but violent crime is increasing, particularly in Gaborone, Francistown and Maun, and there have been isolated thefts from lodges in the Chobe area. Outside the towns, stray wildlife and livestock make driving dangerous, especially after dark; carry water and fuel on trips to remote areas.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says attacks on tourists are rare, but violent crime is increasing, particularly in Gaborone, Francistown and Maun, and there have been isolated thefts from lodges in the Chobe area. It says stray wildlife and livestock make driving outside the major urban areas dangerous, especially after dark, and advises taking water and fuel on trips to remote areas.

entries.old: Botswana is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by nation
entries.new: Botswana is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. No official source we could read states whether a permit is required in addition to a national licence, or for how long a foreign licence may be used.

entries.old: Australia's Smartraveller says malaria occurs throughout Botswana and is widespread in the north, especially in the rainy season from November to March, and suggests considering malaria prevention if you travel north of Gaborone. Use insect repellent.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says malaria occurs throughout Botswana and is widespread in the north, especially in the rainy season from November to March, and advises using insect repellent and insect-proof accommodation.

entries.old: Visa-free visitors may spend at most 90 days in Botswana within any 12-month period — extensions beyond your stamped stay are requested at an immigration office before it expires.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says visitors can stay in Botswana for up to 90 days without a visa.

entries.old: Most visitors do not — citizens of around 100 countries, including the US, UK, EU members, most Commonwealth states and most SADC states, enter visa-free for up to 90 days. entries.field: Summary (euro clause rested on foreign advice; "enter freely" wording)
entries.old: Bulgaria is now a full Schengen member (air and sea borders from March 2024, land borders from January 2025) and adopted the euro in January 2026: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen Area, and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa.
entries.new: Bulgaria is a full Schengen member (air and sea borders from March 2024, land borders from January 2025): EU and EFTA citizens need no visa, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen Area, and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa.

entries.field: FAQ: need a visa (ID-card claim not on a page read)
entries.old: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely with a passport or ID card. Citizens of around 60 countries — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan — can visit visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen Area. Everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa from a Bulgarian mission.

entries.old: ETIAS is the EU's travel authorization for visa-exempt visitors. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once mandatory, it will cost €20 (free for under-18s and over-70s) and cover Bulgaria along with the rest of the Schengen Area.
entries.new: ETIAS is the EU's travel authorization for visa-exempt visitors. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. It will cost €20 (free for under-18s and over-70s) and cover Bulgaria along with the rest of the Schengen Area.

entries.field: FAQ: longer stays (residence-permit conversion and extension claims not on a page read)
entries.old: Apply for a long-stay (type D) visa at the Bulgarian mission in your country of residence, tied to a purpose such as work, study or retirement, and then convert it to a residence permit in Bulgaria. The Schengen short-stay allowance itself cannot be extended.
entries.new: Apply for a long-stay (type D) visa at a Bulgarian diplomatic or consular mission; a personal interview is obligatory. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs sets the application charge at EUR 100, or EUR 200 for applications under article 15(2) of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act.

entries.field: Tip: Schengen ("no routine checks" with Greece paraphrase replaced by the MFA wording)
entries.old: Bulgaria is now fully in Schengen. There are no routine checks at land borders with Greece and Romania, and your days in Bulgaria count against the same 90/180 Schengen allowance as France or Germany.
entries.new: Bulgaria is fully in Schengen: checks on persons at its internal land borders were lifted on 1 January 2025, and since 31 March 2024 days spent in Bulgaria count towards the same 90-days-in-180 Schengen allowance as the rest of the area.

entries.old: The UK Foreign Office reports unlicensed taxis overcharging passengers from Sofia airport: use the official taxi booking office in the arrivals hall, check the licence sticker and tariffs on the window, and check that the meter is working.

entries.field: Tip: ETIAS official site ("inflated fees" replaced by the EU FAQ wording)
entries.old: Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, apply only at the official travel-europe.europa.eu site — unofficial sites charge inflated fees for the €20 authorization.
entries.new: Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, the EU says its official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu) is the only EU site that takes applications directly, at EUR 20, and that intermediary websites may charge additional fees.

entries.field: Passport validity (EU/EEA ID-card clause not on the cited page)

entries.old: …severe shortages of fuel, water, food and medicines…
entries.new: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cuba. Repeated collapses of the national electricity grid and shortages of fuel, electricity, water and basic necessities disrupt transport, medical care and communications, and have led to frequent protests. Cuba's international airports have run out of aviation fuel, only Terminal 3 at Havana's José Martí airport is operating, and several airlines have suspended flights. Opportunistic crime is rising, including muggings in Havana, though overall levels remain lower than in the UK.
entries.note: Corrected to the FCDO's wording (fuel, electricity, water and basic necessities).

entries.new: The Dominican Republic admits tourists from the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and most of the Americas visa-free for 30 days (extendable up to 120), requires every traveler to complete the free digital e-Ticket form for both arrival and departure, and waives its visa entirely for anyone holding a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen multiple-entry visa or permanent residence.

entries.old: For tourists, the Dominican Republic requires your passport to be valid for the duration of your stay. entries.new: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for the Dominican Republic. The Government of Canada says medical facilities may require payment up front and that private hospitals may ask to see proof of insurance before admitting you.

entries.note: The imperative "carry proof" is not an official statement; the two governments' wording is kept, attributed.

entries.old: No minimum amount is published. Canada's travel advice says you may need to prove adequate funds for the duration of your stay when you enter, and give the address where you will be staying.

entries.new: Every passenger entering or leaving the Dominican Republic must complete the digital e-Ticket, a form required by the Dirección General de Migración and the Dirección General de Aduanas. The Dirección General de Migración says the e-Ticket is free and that unofficial lookalike sites charge for it, so use only the official eticket.migracion.gob.do site.

Under Decree No. 691-07, nationals of visa-required countries (such as China, India, the Philippines or Vietnam) who hold permanent residence or a valid multiple-entry visa for the United States, the European Union (Schengen), Canada or the United Kingdom can enter for tourism with just a valid passport and a tourist card.

Keep valuables out of sight, use trusted transport, and avoid remote areas after dark.
entries.new: The UK government describes the crime rate as high, from bag-snatching and pickpocketing to violent crime and carjacking. entries.old: Ecuador has one of the most open visa policies in the world: most nationalities enter visa-free for up to 90 days within a 12-month period, while a negative list of about 45, including India, the Philippines, Vietnam, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cuba, Nigeria, Pakistan, Venezuela and, since the 2024 suspension of its waiver, China, need a visa before travel. Andean Community citizens travel on a national ID card.

entries.old: Arrivals from Colombia, Peru, Bolivia and Brazil no longer need a yellow fever certificate: on 28 August 2025 the Ministry of Public Health dropped the requirement it had imposed in April 2025 and now recommends vaccination at least 10 days before travel, especially for the Amazon provinces (Sucumbíos, Napo, Orellana, Pastaza, Morona Santiago, Zamora Chinchipe). The ministry's notice does not address WHO's listing (2022) of a certificate for travellers aged 1 or over arriving from the Democratic Republic of the Congo or Uganda, or after more than 12 hours' transit there, so carry one on that routing. It is not needed for Quito, the Galápagos or the highlands.
entries.new: Arrivals from Colombia, Peru, Bolivia and Brazil no longer need a yellow fever certificate: on 28 August 2025 the Ministry of Public Health dropped the requirement it had imposed in April 2025 and now recommends vaccination at least 10 days before travel, especially for travellers heading to jungle areas. WHO's 2022 country list gives a certificate requirement for travellers aged 1 or over arriving from the Democratic Republic of the Congo or Uganda, or after more than 12 hours' transit there; the ministry's notice does not address it.

The Galápagos Governing Council charges USD 20 for the Transit Control Card, bought at its counter in Quito or Guayaquil airport before check-in and paid again on every trip. The Galápagos National Park charges foreign tourists an entrance fee of USD 200 (USD 100 under 12, and USD 100 for adult citizens of Andean Community and Mercosur countries). Budget for both.
entries.new: The Galápagos Governing Council charges USD 20 for the Transit Control Card, bought at its counter in Quito or Guayaquil airport and paid again on every trip.

entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says many parts of Ecuador are at high altitude, that you can develop altitude sickness above 2,500 m, and that your travel insurance should cover emergency evacuation from altitude.

Check current advice and follow local authorities.

entries.field: FAQ: do I need a visa
entries.old: Probably not. Ecuador waives visas for most nationalities, giving up to 90 days within a 12-month period. The exceptions are about 45 nationalities that need a visa before travel, including India, the Philippines, Vietnam, Kenya, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cuba, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iraq, Libya, Myanmar, Nigeria, North Korea, Pakistan, Senegal, Somalia, Sri Lanka, Syria, Venezuela and Yemen, plus China since Ecuador suspended the Chinese waiver in 2024. The list has changed several times, so confirm before booking.

The Foreign Ministry lists 45 nationalities that must hold a visa, including India, the Philippines, Vietnam, Kenya, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cuba, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iraq, Libya, Myanmar, Nigeria, North Korea, Pakistan, Senegal, Somalia, Sri Lanka, Syria, Venezuela, Yemen and China.

entries.old: Ninety days within any 12-month period. That allowance is cumulative across all your visits in the year, so a border run does not reset it. An extension of up to a further 90 days can be applied for through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, for a fee, before your current permission expires.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says visitors can stay without a visa for up to 90 days in any 12-month period, and can pay to extend their stay by a further 90 days, applying before the first 90-day period ends.

entries.old: No separate visa — the Galápagos is part of Ecuador — but there are extra steps. The UK government says you need evidence of a hotel booking or an invitation letter, a return flight to the mainland, a Transit Control Card bought at your departure airport before check-in, and travel health insurance, which is mandatory for foreign tourists. Tourists can stay up to 60 days a year. The Galápagos Governing Council charges USD 20 for the Transit Control Card, and the Galápagos National Park charges foreign tourists over 12 an entrance fee of USD 200 (USD 100 for citizens of Andean Community and Mercosur countries).

entries.old: Ecuador's security situation deteriorated sharply from 2023, with gang violence, armed robbery, express kidnappings and repeated states of emergency. The UK advises against all but essential travel to the coastal provinces of Esmeraldas, Manabí, Santa Elena, Guayas (including Guayaquil, except airside transit at its airport), El Oro, Los Ríos and Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, and to within 20 km of the Colombian border. A 60-day state of emergency declared on 15 September 2026 covers eight provinces, including Pichincha (Quito), with midnight-to-5am curfews in four of them (El Oro, Guayas, Los Ríos and Manabí) from 17 to 30 September. The highlands outside those areas and the Galápagos are not covered by the advice against travel, but check current advice before you go.

entries.old: Estonia is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180-day period (ETIAS is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa. Russian citizens face additional entry restrictions even with a valid Schengen visa.

entries.new: Visa-exempt travellers will need an ETIAS travel authorisation to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The official EU site is travel-europe.europa.eu.

entries.old: Estonia is a very safe destination with low crime. Take normal precautions against pickpocketing in Tallinn’s Old Town in high season, and take care on icy pavements in winter.

entries.old: Estonia is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Estonia yet.

entries.old: Ordinary Chinese passports are covered by the Fiji–China mutual visa-exemption agreement, which allows a shorter visa-free stay than the general four-month permit. Confirm the current limit with Fiji Immigration for longer trips.
entries.new: On the Fiji Immigration Department's list of visa-exempted countries. A visitor permit for up to four months is issued on arrival, and it can be extended by two months.
entries.note: China is on the Ministry of Immigration's visa-exempted list with no shorter limit; no official page read states a shorter stay under a Fiji–China agreement. Stay set to the four-month permit (+2-month extension) the ministry states for visitors.

entries.old: Fiji withdrew its recognition of Kosovo in 2017, so Kosovan passports are not covered by the visa exemption — contact Fiji Immigration before traveling.
entries.new: Not on Fiji's visa-exemption list. Apply for a visa online through the Ministry of Immigration's IMMIHUB portal before travelling: Fiji's Ministry of Immigration says travellers from non-visa-exempt countries must obtain an approved visa before travelling to Fiji.
entries.note: 'withdrew its recognition of Kosovo in 2017' is on no official page read; Kosovo is simply absent from the exemption list.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, which for most visitors only matters if the trip routes through South America or Africa. No vaccination is required for arrivals from Australia, New Zealand, Asia, North America or Europe.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.
entries.note: Removed the age threshold and the claims about which regions do not need it: the cited page states neither.

entries.old: At border control visitors must show an onward or return ticket and a valid visa for the next country they are travelling to. Fiji's immigration ministry likewise asks for an onward ticket for the next destination after Fiji.
entries.new: Fiji's Ministry of Immigration asks for a confirmed return ticket or applicable onward travel ticket. The UK Foreign Office says that at border control you must also show a valid visa for the next country you are travelling to.

entries.old: Visitors are expected to show sufficient funds to support themselves without working. A card statement or cash is enough. No fixed figure is published, and in practice officers only ask when the stay is long or the itinerary is vague.
entries.new: Fiji's Ministry of Immigration asks for funds sufficient to cover the duration of your stay. No official source we could read states a fixed amount.
entries.note: Removed 'a card statement or cash is enough' and 'in practice officers only ask when…': no official page says so.

entries.old: Amounts of FJD 10,000 or more in cash (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival and departure.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says you must declare currency worth more than FJD 5,000 when entering Fiji and more than FJD 10,000 when leaving, and that undeclared money can lead to a fine or a prison sentence. The UK Foreign Office gives a single threshold: cash worth FJD 10,000 or more.
entries.note: Two foreign-government sources disagree on the entry threshold (Canada FJD 5,000 on entry; UK FJD 10,000); same rank, no dates, the stricter wins and the UK figure is recorded as the conflict.

entries.old: Fiji is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national …
entries.new: Fiji is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. The UK Foreign Office says you can use a UK driving licence to drive in Fiji. No official source we could read states for how long a foreign licence may be used.
entries.note: Replaced 'have not been checked for Fiji yet' with what the UK Foreign Office states.

entries.old: The Government of Canada says the rainy and cyclone season runs from November to April, and the UK Foreign Office notes that cyclones can occur throughout the year. Cyclones can cause flooding and landslides that block roads, including access to the airport, so keep an eye on forecasts and make sure your insurance covers weather disruption.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says the rainy and cyclone season runs from November to April, and the UK Foreign Office notes that cyclones can occur throughout the year and can cause flooding and landslides that damage or block roads. The UK Foreign Office points to weather updates from the Fiji Meteorological Service.
entries.note: Removed 'including access to the airport' and the insurance advice: no official page says so.

entries.old: Visa-exempt visitors are granted a free visitor permit of up to four months on arrival, which can be extended to a maximum of six months in any twelve.
entries.new: Visa-exempt visitors are granted a visitor permit of up to four months on arrival; Fiji's Ministry of Immigration says it can be extended by two months if you apply for an extension and pay the fee.
entries.note: Corrected: 'free' and 'maximum of six months in any twelve' are on no official page; the ministry states a two-month extension.

entries.old: Probably not. More than a hundred nationalities — all EU and EEA states, the UK, Ireland, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, India, most Commonwealth countries and every Pacific Islands Forum neighbor — get a free visitor permit stamped on arrival for up to four months. If your country is not on that list you must apply to the Fiji Immigration Department before you travel…
entries.new: Probably not. More than a hundred nationalities on Fiji's visa-exemption list — all EU and EEA states, the UK, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea and India among them — receive a visitor permit of up to four months on arrival. If your country is not on that list you must obtain an approved visa from Fiji's Ministry of Immigration before you travel.
entries.note: Removed 'free', 'stamped', 'most Commonwealth countries' and 'every Pacific Islands Forum neighbor'.

entries.old: Visa-exempt visitors are normally granted four months on arrival; ordinary Chinese passports get a shorter 30-day stay under the Fiji–China agreement. That can be extended in further blocks at an Immigration office, but the total visitor stay is limited to six months within any twelve-month period, after which you need a different permit category.
entries.new: Visa-exempt visitors are granted a visitor permit of up to four months on arrival. Fiji's Ministry of Immigration says the stay can be extended by two months if you apply for an extension and pay the fee.
entries.note: Removed the 30-day Chinese stay (no official page; China is on the exemption list) and the 'six months within any twelve' cap and 'further blocks' (the ministry states a two-month extension).

entries.old: A passport valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay, a confirmed onward or return ticket, the address of your first accommodation, and a completed arrival card with the biosecurity declaration. Officers may also ask how you will fund the stay.
entries.new: Fiji's Ministry of Immigration lists a passport valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay, sufficient funds for the stay, confirmed accommodation, a confirmed return or onward ticket, and a visa or permit where one is required. The Biosecurity Authority of Fiji gives every arriving passenger an arrival card, which is also the biosecurity declaration.

entries.old: The Government of Canada gives the rainy and cyclone season as November to April, but the UK Foreign Office notes that cyclones can occur throughout the year. Cyclones can bring strong winds, heavy rain, flooding and landslides that block roads, including to the airport. If you travel in those months, choose flexible tickets and insurance that covers weather disruption.
entries.new: The Government of Canada gives the rainy and cyclone season as November to April, but the UK Foreign Office notes that cyclones can occur throughout the year. It says they can bring strong winds and heavy rain, and flooding and landslides that damage or block roads.
entries.note: Removed the advice to choose flexible tickets and weather-disruption insurance, and 'including to the airport': no official page says so.

entries.new: https://immigration.gov.fj/application-forms-publications-fees

entries.old: Finland is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180-day period (ETIAS is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa. The land border with Russia is closed, and Russian citizens on Schengen tourist visas are refused entry.
entries.new: Finland is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180-day period (ETIAS is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa. The land border with Russia is closed, and Finland restricts non-essential travel by Russian citizens.

entries.old: A Schengen visa is required, but Finland has closed its land border crossings with Russia and refuses entry to Russian citizens traveling on Schengen visas issued for tourism — only narrow exemptions (family, work, study, humanitarian) apply. The EU’s visa facilitation agreement is suspended: fees are higher (€90) and processing slower.
entries.new: A Schengen visa is required (€90). The Finnish Border Guard says Finland restricts the non-essential travel of Russian citizens to Finland and to the Schengen Area via Finland; listed groups such as family members, work-visa holders, business travellers, students and patients are exempt, and entry is decided case by case at the border check. All land border crossings with Russia are closed.
entries.note: Global rule pass: sentences no official page states were removed; the rest was checked against the cited official page.

entries.old: €95 when applied for through the electronic e-service; €120 on a paper application. Issued mainly alongside residence-permit decisions for workers, students, researchers and their families. Most stays over 90 days are handled as residence permits through the Finnish Immigration Service (Migri). Confirm current conditions with the Finnish mission.
entries.new: €95 when applied for through the electronic e-service; €120 on a paper application. Finland grants a D visa only to applicants who have a residence permit for Finland; it is valid for 100 days.

entries.new: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay.

entries.new: Finland requires a minimum of €50 per person per day of the stay, and the funds must also cover the return or onward journey.

entries.new: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. Your passport is not stamped.

It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.
entries.new: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch.

entries.new: The UK FCDO and the Government of Canada say all land border crossings between Finland and Russia are closed until further notice. The Finnish Border Guard says Finland restricts non-essential travel by Russian citizens.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says winter daylight hours are very short, so you will drive in darkness for most of the day, and icy roads are common and can close roads, particularly in the north. Winter tyres are mandatory from 1 November to 31 March.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says winter daylight hours are very short, so you will drive in darkness for most of the day, and icy roads are common and can close roads, particularly in the north. Finland's Road Traffic Act requires winter tyres from November to March when the weather or road conditions call for them.

entries.new: Sweden, Norway and Estonia are also in the Schengen Area, so your 90/180-day allowance is shared across all of them.
entries.note: Global rule pass: sentences no official page states were removed; the rest was checked against the cited official page.

The Finnish Border Guard says Finland restricts non-essential travel by Russian citizens, with exemptions for listed groups such as family members, workers, students and patients.

It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU ETIAS site for the current status.

It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch.

entries.old: For stays over 90 days: work, family and other long-stay purposes. Many long-stay visas act as residence permits (VLS-TS) and must be validated online within 3 months of arrival. Confirm the fee for your category on France-Visas.
entries.new: For stays over 90 days: work, family and other long-stay purposes. Many long-stay visas act as residence permits (VLS-TS) and must be validated online within 3 months of arrival, with a tax on top of the visa fee.

entries.old: Reduced fee for students going through the Études en France / Campus France procedure; €99 otherwise. Requires proof of enrollment, funds and accommodation. Confirm the current fee on France-Visas.
entries.new: Reduced fee for students whose application was examined by a Centre pour les études en France (Campus France); €99 otherwise.

entries.old: For highly skilled employees, investors, researchers, artists and start-up founders; leads to a multi-year residence permit of up to 4 years. Confirm your category's conditions on France-Visas.
entries.new: France-Visas lists €99 for long-stay visas.

entries.old: Requires a work authorization obtained by the employer in France before the visa application.
entries.new: France-Visas lists €99 for long-stay visas.

entries.old: France scales the means requirement by accommodation: roughly €65 per day with prepaid accommodation, €120 per day without proof of accommodation, and about €32.50 per day with a validated attestation d'accueil (host certificate). Confirm current figures on France-Visas.
entries.new: France scales the means requirement by accommodation: €65 per day with proof of a hotel reservation, €120 per day without one, and €32.50 per day with an attestation d'accueil (host certificate).

entries.old: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.
entries.new: Non-EU travellers are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders: on the first crossing since the EES started, border officers take a facial photo and/or scan fingerprints. The EU says this can be quicker if you register some of your data in advance, at a self-service system or through a mobile app where one is available.

It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.
entries.new: Visa-exempt travellers will need an ETIAS travel authorisation to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The official EU site is travel-europe.europa.eu.

entries.old: France is a safe destination overall. The main risks for visitors are pickpocketing on the Paris metro and around major sights, common tourist scams, and occasional demonstrations or transport strikes.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in France, that pickpockets can work in gangs, and that demonstrations can take place with little or no warning, particularly in cities. Canada's travel advice says strikes occur regularly, particularly in transport.

entries.old: France is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for France yet.
entries.new: France is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. No official source we could read states whether a permit is required in addition to a national licence, or for how long a foreign licence may be used.

entries.old: The UK government says thieves and pickpockets operate on the Paris Métro, on RER lines and at mainline stations, sometimes in gangs where one person distracts you. Keep your passport, cards and valuables in separate bags or pockets.
entries.new: The UK government says thieves and pickpockets operate on the Paris Métro, on RER lines and at mainline stations, sometimes in gangs where one person distracts you, and advises keeping your passport, cards and valuables in separate bags or pockets.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says strikes occur regularly, particularly in transport, and Australia's Smartraveller says they can affect trains and flights. Check the status of your trains and flights before travel days and build in slack.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says strikes occur regularly, particularly in transport, and Australia's Smartraveller says strikes are frequent across France and bring significant disruptions, particularly to public transport.

entries.old: Apply for ETIAS only at the official travel-europe.europa.eu site once it becomes mandatory — unofficial sites charge inflated fees.
entries.new: The official ETIAS website, travel-europe.europa.eu, gives the fee as EUR 20 when you apply through it; applicants under 18 or over 70 are exempt from paying.

entries.old: You need a national long-stay visa (Type D), applied for via France-Visas before travel — typically around €99 (€50 for Campus France students). Many long-stay visas (VLS-TS) double as residence permits and must be validated online within 3 months of arrival.
entries.new: You need a national long-stay visa (Type D), applied for via France-Visas before travel: €99, or €50 for students whose application went through a Centre pour les études en France. Many long-stay visas (VLS-TS) double as residence permits and must be validated online within 3 months of arrival.

entries.old: EU citizens can enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without a visa; register if staying over 3 months.
entries.new: EU citizens can enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without a visa.
entries.note: No French official page we read requires EU citizens to register after 3 months.

entries.old: A Schengen short-stay visa is required. The EU suspended its visa facilitation agreement with Russia; fees are higher (€90) and processing is slower.
entries.new: A Schengen short-stay visa is required (€90), applied for via France-Visas and the French consular authorities in the country where you live.

entries.old: A Schengen short-stay visa is required, applied for via France-Visas and the visa center (VFS Global) serving your place of residence.
entries.new: A Schengen short-stay visa is required, applied for via France-Visas and the French consular authorities in the country where you live.

entries.old: The EU suspended Vanuatu’s visa waiver over its citizenship-by-investment scheme; a Schengen short-stay visa is required.
entries.new: Vanuatu is listed in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (nationals who need a visa), so a Schengen short-stay visa is required.

Extensions are handled by Immigration Support Services, which grants at most two, of three months each, for a GYD 5,125 processing fee; the advisory's older terms were one month and USD 25 per extension. The Foreign Ministry's advisory offers this route to visa nationals who are unable to apply at a Guyanese mission or consulate, and Immigration Support Services takes the application online before you travel, with a mandatory letter requesting a visa on arrival.

entries.old: Apply to Immigration Support Services before your permitted stay expires, with a letter
entries.new: Processing fee for an extension of stay of three months, payable in cash or by manager's cheque to the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs; GYD 28,700 if the extension granted exceeds three months. Apply to Immigration Support Services with a letter to its Head requesting the extension and evidence of funds for the longer stay. At most two extensions are granted.

entries.old: CARICOM nationals traveling on a national ID card under free-movement arrangements should still carry a passport for onward connections.
entries.new: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on the day you arrive.

entries.old: Not an entry requirement. Malaria is present in the interior of the country, so discuss prophylaxis with a travel clinic if you are going beyond the coast.
entries.new: Not an entry requirement. The UK Foreign Office lists malaria in the interior of the country among the health risks in Guyana.

entries.old: No official source makes insurance a condition of entry.
entries.new: No official source we could read makes insurance a condition of entry. The UK government advises cover for local treatment and medical evacuation: medical facilities are very limited, even in Georgetown, and serious cases may need evacuation.

entries.old: Officers may ask any visitor how they will support themselves.
entries.new: Visitors who get a visa on arrival must show evidence of finances to cover 30 days' expenses, and the name and address of their hotel or sponsor. No sum is published.

entries.old: Crime levels are significant and police capacity is low. Muggings
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says crime levels are significant and police capacity is low. Muggings and attacks, sometimes with knives or firearms, happen in daylight but more often at night and can target tourists who show signs of wealth; reported hotspots in Georgetown include Stabroek Market, Tiger Bay, Albouystown and the Botanical Gardens. Gangs have followed cars from Cheddi Jagan International Airport, so drive with doors locked and use a taxi booked by your hotel or a licensed operator.

entries.old: Carry your yellow fever certificate with your passport: you must show it if you arrive from a country with a risk of yellow fever transmission, and Canada's travel advice notes there is a risk of yellow fever in Guyana itself.
entries.new: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from a country with a risk of yellow fever transmission, and WHO lists Guyana itself among the countries with that risk.

entries.field: FAQ: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Guyana?
entries.old: Canada's travel advice notes that there is a risk of yellow fever in Guyana itself.
entries.new: Only if you are arriving from, or have spent more than 4 hours transiting through the airport of, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — then a certificate is required from age 1. WHO lists Guyana itself among the countries with risk of yellow fever transmission.

entries.field: FAQ: Do I need a visa for Guyana?
entries.old: CARICOM nationals travel freely and are normally admitted for six months.
entries.new: It depends on your passport. CARICOM nationals are granted a definite entry of six months. About 40 other nationalities are visa-exempt on ordinary passports, among them the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Japan, most of western Europe, and several Latin American states — 90 days for some, such as Albania, Brazil and Peru, and 30 days for others, such as South Korea, Singapore and South Africa; for the United States, Canada, Japan and most of western Europe the list states no period, and the UK government says British visitors can normally stay 30 days. Several EU countries, including Germany and Poland, are not on the list. Everyone else needs a visitor's visa arranged before travel through a Guyanese embassy or high commission.

entries.field: FAQ: How does CARICOM free movement work in Guyana?
entries.old: nationals of other CARICOM member states are entitled to an automatic stay of six months on arrival under the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas.
entries.new: Guyana is a founding member of the Caribbean Community, and under a CARICOM Heads of Government decision that Guyana has implemented, nationals of other member states are granted a definite entry of six months. Skilled nationals with a CARICOM Skills Certificate can also live and work in Guyana. Bring proof of nationality. A passport is simplest, and is needed for onward flights.

entries.field: FAQ: How does CARICOM free movement work in Guyana?
entries.old: Bring proof of nationality. A passport is simplest, and is needed for onward flights.
entries.new: Guyana is a founding member of the Caribbean Community, and under a CARICOM Heads of Government decision that Guyana has implemented, nationals of other member states are granted a definite entry of six months. Skilled nationals with a CARICOM Skills Certificate can also live and work in Guyana.

entries.field: FAQ: Can I get a visa on arrival in Guyana?
entries.old: Only as an exception. Travelers from countries with no Guyanese diplomatic representation can be authorized to collect a visa at the port of entry, but this needs written approval from the Ministry of Home Affairs arranged well in advance. Turning up without it risks being refused boarding, so treat the visitor's visa from a Guyanese mission as the normal route.
entries.new: Only as an exception. The Foreign Ministry's advisory says visas will be issued on arrival to visa nationals who are unable to apply at a Guyanese mission or consulate, and Immigration Support Services takes these applications online before travel, with a mandatory letter requesting a visa on arrival.

entries.field: FAQ: Can I extend my stay in Guyana?
entries.old: before the days written in your passport run out, with a letter
entries.new: Yes. Apply to Immigration Support Services (Ministry of Home Affairs) with a letter requesting the extension and evidence of funds for the longer stay. Each extension is for three months and at most two are granted; the processing fee is GYD 5,125 (GYD 28,700 if an extension of more than three months is granted).

entries.field: Summary (CARICOM six-month claim and editorial framing not on an official page)
entries.old: Haiti admits citizens of most countries visa-free for up to 90 days, collecting a USD 10 tourist fee on arrival, and CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months. Paperwork is not the obstacle here: gang violence has put the whole country, including Port-au-Prince, under do-not-travel advisories, and commercial flights are frequently suspended.
entries.new: The Embassy of Haiti in Washington says most tourists need no visa and pay a USD 10 fee on arrival at the airport, while nationals of nine countries need a visa in advance; the UK government says visits of up to 90 days need no visa. The UK and Canada advise against all travel to Haiti, and Canada says there are no regular international flights to or from Port-au-Prince until further notice.

entries.field: FAQ: need a visa (CARICOM six-month and country-group claims not on a page read)
entries.old: Usually not. Haiti admits citizens of most countries — including the EU, UK, US, Canada and the Commonwealth — visa-free for up to 90 days, with a USD 10 tourist fee paid on arrival. CARICOM nationals get six months. Nine nationalities must obtain a visa from a Haitian mission first, applying at least a month before departure: Colombia, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Iran, Libya, Panama, Syria, …
entries.new: Generally not: the Embassy of Haiti in Washington says tourists do not need a visa and pay a USD 10 fee on arrival at the airport, and the UK government says no visa is needed for visits of up to 90 days. Nine nationalities must obtain a visa from a Haitian mission first, applying at least a month before departure: Colombia, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Iran, Libya, Panama, Syria, Vietnam and …

entries.field: FAQ: is it safe (editorial framing and unread US advice removed)
entries.old: No, and that is the central fact about visiting Haiti right now. The US, UK and Canada all advise against all travel because of gang control of Port-au-Prince and much of the country, widespread kidnapping and armed roadblocks. Visa rules are the easy part; getting in, moving around and getting out safely is not.
entries.new: The UK and Canada advise against all travel to Haiti; Canada cites the threat of kidnappings, gang violence and potential civil unrest throughout the country. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs rates Haiti at its highest risk level and advises its citizens not to travel there.

entries.field: FAQ: tourist fee (advice removed; official exemptions and departure tax added)
entries.old: USD 10 per visitor, collected in cash on arrival from travelers entering without a visa. It is separate from any airline taxes and from the departure fee usually built into your ticket. Carry it in US dollar notes.
entries.new: USD 10, paid on arrival at the airport, according to the Embassy of Haiti in Washington; the UK government says it is paid in cash. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says the fee is USD 10 or EUR 10, with children up to 5 and holders of diplomatic or official passports exempt. The UK government also says tourists pay a departure tax of USD 55, included in the ticket price for most internation…

entries.field: FAQ: length of stay (stamp and extension-office claims not on a page read)
entries.old: Up to 90 days for most nationalities, with the officer writing the actual period on your stamp. Extensions are handled by the Direction de l'Immigration et de l'Émigration in Port-au-Prince.
entries.new: The UK government says no visa is needed for visits of up to 90 days. No official source we could read describes how to extend a stay.

entries.old: Barely. The Government of Canada says there are no regular international flights to or from Port-au-Prince until further notice and that Cap-Haïtien's international airport is the best option; Australia's Smartraveller says many airlines have limited or suspended Port-au-Prince flights. Confirm your flight with the airline before you travel.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says there are no regular international flights to or from Port-au-Prince until further notice, that Cap-Haïtien's international airport is the best option for leaving the country, and advises confirming the status of your flight with your airline.

entries.field: FAQ: yellow fever (transit and regional claims not on the cited pages)
entries.old: Only if you arrive from or transit a yellow fever risk country in tropical Africa or South America. Australia's Smartraveller adds that cholera is an ongoing risk in parts of Haiti: drink boiled or bottled water with intact seals.
entries.new: Only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Australia's Smartraveller says cholera is an ongoing risk in parts of Haiti and advises drinking boiled or bottled water with intact seals.

entries.field: Tip: security crisis (unattributed claims and advice)
entries.old: Most governments advise against all travel to Haiti. Gangs control roads around Port-au-Prince — including the route to the airport — and foreigners have been kidnapped for ransom. Anyone traveling for work should have professional security and evacuation arrangements in place before arrival.
entries.new: (removed)

entries.old: The Government of Canada says there are no regular international flights to or from Port-au-Prince until further notice, that flights using the airport are often targeted by gunfire, and that Cap-Haïtien's international airport is the best option. Confirm your flight's status with your airline before you travel.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says there are no regular international flights to or from Port-au-Prince until further notice, that flights using the airport are often targeted by gunfire, and that Cap-Haïtien's international airport is the best option; it advises confirming your flight's status with your airline before going to the airport.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says tourists must pay an entry fee of 10 US dollars in cash on arrival — have it ready in US dollar notes.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says tourists must pay an entry fee of 10 US dollars in cash on arrival.
