entries.new: The Government of Canada says prices are often quoted in 'Haitian dollars' (5 gourdes = 1 Haitian dollar) or in US dollars, although all prices should be in gourdes since March 2018.

entries.old: Register with your embassy before arrival and carry a charged phone with emergency contact numbers. The Government of Canada says mobile coverage may be intermittent in rural areas and roadside assistance is deficient.
entries.new: The Government of Canada advises anyone driving in Haiti to carry a cell phone and a list of emergency contact numbers, because roadside assistance is deficient and mobile coverage may be intermittent in some rural areas.

entries.field: Tourist visa fee notes (claim about other missions not on an official page)
entries.old: Charged by the Embassy of Haiti in Washington for a three-month tourist visa; a six-month multiple-entry visa is USD 200. Pay by money order, certified cheque or cashier's cheque. Other Haitian missions set their own fees.
entries.new: Charged by the Embassy of Haiti in Washington for a three-month tourist visa; a six-month multiple-entry visa is USD 200. Pay by money order, certified cheque or cashier's cheque.

entries.field: Passport validity (advice removed; Embassy of Haiti cited)
entries.old: Carry a passport valid for at least six months on arrival. Given how often Haitian departures are disrupted, leaving extra validity beyond the six months is sensible.
entries.new: Your passport must be valid for at least six months.

entries.field: Yellow fever (regional and transit claims not on the cited page)
entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you are arriving from, or have recently transited, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — mainly parts of tropical Africa and South America. Travelers coming directly from Europe, North America or elsewhere in the Caribbean do not need one to enter Haiti.
entries.new: A yellow fever certificate is required for travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

entries.field: Routine vaccines (now attributed to CDC; "since 2022" not stated)
entries.old: Not an entry condition, but hepatitis A and typhoid vaccination and up-to-date routine vaccines are strongly recommended for Haiti. Cholera has circulated since 2022 and water-borne illness is common; malaria is present year-round in much of the country.
entries.new: Not an entry condition. The US CDC recommends hepatitis A vaccination for unvaccinated travellers aged one or over, typhoid vaccination for most travellers and up-to-date routine vaccines; it says active cholera transmission is widespread in Haiti and recommends malaria prevention medicine for all areas.

entries.field: Travel insurance (insurer-voiding and advice claims not on an official page)
entries.old: No official source states an insurance requirement for entry, but comprehensive coverage including medical evacuation is essential: Canada's travel advice says doctors and hospitals expect immediate cash payment even from insured patients. Read the policy wording carefully. Many insurers void coverage for countries under a government do-not-travel advisory, which now covers all of Haiti.
entries.new: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for Haiti. Canada's travel advice says physicians and hospitals generally expect immediate cash payment even from patients with valid travel health insurance.

entries.field: Onward ticket ("in practice airlines" claim removed; statements attributed)
entries.old: Visitors are expected to hold a confirmed return or onward ticket. In practice airlines check this more consistently than immigration does.
entries.new: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says its citizens entering visa-free must hold a return ticket, and the Embassy of Haiti in Washington asks visa applicants for an airline reservation or round-trip ticket. Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket.

entries.field: Arrival card (aircraft hand-out and "no online form" claims not on the cited page)
entries.old: A paper immigration and customs declaration is handed out on the aircraft and collected at the border. There is no official online pre-arrival form for Haiti. Treat any website charging for one as fraudulent.

entries.field: Currency limits (now attributed; receipt advice removed)
entries.old: Cash above USD 10,000, or the equivalent in gourdes, must be declared to customs on arrival. Given how cash-dependent Haiti is, keep receipts for any large sums you bring in.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs are severe: suspects may be jailed for weeks or months before appearing in court. Pack your own luggage and do not carry items through customs for anyone else.

The US, UK and Canada all advise against all travel to Haiti. Toussaint Louverture airport has been closed to commercial traffic for extended periods since 2024. Do not travel without professional security arrangements.

entries.old: Violent crime is low, but pickpocketing and other street crime happen in crowded areas. Typhoon season runs from May to November. entries.old: Indian nationals must complete the free online Pre-arrival Registration on the Immigration Department website before boarding. It takes minutes, lasts 6 months and allows multiple visits of up to 14 days.

entries.field: FAQ: Do US citizens need a visa (USD conversion and queue claim removed)

entries.field: Summary ("no ETA or pre-registration" rested on silence; stay limit per the Immigration Service)
entries.old: Ireland is not in the Schengen Area and runs its own visa policy: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens have freedom of movement, British citizens enjoy the Common Travel Area, visitors from the US, Canada, Australia, Japan and many other countries get up to 90 days visa-free with no ETA or pre-registration, and visa nationals apply for a short stay 'C' visa (€60 single entry).
entries.new: Ireland runs its own visa policy: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens have freedom of movement, British citizens travel under the Common Travel Area, visitors from the US, Canada, Australia, Japan and many other countries need no visa and are admitted for up to 3 months at the immigration officer's discretion, and visa nationals apply for a short stay 'C' visa (€60 single entry).

entries.field: FAQ: US citizens ("no ETA" and "nothing to apply for" rested on silence)
entries.old: No visa and no ETA. US citizens simply arrive with a passport valid for their stay and can be admitted for up to 90 days. Unlike the UK, Ireland has no electronic travel authorization. There is nothing to apply for before travel when flying directly to Ireland.
entries.new: No. The United States is on the Immigration Service's list of nationalities that do not need a visa for Ireland. On arrival the immigration officer decides how long you may stay, up to a maximum of 3 months, and stamps the date in your passport.

entries.field: FAQ: Schengen visa (Schengen claims not on an official page read; BIVS/SSVWP conditions added)
entries.old: No. Ireland is not in the Schengen Area and runs its own visa system, so a Schengen visa gives no right to enter Ireland. Visa-required nationals need an Irish short stay 'C' visa — though Chinese and Indian citizens with a UK visa endorsed "BIVS", and some nationalities under Ireland's Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme with a valid UK visa, can visit without a separate Irish visa.
entries.new: Not on its own. Ireland's Immigration Service bases the visa requirement on nationality, and visa-required nationals need an Irish short stay 'C' visa. The exceptions it lists are Chinese and Indian nationals living in China or India whose UK visa is endorsed "BIVS", and nationals of the Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme countries who have entered the UK on an eligible UK short-stay visa.

entries.field: FAQ: UK ETA (UK-rule claims not on a page read; Irish SSVWP rule added)
entries.old: Not if you fly directly to Ireland. The UK ETA is a British requirement and Ireland has no equivalent. But if your route transits or enters the UK first (including connecting through London), non-visa-national travelers generally need a UK ETA for that leg, so check UK rules for your itinerary.
entries.new: No official Irish source we could read requires a UK ETA for travel to Ireland. Ireland's Immigration Service says a UK ETA cannot be used under its Short-stay Visa Waiver Programme: a visa-required national who holds a UK ETA rather than a UK visa needs a separate Irish visa.

entries.field: FAQ: South Africa ("reintroduced in June 2022" not on an official page read)
entries.old: Yes. Ireland reintroduced the visa requirement for South African passport holders in June 2022, so the old visa-free access no longer applies. South Africans must obtain a short stay 'C' visa (€60 single entry) through the AVATS online system before traveling.
entries.new: Yes. South Africa is on the Immigration Service's list of nationalities that need a visa for Ireland. South Africans apply for a short stay 'C' visa (€60 single entry) online through AVATS before travelling.

entries.field: FAQ: length of stay ("typically", "generally not extendable" and EU/UK claims not on the cited page)
entries.old: Non-EEA visitors are typically admitted for up to 90 days — the immigration officer stamps the exact permission in your passport at entry. EU/EEA, Swiss and British citizens have no time limit under free movement and the Common Travel Area. Short-stay permissions are generally not extendable for tourism.
entries.new: The immigration officer decides how long you may stay, up to a maximum of 3 months, and stamps the date in your passport; visitors on a short stay 'C' visa must leave before that stamp expires.

entries.field: Tip: not Schengen (no official page read states it)

EU citizens can use the EHIC card for necessary public healthcare.

entries.old: Israel is a modern, orderly country, but the security situation can change quickly: government advisories warn particularly about areas near Gaza and the Lebanese border, and rocket alerts can occur elsewhere. Learn how Home Front Command alerts work, follow local instructions, and check your government's advisory before and during your trip.

entries.field: FAQ: Is Macau covered by a Chinese visa?
entries.old: No — Macao keeps its own immigration system. A mainland Chinese visa is not needed (or valid) for Macao, and Macao's visa-free entry gives no right to cross into Zhuhai or the rest of mainland China, which requires its own visa or exemption.
entries.new: Macao's Public Security Police sets its own entry rules: its own list of visa-exempt nationalities, a visa on arrival, and visas obtained through Chinese diplomatic missions for the nationalities that need one in advance. entries.field: FAQ: Can I do a day trip to Macau from Hong Kong?

entries.field: FAQ: How does the Macau visa on arrival work?

entries.new: Eligible nationalities pay for the visa at the border checkpoint — MOP 200, or MOP 100 for children under 12 — and are granted a stay of up to 30 days; MOP 300 buys multiple entries within that stay. Nationalities excluded from the scheme must apply in advance through a Chinese embassy or consulate.

Most Western governments advise against all travel to Mali.
entries.new: A visa is required. entries.old: Visa-free under a bilateral agreement, generally for up to 90 days. Confirm the current terms with a Malian embassy before travel.
entries.new: Visa-free: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check (diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml) answers that no visa is needed and that you travel with the identity card or passport valid in your country.

No official page names a bilateral agreement or a 90-day stay; the advice to confirm with an embassy is removed. maxStayDays (90) remains in the data and is not confirmed by the check.

entries.old: ECOWAS citizens have continued to enter Mali visa-free under transitional free-movement arrangements despite Mali's January 2025 withdrawal from the bloc — re-confirm shortly before travel as this may change.
entries.new: Visa-free: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check (diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml) answers that no visa is needed and that you travel with the identity card or passport valid in your country, although Mali left ECOWAS in January 2025.
entries.note: 'Transitional free-movement arrangements' and 're-confirm before travel' rest on no official page; the ministry's check (re-run 2026-10-06 for Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire) answers no visa needed.

entries.old: Burkina Faso and Niger form the Alliance of Sahel States confederation with Mali — citizens of the three countries move freely between them.
entries.new: Visa-free: Burkina Faso and Niger are Mali's partners in the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check (diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml) answers that no visa is needed and that you travel with the identity card or passport valid in your country.
entries.note: Ministry visa check re-run 2026-10-06 for Burkina Faso and Niger: no visa needed. 'Move freely between them' is not stated by an official page read.

entries.old: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay in Mali.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay in Mali.

entries.old: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required to enter Mali.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Mali.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are rarely accepted outside a few major hotels and that access to ATMs is limited outside Bamako. Exchange facilities are often slow.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are rarely accepted outside a few major hotels, that access to ATMs is limited outside Bamako, and that exchange facilities are often slow.

entries.old: Mali is run by a military junta and large areas are affected by jihadist insurgency and armed conflict. The UK advises against all travel to the whole of Mali: JNIM blockades on key routes, including around Bamako, target fuel trucks and travellers, overland routes to neighbouring countries are too dangerous, and the kidnapping threat extends to the capital.
entries.new: The UK advises against all travel to the whole of Mali. It says JNIM has implemented blockades on key routes in southern and western Mali, including around Bamako, targeting fuel trucks and enforcing checkpoints for travellers, that leaving by overland routes to neighbouring countries is too dangerous, and that there is a high threat of kidnapping across Mali, including in Bamako. Canada says Mal…
entries.note: 'Military junta' and 'jihadist insurgency' were unattributed; now attributed to Canada and the UK as stated.

entries.old: Mali is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.
entries.new: Mali is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna Convention, according to the UN treaty records.
entries.note: Removed the legal inference about which permit Mali is 'bound to recognize'; no official page states it.

Canada's travel advice says you should carry an International Driving Permit. No official source we could read states for how long a foreign licence may be used.

entries.old: The UK advises against all travel to the whole of Mali, including Bamako — terrorism, blockades on main roads and kidnapping are real risks. Take professional security advice before any trip.
entries.new: The UK advises against all travel to the whole of Mali, including Bamako. It says terrorist attacks can occur at any time, that JNIM blockades target key routes, and that there is a high threat of kidnapping across the country.

entries.old: Mali formally left ECOWAS in January 2025 together with Burkina Faso and Niger. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check still waives the visa for nationals of Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria, Senegal and Togo, but asks those of Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone to apply. West African travelers should re-check shortly before traveling.
entries.new: Mali formally left ECOWAS in January 2025 together with Burkina Faso and Niger. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check still waives the visa for nationals of Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria, Senegal and Togo, but asks those of Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone to apply.

entries.old: Do not photograph military or government installations — the UK Foreign Office and Canada both warn against it — and ask permission before photographing people.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says not to take pictures of military or government installations and to always ask permission before photographing local people; Canada says photographing military personnel and installations is prohibited.

entries.old: Bring enough cash. Canada's travel advice says credit cards are rarely accepted outside a few major hotels and that ATM access is limited outside Bamako.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are rarely accepted outside a few major hotels and that ATM access is limited outside Bamako.
entries.note: Removed 'Bring enough cash' (advice on no official page).

The application and payment are made online through the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular portal, and the entry permit is issued electronically; there is no tourist visa on arrival. Most ECOWAS nationals are still exempt (Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone are not), and citizens of Burkina Faso and Niger move freely under the Alliance of Sahel States.
entries.new: Most nationalities do. The application and payment are made online through the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular portal, and the entry permit is issued electronically. Most ECOWAS nationals are still exempt (Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone are not), and the ministry's visa check also answers that citizens of Burkina Faso and Niger need no visa.

entries.new: No. The UK and Canadian governments both advise against all travel to Mali; Canada cites the threat of terrorism, kidnapping, banditry and fuel shortages.

entries.old: Under the Compact of Free Association, US citizens may enter, live and work in the Marshall Islands with no visa and no time limit. A valid passport and the arrival card are still required.
entries.new: Visa-exempt under the Compact of Free Association, with no restriction on the period of stay, according to the RMI Division of Immigration. It says the Compact exempts US citizens from entry visa requirements only: work registration is still required.
entries.note: Corrected: the Division of Immigration says the Compact exempts US citizens from entry visas only and that work registration is still required; 'arrival card still required' is on no official page read.

entries.old: Citizens of the other freely associated Micronesian states are admitted without a visa and with no limit on their stay. Carry a passport and complete the arrival card as usual.
entries.new: Visa-exempt under the Compact of Free Association, with no restriction on the period of stay, according to the RMI Division of Immigration.
entries.note: Removed 'complete the arrival card as usual' (no official page describes the card).

entries.new: The RMI Division of Immigration requires visitors entering on a visa on arrival or visa waiver, and visitor-visa applicants, to hold a passport valid for at least 6 months from the intended date of departure from the Marshall Islands.
entries.note: Removed 'including for US citizens … the Compact removes the visa, not the passport': the Division of Immigration states the 6-month rule for visa-on-arrival entry and visa applicants only.

entries.old: The Marshall Islands' Office of Commerce, Investment and Tourism says yellow fever (and cholera) immunization is required for travellers arriving from infected areas. Standard routings via Honolulu, Guam or Nadi do not trigger it.
entries.new: The Marshall Islands' Office of Commerce, Investment and Tourism says yellow fever (and cholera) immunization is required for travellers arriving from infected areas.

Proof must be shown on entry or entry may be denied, though entry can be granted on an underta…
entries.new: The Ministry of Health and Human Services' measles travel advisory (Issuance 02, 9 May 2023) makes it mandatory for all incoming travellers that children under 5 have up-to-date MMR or measles-rubella vaccinations, including the early "zero dose" for infants aged 6 to 11 months. Proof must be shown on entry or entry may be denied, though entry can be granted on an undertaking to have the vaccinat…

entries.old: Visitors must show a confirmed onward or return ticket and where they will stay.
entries.new: The RMI Division of Immigration requires a confirmed return or onward ticket out of the Marshall Islands, and a valid visa for the next destination where one is needed. Visitor-visa applicants must also give a confirmed hotel booking or contact details.

entries.old: All visitors must have sufficient funds for their stay. No minimum amount is published; carrying US dollars in cash is the practical answer, since card acceptance is patchy.
entries.new: All visitors must have sufficient funds for their stay, according to the RMI Division of Immigration. No minimum amount is published.
entries.note: Removed 'carrying US dollars in cash is the practical answer, since card acceptance is patchy'.

entries.old: Waived for every nationality on the Division of Immigration's visa-on-arrival list. A USD 20 departure fee is charged when you leave.
entries.new: Waived for every nationality on the Division of Immigration's visa-on-arrival list. Australia's Smartraveller says a departure fee must be paid in US dollars cash when you leave.
entries.note: The USD 20 amount of the departure fee is on no official page read.

entries.old: Australia's Smartraveller says the currency is the US dollar and that many businesses in Majuro and Ebeye take credit cards but others do not; there are only a few ATMs and none at the airport, and the airport departure fee must be paid in US dollars cash.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says ATMs are not available at the airport and that a departure fee must be paid in US dollars cash when you leave.
entries.note: Card acceptance in Majuro and Ebeye and 'only a few ATMs' could not be read on Smartraveller's page.

entries.old: Serious crime against visitors is uncommon and the islands are welcoming, with occasional petty theft and some alcohol-related trouble at night in Majuro and Ebeye. The practical risks dominate: very limited medical care, thin flight connections, no drinkable tap water, strong reef currents, and low-lying atolls exposed to king tides, flooding and drought.
entries.new: The UK government says crime rates are low, but there is a risk of petty crime, including break-ins and non-violent theft, and that medical facilities are very limited. Australia's Smartraveller says assaults also occur, that feral dogs are common and can attack, and that travelling by boat between atolls can be hazardous.
entries.note: Removed unsourced 'islands are welcoming', alcohol-related trouble, flight connections, tap water, reef currents, king tides and drought.

entries.old: Under the Compact of Free Association, US citizens may enter the Marshall Islands and live and work there without a visa or time limit. You still need a valid passport and still complete the arrival card. The arrangement runs the other way too: Marshallese citizens may live and work in the United States.
entries.new: US citizens are visa-exempt under the Compact of Free Association, with no restriction on the period of stay. The RMI Division of Immigration says the Compact exempts them from entry visa requirements only: work registration is still required. Under the Compact, it says, Marshallese citizens may live and work in the United States.
entries.note: Corrected 'live and work without a visa'; removed 'still complete the arrival card'.

entries.old: The UK government says medical facilities are very limited. Bring enough prescription medicine for your stay, and insurance that covers all medical costs including medical evacuation.
entries.new: The UK government says medical facilities are very limited, and advises bringing sufficient prescription medicines and comprehensive travel insurance covering all medical costs, including medical evacuation.

entries.old: International flights are few, so leave buffer time and avoid tight onward international connections.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: Generic advice on no official page.

entries.old: Australia's Smartraveller advises drinking boiled or bottled water, and says there are only a few ATMs, none of them at the airport, and that the departure fee must be paid in US dollars cash.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says ATMs are not available at the airport and that the departure fee must be paid in US dollars cash.
entries.note: Boiled/bottled-water advice and 'only a few ATMs' could not be read on Smartraveller's page.

The Compact of Free Association lets them enter, live and work in the Marshall Islands indefinitely with just a valid passport, and citizens of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia also have no time limit. EU and UK citizens, Taiwan and Guatemala get a free visa waiver for up to 90 days; citizens of countries with diplomatic relations with the Marshall Islands — includ…

EU and UK citizens, Taiwan and Guatemala get a free visa waiver for up to 90 days; citizens of countries with diplomatic relations with the Marshall Islands — including Australia…

entries.old: It is issued at the immigration desk at Amata Kabua International Airport in Majuro, free of charge, to citizens of countries on the Division of Immigration's visa-on-arrival list. You need a passport valid 6 months beyond your departure, a confirmed return or onward ticket, any visa you need for your next destination, and sufficient funds. It allows up to 90 days and cannot be extended.
entries.new: It is granted on arrival, free of charge, to citizens of countries on the Division of Immigration's visa-on-arrival list. You need a passport valid 6 months beyond your departure, a confirmed return or onward ticket, any visa you need for your next destination, and sufficient funds. It allows up to 90 days and cannot be extended.
entries.note: Removed the issuing desk location (not stated).

entries.old: Yes. The Compact of Free Association gives US citizens the right to reside and be employed in the Marshall Islands without an immigration permit, which is why it functions more like freedom of movement than a visa waiver. Employers may still require local registration or professional licensing, so check with them before you start.
entries.new: Not on the Compact alone. The RMI Division of Immigration says the Compact exempts US citizens from entry visa requirements only, and that work registration is still required.
entries.note: Corrected: the answer said 'Yes … without an immigration permit'; the Division of Immigration (immigration-laws-policies, live-work-permits) says work registration is still required.

entries.old: Mauritania scrapped its visa on arrival in January 2025 — nearly all visitors now pre-apply online through the official ANRPTS eVisa portal and pay EUR 55 in cash when they land (EUR 40 for nationals of Arab and African countries), while citizens of eleven neighboring West African and Maghreb states enter visa-free under bilateral agreements.
entries.new: Mauritania ended its visa on arrival on 5 January 2025: nearly all visitors now apply online for an eVisa through the official ANRPTS portal and pay the fee in cash when they land (EUR 55 for 30 days, or EUR 40 for nationals of Arab and African countries), while citizens of eleven West African and Maghreb states enter visa-free under reciprocal agreements.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission; the vaccine is recommended for most travelers to Mauritania in any case.
entries.new: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

entries.old: It is illegal to take Mauritanian ouguiyas out of the country, and the authorities may confiscate them. No official source we could read publishes a threshold for declaring foreign currency. US dollars and euros can be exchanged at banks, some hotels and official bureaux de change.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal to import or export ouguiyas, that any foreign currency must be declared on arrival (there is no limit on the amount), and that you cannot leave with more foreign currency than you declared. No Mauritanian source we could read publishes a declaration threshold.

entries.old: The UK government says Mauritania is mainly a cash-based society: a few hotels in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou accept credit cards (some only Visa), and some ATMs accept foreign cards. US dollars and euros can be exchanged at banks, some hotels and official bureaux de change. Canada and Australia add that you must declare foreign currency on arrival and cannot leave with more than you declared.
entries.new: The UK government says Mauritania is mainly a cash-based society: a few hotels in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou accept credit cards (some only Visa), and some ATMs accept foreign cards. US dollars and euros can be exchanged at banks, some hotels and official bureaux de change. Australia's Smartraveller adds that you must declare foreign currency on arrival and cannot leave with more than you declared.

entries.old: The UK government advises against all travel to areas within 25 km of the Malian border in the south, including Khabou, and to the east of a line through Kankossa, Akhreijit, Ghallaouia, Zouérat and Fdérik; Canada advises against all travel to northern and eastern Mauritania. Check current advice before planning any route.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all travel to areas within 25 km of the Malian border in the south, including Khabou, and to the east of a line through Kankossa, Akhreijit, Ghallaouia, Zouérat and Fdérik; Canada advises against all travel to northern and eastern Mauritania.

entries.old: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — common on overland routes from Senegal or Mali. The vaccine is recommended for most travelers regardless, so carry your yellow card.
entries.new: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

entries.old: The UK government advises against all travel to areas within 25 km of the Malian border and to the east of the country, and Canada advises against all travel to northern and eastern Mauritania, citing extremist groups, armed smugglers and a high risk of kidnapping, with Westerners a preferred target. Check current advisories before planning a trip.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all travel to areas within 25 km of the Malian border and to the east of the country, and Canada advises against all travel to northern and eastern Mauritania; Canada says there is a high risk of kidnapping and that Westerners are a preferred target.

entries.old: Rarely. The UK government says Mauritania is mainly a cash-based society, with only a few hotels in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou accepting credit cards and some ATMs taking foreign cards. Bring US dollars or euros to exchange at banks or official bureaux de change, and declare foreign currency on arrival.
entries.new: Rarely. The UK government says Mauritania is mainly a cash-based society, with only a few hotels in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou accepting credit cards and some ATMs taking foreign cards, and that US dollars and euros can be exchanged at banks or official bureaux de change. Australia's Smartraveller says foreign currency must be declared on arrival.

entries.old: Mauritania severed relations with Israel in 2010 and Israeli passports are not accepted for entry.
entries.new: No official source we could read states the entry rules for Israeli passport holders.
entries.note: No official page we could read says Israeli passports are refused; the requirement itself is left for a row-level pass.

entries.old: Mauritius only requires your passport to be valid for the whole of your intended stay, but some airlines apply a stricter six-month rule at check-in — more validity is safer.
entries.new: Mauritius's Passport and Immigration Office requires a passport or other recognized travel document valid beyond the intended period of stay.
entries.note: "Some airlines apply a stricter six-month rule at check-in — more validity is safer" rests on no official page.

entries.old: You must hold a confirmed return or onward ticket — arriving without one can mean refused boarding or refused entry.
entries.new: Mauritius's Passport and Immigration Office requires every visitor to hold a valid return ticket to their country of origin or residence.
entries.note: The office requires a return passage ticket to the country of origin or residence; "refused boarding or refused entry" is not stated.

entries.old: All passengers must complete the All-in-One Travel Form and the Health Declaration Form before boarding any aircraft or vessel bound for Mauritius, under the Quarantine (Health Declaration Form) Regulations 2026. The forms are free.
entries.new: All passengers must complete the All-in-One Travel Form and the Health Declaration Form before boarding any aircraft or vessel bound for Mauritius, under the Quarantine (Health Declaration Form) Regulations 2026.
entries.note: "The forms are free" is not stated on the notice.

entries.old: Remote workers, retirees and long-stay visitors can apply free of charge for the Premium Travel Visa, which allows stays of up to a year (renewable) while living on income earned outside Mauritius. Apply online before travel.
entries.new: The Premium Visa, free of charge, lets foreign nationals stay in Mauritius for one year, renewable, as tourists, retirees or professionals working remotely from Mauritius, with their families. The Passport and Immigration Office links to an online application.
entries.note: Reworded to what the Passport and Immigration Office page says; "living on income earned outside Mauritius" is not on it.

entries.old: Immigration asks where you are staying. Have your accommodation booking or host's details ready at the desk, along with your return ticket.
entries.new: The Passport and Immigration Office requires every visitor to have a confirmed hotel booking or sponsorship for accommodation, adequate funds for the stay and a valid return ticket.
entries.note: "Immigration asks where you are staying… have details ready at the desk" is not on an official page; replaced by the office's stated entry conditions.

entries.old: EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Mauritius visa waiver agreement. British, Canadian, Chinese and Russian citizens are admitted for up to 60 days, as are most visa-on-arrival nationalities (two weeks for a few). For other visa-free nationalities no maximum is published: the immigration officer sets the length of each stay on arrival. Tourist stays can be extended by the Passport and Immigration Office in Port Louis, with proof of funds and accommodation.
entries.new: EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Mauritius visa waiver agreement. British, Canadian, Chinese and Russian citizens are admitted for up to 60 days, as are most visa-on-arrival nationalities (two weeks for a few). For other visa-free nationalities the Passport and Immigration Office's country list gives no maximum. Tourist stays can be extended by the Passport and Immigration Office in Port Louis, with bank statements and a confirmed accommodation booking.
entries.note: "The immigration officer sets the length of each stay on arrival" is not stated on an official page.

entries.old: A free long-stay visa aimed at remote workers, retirees and families who want to live in Mauritius for up to a year (renewable) while earning their income abroad. You apply online with proof of income, accommodation and insurance. It cannot be used to take up work in Mauritius itself.
entries.new: A free visa for foreign nationals who want a long stay in Mauritius as a tourist, a retiree or a professional working remotely, with their family. It allows a stay of one year, renewable. The Passport and Immigration Office links to an online application.
entries.note: Proof of income and insurance, and "cannot be used to take up work in Mauritius", are not on the official page.

entries.old: A passport valid beyond your stay, a confirmed return or onward ticket, a confirmed hotel booking or sponsorship for accommodation, and adequate funds for the stay (no daily amount is published). Entry is normally granted for the length of your booking, up to your nationality's maximum.
entries.new: A passport valid beyond your stay, a valid return ticket to your country of origin or residence, a confirmed hotel booking or sponsorship for accommodation, and adequate funds for the stay (no daily amount is published).
entries.note: "Entry is normally granted for the length of your booking" is not stated on an official page.

entries.old: Most crime is non-violent, such as burglaries from tourist villas and theft of unattended bags, but petty crime is common in tourist areas such as Port Louis, Grand Baie and Flic en Flac, and there have been some reports of sexual assaults on tourists. Avoid walking alone at night on beaches or in poorly lit areas.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says most crime is non-violent, such as burglaries from tourist villas and theft of unattended bags, that petty crime is common in tourist areas such as Port Louis, Grand Baie and Flic en Flac, and that there have been some reports of sexual assaults on tourists. It advises not walking alone at night on beaches or in poorly lit areas.
entries.note: The UK Foreign Office text is now attributed by name.

entries.old: Visa-free entry with proof of accommodation, sufficient funds and a return ticket. The immigration officer sets the length of stay on arrival.
entries.new: No visa required, per the Passport and Immigration Office's country list, which gives no maximum stay. Every visitor must have a confirmed accommodation booking or sponsorship, adequate funds and a return ticket.
entries.note: "The immigration officer sets the length of stay on arrival" is not stated on an official page.

entries.old: Mauritius does not recognize Kosovo passports for visa-free or on-arrival entry — arrange a visa through the Passport and Immigration Office before travel.
entries.new: No official source we could read states the rule for Kosovo passports: the Passport and Immigration Office's country list does not name Kosovo, and its list of unrecognized passports does not include it.

entries.old: Mexico requires your passport to be valid for the entire duration of your stay; there is no formal 6-month rule, but airlines sometimes apply one — extra validity is safer.
entries.new: INM requires a passport or identity and travel document that is valid (vigente) at the immigration check; it states no minimum validity period.

entries.old: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but private healthcare — the standard for visitors — must be paid for, so medical coverage is strongly recommended.
entries.new: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for Mexico.

entries.old: Not a formal entry requirement, but immigration officers and airlines may ask for proof of return or onward travel and where you will stay.
entries.new: INM says the immigration authority may ask you to prove the purpose of your trip, for example with a hotel reservation, return tickets or tour tickets, and to state the means of transport you will use to leave the country.

entries.old: No fixed amount is set, but officers may ask about your funds, accommodation and purpose of visit when deciding how many days to grant.
entries.new: No fixed amount is set. INM says the immigration authority may ask about your means of subsistence during your stay (except holders of a Mexican visa), your address and how long you will stay.

entries.old: At international airports you no longer fill in an FMM: the immigration officer stamps your passport with your expected departure date, and you can download the digital FMM (FMMd) afterwards. Note the date in the stamp — that, not 180 days, is your permitted stay. If you enter by land, you must present a completed FMM at the immigration filter.
entries.new: At international airports you no longer fill in an FMM: it is generated at entry, your entry stamp carries the information, and you can download the digital FMM (FMMd) afterwards. If you enter by land, you must present a completed FMM at the immigration check.

entries.old: Safety varies sharply by state. The UK government advises against all but essential travel to all or parts of several states, including Zacatecas, Michoacán, Sinaloa, Tamaulipas, Chihuahua and parts of Baja California and Guanajuato, because of organised-crime violence. Risks are lower in tourist areas, though sexual offences have been reported there too. Check the advice for every state on your r
entries.new: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to all or parts of several states, including Zacatecas, Michoacán, Sinaloa, Tamaulipas, Chihuahua and parts of Baja California and Guanajuato, because of organised-crime violence. It says sexual offences have been reported in tourist areas and advises taking care even close to hotels, especially after dark.

entries.old: Mexico is not one uniform risk level. Several states are under advice against all but essential travel, while risks are lower in the main tourist areas. Check advice for each state on your itinerary, not just the country page.
entries.new: The UK government gives its Mexico advice state by state and advises against all but essential travel to all or parts of several states.

entries.old: Entry to Mexico is free for visa-free tourists. Air arrivals no longer fill in an FMM, and third-party websites selling "Mexico tourist cards" or "entry registrations" are unnecessary.
entries.new: INM says travellers arriving at international airports do not have to present, fill in or carry an FMM: it is generated at entry.
entries.note: 'Entry to Mexico is free' is not stated; INM publishes entry-duty tariffs (derechos migratorios por internación).

entries.old: 180 days is the legal maximum, not a guarantee. Check the number of days the officer writes in your stamp before leaving the desk, and ask for more if your trip needs it.
entries.new: INM says a visitor's stay cannot exceed 180 days; your entry stamp carries the information on your entry.

entries.old: No. US citizens can visit Mexico visa-free for tourism or business for up to 180 days. The immigration officer decides the exact number of days and records it in your passport stamp. It is no longer an automatic 180.
entries.new: No. US citizens can visit Mexico visa-free for tourism or business for up to 180 days. The immigration officer decides the stay granted, and your entry stamp carries the information.

entries.old: Up to 180 days if the immigration officer grants it — officers now often stamp shorter periods matched to your ticket and plans. The days granted appear in your entry stamp; overstaying leads to fines on exit.
entries.new: Up to 180 days, which INM says a visitor's stay cannot exceed. The immigration officer decides the stay granted, and your entry stamp carries the information.

entries.old: Visa-free for tourism and business. The immigration officer sets the length of stay, up to a maximum of 180 days. It is no longer automatic, so state your plans clearly.
entries.new: Visa-free for tourism and business. The immigration officer sets the length of stay, up to a maximum of 180 days.

entries.old: Ukrainian citizens arriving BY AIR can use the free Electronic Authorization (SAE) instead of a consular visa; land/sea arrivals need a visitor visa. Anyone holding a valid US, Canadian, UK, Japanese or Schengen visa is exempt from both. Rules for Ukrainians have shifted in recent years. Confirm with the nearest Mexican consulate before booking.
entries.new: Ukrainian citizens arriving BY AIR can use the free Electronic Authorization (SAE) instead of a consular visa; land/sea arrivals need a visitor visa. Anyone holding a valid US, Canadian, UK, Japanese or Schengen visa is exempt from both.

entries.old: Mexico reimposed a consular visa requirement for Ecuadorian citizens in 2021; holders of a valid US, Canadian, UK, Japanese or Schengen visa remain exempt.
entries.new: Mexico requires a consular visa for Ecuadorian citizens; holders of a valid US, Canadian, UK, Japanese or Schengen visa remain exempt.

entries.old: Mexico reintroduced a consular visa requirement for Peruvian citizens in 2024; holders of a valid US, Canadian, UK, Japanese or Schengen visa remain exempt.
entries.new: Mexico requires a consular visa for Peruvian citizens; holders of a valid US, Canadian, UK, Japanese or Schengen visa remain exempt.

entries.old: Mexico reimposed a consular visa requirement for Venezuelan citizens in 2022; holders of a valid US, Canadian, UK, Japanese or Schengen visa remain exempt.
entries.new: Mexico requires a consular visa for Venezuelan citizens; holders of a valid US, Canadian, UK, Japanese or Schengen visa remain exempt.

entries.old: Micronesia needs no visa or permit for visits of 30 days or less from citizens of essentially every country; longer stays need an entry permit. US citizens go further still: under the Compact of Free Association they may enter, live and work in the FSM without a visa.
entries.new: The Federated States of Micronesia requires no permit for visits of 30 days or less; visitors complete a Customs, Immigration & Quarantine form on arrival and need a passport valid at least 120 days beyond entry and a way to travel onward. Longer stays need an entry permit. US citizens may enter with a US passport or a birth certificate and may be issued an entry permit for the whole visit, up to one year.

entries.old: Visitors entering on the 30-day permit must hold a confirmed onward or return ticket; airlines check this at check-in and immigration officers may ask to see it.
entries.new: Every visitor must be able to show they can travel onward and leave the FSM at the end of the visit, normally with a return or onward ticket; the Chief of Immigration & Labor may accept other proof instead.

entries.old: No FSM official source we could read states a funds requirement or amount. Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask you to show proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay.
entries.new: No FSM official source we could read states a funds requirement or amount. Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask you to show proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay.

entries.old: The US Department of State says amounts equivalent to US$10,000 or more must be declared on entry to the FSM. It lists no restriction on exit.
entries.new: No official source we could read states a currency declaration threshold for the FSM.
entries.note: The US State Department page is blocked to us and its archived copies are a 404 or a block page; the USD 10,000 figure is withdrawn under the global rule.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says most hotels accept credit cards and ATM facilities are limited; Canada says most hotels and tourist facilities accept major credit cards and that there are few ATMs.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says the currency is the US dollar, that most hotels accept credit cards and that ATM facilities are limited; Canada says most hotels and tourist facilities accept major credit cards and that there are few ATMs.

entries.old: Serious crime against visitors is rare and island communities are welcoming. The practical risks are alcohol-related trouble after dark, occasional theft from unlocked rooms, weak road lighting, and how far you are from advanced medical care.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says crime levels are low, that the risk of crime is higher at night, particularly if alcohol is involved, and that it is also higher in the state of Chuuk.

entries.old: Bring enough US dollars in cash: the UK FCDO says ATM facilities are limited, and Canada says there are few ATMs.
entries.new: The currency is the US dollar. The UK FCDO says ATM facilities are limited, and Canada says there are few ATMs.

entries.old: Almost certainly not. Citizens of essentially every country need neither a visa nor a permit for visits of 30 days or less, provided they hold a passport valid at least 120 days beyond the date of entry and a return or onward ticket; stays over 30 days need an entry permit. US citizens need no visa under the Compact of Free Association, and their entry permit can cover the whole visit, up to one y
entries.new: Not for visits of 30 days or less: the FSM requires no permit for them, provided you hold a passport valid at least 120 days beyond the date of entry and can show a return or onward ticket, and complete the CIQ form on arrival. Stays over 30 days need an entry permit. US citizens may be issued an entry permit for the whole visit, up to one year.

entries.old: Under the Compact, US citizens may enter the Federated States of Micronesia without a visa, and FSM citizens have the same right in the United States. A US passport or a birth certificate proves citizenship, and the entry permit covers the length of the visit, up to one year. You still pass through immigration, and local rules on employment and land ownership apply.
entries.new: The FSM's visitor regulations say US citizens may enter any FSM state with a US passport or proof of US citizenship (a birth certificate), and may be issued an entry permit for the duration of the visit, up to one year. Each island airport has its own customs and immigration officers.

entries.old: Yes. Visitors staying longer than 30 days need an entry permit from the FSM Division of Immigration, which may be issued for an additional period of up to 60 days. Apply before your first 30 days end.
entries.new: Yes. Visitors staying longer than 30 days need an entry permit, which may be issued for an additional period of up to 60 days.

entries.old: None is required for entry: the FSM is not on WHO's list of countries that ask for a yellow fever certificate, and no FSM authority publishes a vaccination rule. Routine vaccinations should be up to date; dengue outbreaks occur, so mosquito precautions matter more than paperwork.
entries.new: The FSM's visitor regulations say vaccination or certification is not required unless the traveller comes from an infected area.
entries.note: 'no FSM authority publishes a vaccination rule' was wrong: the FSM regulations page says vaccination is not required unless the traveller comes from an infected area.

entries.old: Marshallese citizens need no visa under the reciprocal arrangements between the Compact states. A passport, a birth certificate or an FSM entry permit proves citizenship, and the entry permit may be issued for the length of the visit, up to one year.
entries.new: Citizens of the Marshall Islands may prove citizenship with a passport, a birth certificate or an FSM entry permit, and may be issued an entry permit for the length of the visit, up to one year.
entries.note: 'need no visa under the Compact / reciprocal arrangements' is not stated on the FSM page; requirement left as is.

entries.old: Palauan citizens need no visa under the reciprocal arrangements between the Compact states. A passport, a birth certificate or an FSM entry permit proves citizenship, and the entry permit may be issued for the length of the visit, up to one year.

entries.old: Under the Compact of Free Association, US citizens need no visa. A US passport or a birth certificate proves citizenship, and the entry permit may be issued for the length of the visit, up to one year.
entries.new: US citizens may enter any FSM state with a US passport or proof of US citizenship (birth certificate), and may be issued an entry permit for the length of the visit, up to one year.

entries.old: Monaco has no border controls of its own — entry follows Schengen rules applied through France, so EU/EEA citizens enter freely, visa-exempt nationalities get 90 days within the shared Schengen allowance, and visa-required travelers need a French-issued Schengen visa, which is valid for Monaco.
entries.new: Monaco's government says visitors need the passport, and any visa, required to enter France: EEA citizens need only a valid passport or identity card, visa-exempt nationalities can stay under 90 days, and others need a Schengen visa from the embassy of the Schengen country through which they enter Europe. The UK says France handles immigration matters for Monaco and that days there count within the Schengen 90-day limit.
entries.note: Global rule: a sentence no official page states is not shown.

entries.old: A Schengen short-stay visa issued by France is required — Monaco has no border controls with France and issues no short-stay visas of its own; apply through France-Visas.
entries.new: A Schengen short-stay visa is required. Monaco's government says non-EEA nationals need a Schengen visa to travel to Monaco, applied for at the embassy of the Schengen country through which they will enter Europe; once it is obtained, Monaco can be visited without any other formality.
entries.note: Corrected: Monaco's government says to apply at the embassy of the Schengen country of entry, not necessarily France; 'no border controls' is on no official page read.

entries.old: 90 days visa-free under the Schengen rules applied through France — time in Monaco counts within your 90 days in any 180 in the Schengen Area. ETIAS authorization will be required once mandatory.

The confirmation (PDF with QR code) is shown to port health officers on arrival.

The FCDO advises against all travel to Borno, Yobe, Adamawa, Gombe, Katsina and Zamfara states and to the riverine areas of the Niger Delta, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the north, the Middle Belt and parts of the south-east, because of terrorism, banditry and kidnapping. entries.old: Nigeria is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Nigeria yet.
entries.new: Nigeria is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic. The UK Foreign Office says UK drivers need a 1968 International Driving Permit and a Nigerian licence for stays of more than a year; the Government of Canada says Canadian drivers need their licence and an International Driving Permit, and a Nigerian permit after 3 months.

entries.old: Norway is in the Schengen Area through its association agreement with the EU: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities including the US and UK get 90 days in any 180-day period counted across the whole Schengen Area, and everyone else needs a Schengen visa Svalbard, though Norwegian, is outside the Schengen Area.

Canada's travel advice says Svalbard, though Norwegian territory, is not part of the Schengen Area.

entries.old: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. Fee set EU-wide since June 11, 2024; paid in local currency where you apply.
entries.new: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. Fee set EU-wide since June 11, 2024.

entries.old: Stays over 90 days (work, study, family) are handled as residence-permit applications through UDI; fees vary by purpose. Confirm the current fee on udi.no before applying.
entries.new: Stays over 90 days (work, study, family) are handled as residence-permit applications; the Immigration Regulations (§ 17-10) set the fee by purpose.

entries.old: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it, but medical care is expensive — cover is strongly recommended.
entries.new: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. No official source we could read states an insurance requirement for visa-exempt visitors.

entries.old: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.
entries.new: Non-EU travellers are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders: on the first crossing since the EES started, border officers take a facial photo and/or scan fingerprints. The EU says this can be quicker if you register some of your data in advance, at a self-service system or through a mobile app where one is available.

entries.old: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

entries.old: Norway is one of the safest countries in the world, with very low crime. The main risks are outdoors: fast-changing mountain and sea weather, and winter road conditions.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says there is a small risk of petty theft, particularly at airports and railway stations in and around Oslo, and that terrorist attacks in Norway cannot be ruled out. Canada's travel advice says weather conditions can change rapidly, even in summer, and that there is a risk of avalanches in winter.

entries.old: Norway is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. entries.old: Under Norway's Alcohol Act, drinks over 4.7% alcohol are sold in shops only by the state-owned Vinmonopolet, which may not sell on Sundays and public holidays. Other shops may sell beer up to 4.7% no later than 20:00 on weekdays and 18:00 on the day before a Sunday or public holiday.
entries.new: Under Norway's Alcohol Act, drinks over 4.7% alcohol are sold in shops only by the state-owned Vinmonopolet, whose shops may sell from 08:30 to 18:00 (10:00 to 16:00 on the day before a Sunday or public holiday). Other shops may sell drinks of up to 4.7% from 08:00 to 18:00, and until 15:00 on the day before a Sunday or public holiday, unless the municipality sets other hours.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says Svalbard is Norwegian territory but not part of the Schengen area. You need a valid passport to enter it, and you must meet Schengen entry rules when you return to mainland Norway — so if you need a Schengen visa, it has to allow that re-entry.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says Svalbard is Norwegian territory but not part of the Schengen area. You need a valid passport to enter it, and you must meet Schengen entry rules when you return to mainland Norway.

entries.old: Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, visa-exempt travelers will need the authorization (€20, valid 3 years) for Norway as for the rest of the Schengen Area. Check the official travel-europe.europa.eu site for the current status.

entries.field: FAQ: How long can I stay in Peru as a tourist?

entries.old: The UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned in Singapore: bringing them in is illegal even for personal use, and they are confiscated, with a possible fine. Leave them at home.
entries.new: The UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned in Singapore: bringing them in is illegal even for personal use, and they are confiscated, with a possible fine.

entries.old: Australia's Smartraveller says Singapore has strict laws and penalties for acts that are legal or minor offences elsewhere, including smoking in public, spitting, importing or chewing gum, littering and jaywalking, and that drug trafficking can carry the mandatory death sentence. Follow the rules and the city is easy to visit.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says Singapore has strict laws and penalties for acts that are legal or minor offences elsewhere, including smoking in public, spitting, importing or chewing gum, littering and jaywalking, and that drug trafficking can carry the mandatory death sentence.

entries.field: FAQ: Schengen (accession year and "no border checks" not on a page read)
entries.old: Yes, since 2007. There are no border checks when arriving from other Schengen countries, and your 90/180-day visa-free allowance is counted across the entire area, not per country.
entries.new: Yes. The UK government says Slovakia follows Schengen area rules, and the 90/180-day visa-free allowance is counted across the entire area, not per country.

entries.field: FAQ: ETIAS ("expected to cost a small fee" hedge replaced by the EU figures; advice removed)
entries.old: Once the EU's ETIAS system becomes mandatory, visa-waiver travelers will need to obtain the online authorization before their trip. It is expected to cost a small fee, be valid for three years, and cover the whole Schengen Area. Check the official EU site for the launch date.

entries.field: Tip: vignette ("only official channel" and points-of-sale claims not on the cited page)
entries.old: Driving on Slovak motorways requires a vignette. The toll operator's site eznamka.sk is the only official sales channel online, and its points of sale are mostly at selected petrol stations and at border crossings. The UK government says you could get a heavy fine without one.
entries.new: Using marked sections of Slovak motorways and expressways requires an electronic vignette, sold at eznamka.sk. The UK government says you could get a heavy fine without one.

entries.field: Tip: Tatras rescue (insurance advice now attributed)
entries.old: The UK government says that if you need the Slovak Mountain Rescue Service (HZS) you will have to meet costs of up to €1,000, and that ignoring HZS rules or instructions can bring a fine of up to €3,320. Make sure your insurance covers mountain rescue.
entries.new: The UK government says that if you need the Slovak Mountain Rescue Service (HZS) you will have to meet costs of up to €1,000, advises making sure your insurance includes rescue costs, and says ignoring HZS rules or instructions can bring a fine of up to €3,320.

entries.new: Schengen visa applicants must show travel medical insurance with at least €30,000 of cover valid across the Schengen Area.
