entries.new: Visa-free for up to 14 days on an ordinary passport, effective until 31 July 2027. You must show a hotel booking, your host's or sponsor's contact details and sufficient travel funds.
entries.note: 'Trial program repeatedly extended' and 'confirm before travel' are not on BOCA's page, which gives the 31 July 2027 end date.

entries.old: Mainland Chinese citizens need entry permits issued by both sides rather than a visa; individual tourist travel has been suspended since 2019, and only limited categories such as business, family visits and approved group programs are processed.
entries.new: No official source we could read states the entry rules for mainland Chinese citizens.

entries.old: Hong Kong and Macao permanent residents apply online for an entry permit rather than a visa; those not eligible online apply through the National Immigration Agency.
entries.new: Hong Kong and Macao residents can apply online to the National Immigration Agency for an entry permit rather than a visa.

entries.old: Travelers who hold a valid (or recently expired) visa or residence permit from designated countries can use the free online travel authorization for a 14-day stay; otherwise a visitor visa is required.
entries.new: Citizens of India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam can apply online to the National Immigration Agency for a Travel Authorization Certificate; otherwise a visitor visa is required. No official page we could read states the certificate's conditions, fee or stay.
entries.note: Conditions (valid or recently expired visa from designated countries), 'free' and '14-day stay' are not on the NIA or BOCA pages read.

entries.old: Free — for nationals of India, Vietnam, Indonesia, Laos and Myanmar who hold a valid (or recently expired) visa or residence permit from designated countries such as the US, UK, Schengen states, Japan, Korea, Australia or New Zealand.
entries.new: No official page we could read states the fee or the eligibility conditions. BOCA says citizens of India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam can apply online.

entries.old: Single-entry visitor visa applied for overseas (USD 100 for multiple entry). Nationals of countries that charge Taiwanese passport holders a special handling fee pay the equivalent extra. Applications go through the nearest Taipei Economic and Cultural Office.
entries.new: Single-entry visitor visa applied for overseas (USD 100 for multiple entry); rush handling adds 50%. Nationals of countries that charge Taiwanese passport holders a special handling fee pay the equivalent extra.

entries.old: Taiwan waives visas for around 60 nationalities — 90 days for the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand among others — with free online travel authorisations or eVisas for several more. Remaining nationalities apply for a visitor visa at a Taipei representative office, and mainland Chinese travelers need special entry permits.
entries.new: Taiwan waives visas for 65 nationalities — 90 days for the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand among others — and 20 more can apply online for an eVisa. Remaining nationalities apply for a visitor visa at a Taiwan overseas mission.
entries.note: 'around 60' -> BOCA list count; removed the unsourced mainland-permit clause and 'free travel authorisations'.

entries.old: Passports must generally be valid for at least 6 months on arrival. US and Japanese passport holders are exempt from the 6-month rule and need validity only for the length of their intended stay.
entries.new: Visa-exempt entry requires a passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry. US and Japanese nationals need a passport valid only for the intended stay.

entries.old: Visa-free entry requires a confirmed onward or return ticket — airlines check before boarding and immigration officers may ask to see it.
entries.new: Visa-free entry requires a confirmed return ticket, or an onward ticket and a visa for the next destination, and a confirmed seat reservation for the departure flight.
entries.note: 'Airlines check before boarding and officers may ask' is not stated.

entries.old: No fixed amount is published; immigration officers occasionally ask about means of support for the stay. Visa-exempt visitors from Thailand, the Philippines and Brunei must show a hotel booking, their host's contact details and sufficient travel funds.
entries.new: No fixed amount is published. Visa-exempt visitors from Thailand, the Philippines and Brunei must show a hotel booking, their host's contact details and sufficient travel funds.

entries.old: Cash over USD 10,000 (or over TWD 100,000 in local currency) must be declared on arrival. Confirm current thresholds with Taiwan Customs before carrying large sums.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says you must declare cash or travellers cheques worth more than NT$100,000 or US$10,000 on arrival.

entries.old: Taiwan is one of Asia's safest destinations, with very low crime. The main considerations are natural: typhoons, which the Government of Canada and the UK FCDO say usually occur between May and November, and occasional earthquakes.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says crime rates are extremely low in Taiwan, and the Government of Canada says violent crime is rare but petty crime such as pickpocketing occurs. Both say typhoons usually occur between May and November, and the UK says earthquakes are a risk.
entries.note: 'one of Asia's safest destinations' is not on any official page.

entries.old: Visa-free travelers must hold a confirmed onward or return ticket — airlines routinely refuse boarding without one.
entries.new: Visa-free travelers must hold a confirmed return ticket, or an onward ticket and a visa for the next destination.

entries.old: The Government of Canada and the UK FCDO say typhoons usually occur between May and November, with a risk of road blockages and landslides afterwards. Build slack into itineraries and monitor Central Weather Administration warnings.
entries.new: The Government of Canada and the UK FCDO say typhoons usually occur between May and November, with a risk of road blockages and landslides afterwards. The UK FCDO advises monitoring Central Weather Administration warnings and keeping your itinerary flexible.

entries.old: Around 60 nationalities do not: the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and others get 90 days visa-free; Singapore, Malaysia, the Dominican Republic, Belize, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines get 30 days; and Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei and Oman get 14 days. About 20 nationalities, including the Gulf states, can apply online …
entries.new: 65 nationalities do not: the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and others get 90 days visa-free; Singapore, Malaysia, the Dominican Republic, Belize, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines get 30 days; and Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei and Oman get 14 days. 20 nationalities, including the Gulf states, can apply online for an eVisa,…

entries.old: US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days with a confirmed onward or return ticket. The visa-exempt stay cannot normally be extended — leaving and re-entering resets the clock.
entries.new: US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days with a confirmed return or onward ticket. The stay starts the day after arrival and cannot be extended.
entries.note: 'leaving and re-entering resets the clock' is not stated by BOCA.

entries.old: Not as ordinary tourists at present. Mainland residents need entry permits issued by both sides, individual tourist travel has been suspended since 2019, and only limited categories such as business, family visits and approved group programs are processed.
entries.new: No official source we could read states the entry rules for mainland Chinese citizens.

entries.old: Not a visa — eligible Hong Kong and Macao permanent residents apply online for an entry permit through Taiwan's National Immigration Agency, which allows a stay of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Not a visa — Hong Kong and Macao residents can apply online to Taiwan's National Immigration Agency for an entry permit.

entries.old: Yes. A confirmed onward or return ticket is a condition of visa-free entry, and airlines check it at check-in. One-way travelers should obtain a visitor visa instead.
entries.new: Yes. BOCA lists a confirmed return ticket, or an onward ticket and a visa for the next destination, among the conditions of visa-free entry.

entries.old: No official source we read describes card acceptance in Taiwan. The UK FCDO says most ATMs in 7-Eleven stores accept international cards; other ATMs may not.
entries.new: No official source we read describes card acceptance or ATMs in Taiwan.
entries.note: The 7-Eleven ATM statement is no longer on any part of the UK FCDO's Taiwan advice.

entries.old: Tajikistan waives visas for about 80 nationalities — including the EU, US, Canada, Australia and Japan — for stays of up to 30 days, and most CIS citizens enter with no time limit. About 130 nationalities, including the UK, can apply online for an eVisa (with an optional GBAO permit for the Pamir Highway); the rest apply at a Tajik embassy.
entries.new: Since January 2022 Tajikistan has waived visas for citizens of 52 countries, including the EU, US, Canada, Australia and Japan, for stays of up to 30 days, and citizens of Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Ukraine and Georgia enter with no time limit set. About 130 nationalities, including the UK, can apply online for an eVisa (with an optional GBAO permit for the Pamir Highway); the rest apply at a Tajik embassy.

entries.old: Insurance is not among the documents Tajikistan requires for a visa, and no official source states an insurance check at the border. Medical facilities are basic outside Dushanbe, so comprehensive cover including medical evacuation is strongly recommended, especially for the Pamirs.
entries.new: Insurance is not among the documents Tajikistan requires for a visa, and no official source states an insurance check at the border.

entries.old: A return or onward ticket is not among the documents Tajikistan requires for a visa, and no official source states a ticket check at the border. Airlines may still ask for proof of onward travel before boarding.
entries.new: A return or onward ticket is not among the documents Tajikistan requires for a visa, and no official source states a ticket check at the border.

entries.old: Cash above USD 10,000 (or the equivalent) must be declared on arrival, with documents showing where the money came from. Up to USD 3,000 can be taken out without a declaration. Keep your entry declaration until you leave.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says cash above USD 10,000 (or the equivalent) must be declared on entry, with documents showing where the money came from, that up to USD 3,000 can be taken out without a declaration, and that you should keep your entry declaration until you leave.

entries.old: Travelers are generally welcomed, but pickpocketing is common in crowded places in Dushanbe, and terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks. The considerations are practical: rough roads, high altitude on the Pamir Highway, and border areas with Afghanistan and Kyrgyzstan that can be restricted or close at short notice.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says pickpocketing is common in crowded places such as markets and public transport, that terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Tajikistan, and that the land border with Afghanistan has been closed since 2021.

entries.old: Tajikistan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by nati
entries.new: Tajikistan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. No official source we could read states whether a permit is required in addition to a national licence, or for how long a foreign licence may be used.

entries.old: The Pamir Highway runs through the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO), which needs its own permit on top of your visa or visa waiver — eVisa applicants can simply tick the GBAO box on evisa.tj; visa-free travelers should arrange it through OVIR in Dushanbe or a local tour operator.
entries.new: The Pamir Highway runs through the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO), which needs its own permit on top of your visa or visa waiver. eVisa applicants select it in the same application on evisa.tj; the UK Foreign Office says others can get it from a Tajik embassy before travelling or, in Tajikistan, from the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
entries.note: The UK says the permit comes from the Consular Department of the MFA in Dushanbe (or a Tajik embassy before travel), not from OVIR.

entries.old: Check access shortly before travelling. The UK says you need a permit, in addition to your visa, to travel within 20 km of the Afghan border in the Khatlon region, that border areas may be subject to sudden restrictions, and that Border Guard patrols may ask for your passport and GBAO permit in GBAO.
entries.new: The UK says you need a permit, in addition to your visa, to travel within 20 km of the Afghan border in the Khatlon region, applied for at the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dushanbe, and that the government sometimes stops issuing GBAO permits to tourists at short notice.

entries.old: Bring enough cash for your whole trip, or withdraw it in Dushanbe before heading to other regions. The UK says very few businesses accept credit cards, there are no ATMs in rural areas, and official exchange booths may refuse damaged or marked notes and US dollars issued before 2013.
entries.new: The UK advises bringing enough cash for your entire stay or withdrawing it in Dushanbe before heading to other regions. It says very few businesses accept credit cards, there are no ATMs in rural areas, and official exchange booths may refuse damaged or marked notes and US dollars issued before 2013.

entries.old: Visa-free visitors must register with the authorities within 10 working days of arrival, and hotels can no longer do it for you — go to the registration office (OVIR) in Dushanbe. eVisa holders are exempt from registration.
entries.new: Tajikistan's MFA says visitors under the visa waiver must register with the authorities within 10 working days of arrival, and that eVisa holders are exempt from registration. The UK Foreign Office says hotels are no longer permitted to register guests, so register at the OVIR office in Dushanbe.

entries.old: About 80 nationalities — including all EU countries, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea — can visit visa-free for up to 30 days, and most CIS citizens enter visa-free with no time limit. British and Israeli citizens need a visa and can apply for the eVisa at evisa.tj, as can about 130 nationalities in all; the rest apply at a Tajik embassy.
entries.new: Citizens of the 52 countries on Tajikistan's January 2022 visa-waiver list, including all EU countries, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea, can visit visa-free for up to 30 days, and citizens of Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Ukraine and Georgia enter with no time limit set. British and Israeli citizens need a visa and can apply for the eVisa at evisa.tj, as can about 130 nationalities in all; the rest apply at a Tajik embassy.

entries.old: No — US passport holders can enter Tajikistan visa-free for up to 30 days. For a longer trip, apply for the 60-day eVisa at evisa.tj before travel.
entries.new: No. US passport holders can enter Tajikistan visa-free for up to 30 days. For a stay of more than 30 days, Tajikistan's MFA says you need a visa suited to the purpose of the trip before travelling.

entries.old: The Pamir Highway crosses the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region, which requires a separate GBAO permit for all foreigners. eVisa applicants add it for USD 20 during the online application; visa-free travelers arrange it in Dushanbe through OVIR or a tour agency. Carry several copies. It is checked at police posts along the route.
entries.new: The Pamir Highway crosses the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region, which requires a separate permit in addition to a Tajik visa. eVisa applicants add it for USD 20 during the online application; the UK Foreign Office says others can get it from a Tajik embassy before travelling or from the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Tajikistan.

entries.old: Yes. The eVisa and the visa waiver are accepted at the main road borders with Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan as well as at Dushanbe airport. Print your eVisa and GBAO permit, and confirm the specific crossing is open before setting out, as smaller posts close periodically.
entries.new: Yes. Tajikistan's eVisa portal says e-visa holders can enter through all border points. The UK Foreign Office says the land border with Afghanistan has been closed since 2021.

entries.old: Afghan citizens are not eligible for the eVisa. Apply at a Tajik embassy; approval involves additional checks and border crossings may be restricted.
entries.new: Afghan citizens are not eligible for the eVisa. Apply at a Tajik embassy.

entries.old: Visa-free under CIS-era bilateral agreements — long stays are permitted, but registration rules can apply; confirm the exact allowance before staying beyond 90 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days, according to the Consular Department of Tajikistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

entries.old: Visa-free with no time limit set, under CIS-era bilateral agreements. Registration rules can apply to longer stays.
entries.new: Visa-free with no time limit set, according to the Consular Department of Tajikistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

entries.old: Not eligible for the eVisa. Apply for a visa at a Tajik embassy or consulate. A visa can also be issued on arrival at Dushanbe International Airport; some visa types need an invitation confirmed in advance.
entries.new: Not eligible for the eVisa. Apply for a visa at a Tajik embassy or consulate. A visa can also be obtained on arrival from the Consular Bureau at Dushanbe International Airport, by prior agreement with the Consular Department.

entries.old: Visa-free for short tourist stays under the Iran–Tajikistan waiver agreement in force since 2024. Confirm current implementation before travel.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 30 days, according to the Consular Department of Tajikistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

entries.old: Not eligible for the eVisa. Apply for a visa at a Tajik embassy or consulate. A visa can also be issued on arrival at Dushanbe International Airport; some visa types need an invitation confirmed in advance. Travelers over 55 may instead enter visa-free for up to 14 days.
entries.new: Not eligible for the eVisa. Apply for a visa at a Tajik embassy or consulate. A visa can also be obtained on arrival from the Consular Bureau at Dushanbe International Airport, by prior agreement with the Consular Department. Travelers over 55 may instead enter visa-free for up to 14 days.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 30 days under the 2018 bilateral agreement with Uzbekistan.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 30 days, according to the Consular Department of Tajikistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

entries.old: Most visitors need a Tanzanian visa, best obtained as an eVisa through the official immigration portal — USD 50 for an ordinary single-entry visa, while US citizens must buy the USD 100 multiple-entry visa. East African Community neighbors and citizens of many Commonwealth and southern African countries enter visa-free, and every foreign visitor must also buy Tanzania's mandatory local inbound tra
entries.new: Visitors who need a Tanzanian visa can apply online, which Tanzania Immigration recommends, or obtain it on arrival: USD 50 for the ordinary single-entry visa, while US citizens must apply for the USD 100 multiple-entry visa. Nationals of the East African Community, of SADC countries except Comoros and of most Commonwealth countries do not need a visa, and the UK Foreign Office says all visitors except residents must also hold Tanzania's mandatory inbound travel insurance.

entries.old: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Tanzania, with at least one blank page for the visa.
entries.new: Your passport must have at least six months' validity and at least one unused visa page when you apply for the visa.

entries.old: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if you arrive from, or spent more than 12 hours in transit through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — this catches many travelers connecting through Nairobi or Addis Ababa.
entries.new: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required of travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including those who spent more than 12 hours in transit at the airport of such a country.

entries.old: There is a risk of malaria in certain areas of Tanzania and at certain times of year. Antimalarial medication may be recommended depending on your itinerary and season — see a health professional, ideally six weeks before travel — and protect yourself from mosquito bites at all times.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says there is a risk of malaria in certain areas of Tanzania and at certain times of year, that antimalarial medication may be recommended depending on your itinerary and the time of year, and that you should consult a health professional, ideally six weeks before travel, and protect yourself from mosquito bites at all times.

entries.old: All foreign visitors except residents must hold Tanzanian mandatory inbound travel insurance, bought for their first port of entry: from the state National Insurance Corporation (NIC) if they arrive in mainland Tanzania first, or from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) if they arrive in Zanzibar first. One policy is enough, it covers up to 92 days, other insurance is not accepted in its plac
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors except residents must hold Tanzanian mandatory inbound travel insurance, bought for their first port of entry: from the National Insurance Corporation (NIC) if they arrive in mainland Tanzania first, or from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) if they arrive in Zanzibar first. One policy is enough, it covers up to 92 days, other insurance is not accepted in its place, and it can be bought online or on arrival. Visitors without it may be refused entry.

entries.old: Visitors must show a return or onward ticket on arrival.
entries.new: Visitors must show their return ticket on arrival.

entries.old: Foreign visitors (except residents) who arrive in mainland Tanzania first must hold the mandatory inbound travel insurance sold by the state National Insurance Corporation (NIC), covering up to 92 days; other policies are not accepted in its place. Visitors without it may be refused entry.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says visitors (except residents) who arrive in mainland Tanzania first must hold the mandatory inbound travel insurance sold by the National Insurance Corporation (NIC), covering up to 92 days; other policies are not accepted in its place. Visitors without it may be refused entry.

entries.old: Inclusive of all charges, per visitor; covers stays of up to 92 consecutive days. Children aged 3–17 pay half; infants under 3 are free.
entries.new: Inclusive of all charges, per visitor; covers stays of up to 92 consecutive days.

entries.old: Since October 2024, foreign visitors who arrive in Zanzibar first must hold the local inbound travel insurance issued by the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation. It covers the stay in Tanzania for up to 92 days, so only the first port of entry needs a policy. It is checked on arrival; buy it through the official Zanzibar channels before travel to skip airport lines.
entries.new: Foreign visitors who arrive in Zanzibar first must hold the inbound travel insurance issued by the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation; proof of other international insurance is not accepted. The policy is valid inside Tanzania for up to 92 consecutive days, and one policy per visitor is allowed per trip.

entries.old: Cash of USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent in other currencies) must be declared on arrival and departure.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says all currencies exceeding USD 10,000 must be declared on arrival in and departure from Tanzania.

entries.old: Tanzania is one of Africa's most-visited safari destinations and the vast majority of trips are trouble-free. Petty theft occurs in Dar es Salaam, Arusha and on Zanzibar beaches — use registered taxis at night and keep valuables out of sight — and the Mozambique border area in the far south should be avoided.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office (FCDO) advises against all but essential travel to any area within 20 km of Tanzania's border with the Cabo Delgado province of Mozambique, because of attacks by groups linked with Islamic extremism. It also says tourists in Dar es Salaam have been 'express kidnapped', robbed and forced to withdraw cash from ATMs, and that it is safest to arrange a taxi through a hotel or travel operator.

entries.old: Tanzania requires mandatory inbound travel insurance (up to 92 days): from the National Insurance Corporation if you land on the mainland first, or from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (USD 44) if you land in Zanzibar first. One policy is enough, your own insurance does not replace it, and it is checked on arrival.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says Tanzania requires mandatory inbound travel insurance, covering up to 92 days: from the National Insurance Corporation if you land on the mainland first, or from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (USD 44, according to its FAQ) if you land in Zanzibar first. One policy is enough, and your own insurance does not replace it.

entries.old: Visas are issued on arrival at major airports and borders, but lines are long and payment is cash US dollars — the official eVisa at visa.immigration.go.tz is the smoother option; beware lookalike third-party visa sites.
entries.new: Visas can also be obtained on arrival at official entry points, but Tanzania Immigration recommends applying online, and only through its official website, not through any other online links.

entries.old: Most visitors do. An ordinary single-entry visa costs USD 50 as an eVisa or on arrival. East African Community citizens and nationals of many Commonwealth and southern African countries are visa-exempt, while US citizens must buy the USD 100 multiple-entry visa.
entries.new: Nationals of the East African Community, of SADC countries except Comoros and of Commonwealth countries other than the United Kingdom, Canada, Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand do not need a visa. Others need one: the ordinary single-entry visa costs USD 50, online or on arrival, while US citizens must apply for the USD 100 multiple-entry visa.

entries.old: Yes — Zanzibar is part of the United Republic of Tanzania, so the same visa covers it. Zanzibar does run its own immigration checks on arrival. All foreign visitors must also hold the mandatory inbound travel insurance, bought once for the first port of entry: from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (USD 44) if you arrive in Zanzibar first, or from the National Insurance Corporation if you arrive
entries.new: Yes. Tanzania's visa guidelines say a visitor to both the mainland and Zanzibar selects the first destination on the form and may visit both without a new visa. The UK Foreign Office says all visitors except residents must also hold the mandatory inbound travel insurance, bought once for the first port of entry: from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (USD 44) if you arrive in Zanzibar first, or from the National Insurance Corporation if you arrive on the mainland first.

entries.old: For most nationalities, yes — at major airports (Dar es Salaam, Kilimanjaro, Zanzibar) and main land borders, paid in cash US dollars. Nationals of the 23 countries on the guidelines' no-visa-on-arrival list (among them Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Pakistan, Somalia and Syria), stateless people and refugees cannot: they must hold an approved eVisa before travelling. For everyone else the officia
entries.new: For the nationalities on the guidelines' visa-on-arrival list, yes, at official entry points. Nationals of the 23 countries on the guidelines' no-visa-on-arrival list (among them Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Pakistan, Somalia and Syria), stateless people and refugees cannot, unless the Commissioner General of Immigration has given special permission: they must hold an approved eVisa before travelling. Tanzania Immigration recommends applying online.

entries.old: Under a reciprocal arrangement, US passport holders are only eligible for the multiple-entry visa at USD 100 (valid 12 months). The USD 50 single-entry visa is not available to them.
entries.new: Tanzania's visa guidelines say that, under bilateral agreements between Tanzania and the United States, US passport holders are not entitled to the ordinary visa and must apply for the multiple-entry visa (USD 100, valid up to 12 months) even for a single trip.

entries.old: Only if you arrive from — or transit more than 12 hours through — a country with yellow fever risk. Direct arrivals from Europe, the Americas or Asia do not need one, but connections through Nairobi or Addis Ababa can trigger the requirement.
entries.new: Only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from, or spent more than 12 hours in transit at the airport of, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

entries.old: Apply for the USD 50 ordinary eVisa at visa.immigration.go.tz, or obtain the same visa on arrival (cash US dollars) at major airports and border posts.
entries.new: Apply for the USD 50 ordinary eVisa at visa.immigration.go.tz, or obtain the same visa on arrival at an official entry point.

entries.old: Tanzania's visa guidelines exempt nationals of SADC member countries (except Comoros) from the visa, and this nationality is on neither the page's visa-on-arrival list nor its list of nationals who cannot get one. Confirm on visa.immigration.go.tz before travel.
entries.new: Tanzania's visa guidelines exempt nationals of SADC member countries (except Comoros) from the visa, and the Immigration Department's list of nationals who are not required to apply for a visa names this country.

entries.old: Nationals of most Commonwealth countries and southern African neighbors do not need a visa. Tanzania's official visa pages state no maximum length of stay for visa-exempt visitors; the exemption list is maintained by the Immigration Department, so confirm on visa.immigration.go.tz before travel.
entries.new: Tanzania's visa guidelines exempt nationals of the East African Community, of SADC countries except Comoros and of most Commonwealth countries from the visa. Tanzania's official visa pages state no maximum length of stay for visa-exempt visitors.

entries.old: Apply online for the USD 50 ordinary eVisa at visa.immigration.go.tz and wait for approval before you travel. Tanzania's visa guidelines list this nationality among those who cannot obtain a visa on arrival unless the Commissioner General of Immigration has given special permission. The same page also names it in its visa-on-arrival list; we show the stricter statement, which cannot leave you stra
entries.new: Tanzania's visa guidelines name this nationality both in the visa-on-arrival list and among those who cannot obtain a visa on arrival unless the Commissioner General of Immigration has given special permission. Apply online for the USD 50 ordinary eVisa at visa.immigration.go.tz and wait for approval before you travel.

entries.old: Apply for the USD 50 ordinary eVisa at visa.immigration.go.tz, or obtain the same visa on arrival (cash US dollars) at major airports and border posts. Tanzania's visa guidelines exempt most Commonwealth nationals, but the same page lists this nationality for visa on arrival; we show the visa, which cannot leave you stranded at the border.
entries.new: Tanzania's visa guidelines exempt most Commonwealth nationals, but the same page lists this nationality among those who can obtain a visa on arrival. Apply for the USD 50 ordinary eVisa at visa.immigration.go.tz, or obtain the same visa on arrival at an official entry point.

entries.old: The Immigration Department's list of nationals and passport holders who are not required to apply for a visa names "Hong Kong, China". Confirm on visa.immigration.go.tz before travel.
entries.new: The Immigration Department's list of nationals and passport holders who are not required to apply for a visa names "Hong Kong, China".

entries.old: The Immigration Department's list of nationals and passport holders who are not required to apply for a visa names "Macao, China". The visa guidelines' summary of exempt groups (East African Community, SADC and most Commonwealth countries) does not cover this passport, and neither list states a maximum stay, so confirm with the Immigration Department before travel.
entries.new: The Immigration Department's list of nationals and passport holders who are not required to apply for a visa names "Macao, China". The visa guidelines' summary of exempt groups (East African Community, SADC and most Commonwealth countries) does not cover this passport, and neither list states a maximum stay.

entries.old: The Immigration Department's list of nationals and passport holders who are not required to apply for a visa names "Romania". The visa guidelines' summary of exempt groups (East African Community, SADC and most Commonwealth countries) does not cover this passport, and neither list states a maximum stay, so confirm with the Immigration Department before travel.
entries.new: The Immigration Department's list of nationals and passport holders who are not required to apply for a visa names "Romania". The visa guidelines' summary of exempt groups (East African Community, SADC and most Commonwealth countries) does not cover this passport, and neither list states a maximum stay.

entries.old: US citizens are only eligible for the USD 100 multiple-entry visa (valid 12 months). The USD 50 single-entry visa is not available to them; apply at visa.immigration.go.tz or on arrival.

entries.field: FAQ: Do I need a visa for Trinidad and Tobago?
entries.old: Some foreign governments still tell their citizens no visa is needed; the Immigration Division's list is the authority.
entries.new: It depends on your passport. Citizens of the 42 countries and territories on the Immigration Division’s no-visa list — including the UK, Canada and most Commonwealth countries — need no visa, and neither do EU citizens (Ireland is outside the agreement), who get up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU waiver agreement, or South Koreans, who get 90 days under a bilateral agreement. US, Japanese, Brazilian, Irish, Turkish, Serbian and Colombian citizens are visa-free according to their own governments (and, for Brazil, Trinidad and Tobago’s embassy), although the no-visa list does not name them. CARICOM nationals enter under Caribbean free movement with up to six months. Everyone else — including Australian and most Latin American citizens, and Venezuelan passport holders — must obtain a visa before traveling, online through the Immigration Division’s eVisa portal, which replaced all earlier visa procedures in April 2024.

All other Indian passport holders need a pre-arranged tourist eVisa (30 or 60 days), applied for through an airline, a hotel, a licensed travel agent or a sponsor resident in the UAE.

entries.field: FAQ: How much does a UAE tourist eVisa cost?

entries.field: FAQ: Do I need a visa to transit through Dubai or Abu Dhabi?

GDRFA Dubai lists the government fee as AED 50, plus the airline’s own service fee. It must be arranged before travel.

entries.old: The UAE has very low crime and is among the safest destinations for travelers. The main risks are legal, not criminal: strict laws on drugs, medications, public behavior and online speech. Regional tensions occasionally disrupt air travel — monitor the news around departure.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says the crime rate is low and violent crime is rare, though petty crime such as pickpocketing and theft from cars may occur. Because of regional tensions, the UK Foreign Office says travellers should be prepared for flight cancellations and airspace closures at short notice.

entries.old: need prior permission from the Ministry of Health and Prevention, which publishes the list of controlled medicines and issues permits online. Bringing banned medication without approval can mean confiscation, heavy fines or jail.

The UK Foreign Office says the Ministry publishes the list of controlled drugs and that approval is applied for online.

Canada adds that the legal blood alcohol limit for driving is zero, that verbal insults and obscene gestures may be criminal acts, and that laws on online behaviour, including social media, are strict.

entries.field: FAQ: ESTA (fee rises to $40.62 on 16 October 2026 per the DHS FY 2027 notice)
entries.old: ESTA is the online travel authorization for the US Visa Waiver Program. Citizens of VWP countries (including the UK, most of Western Europe, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand) must obtain it before boarding. It costs $40.27, is valid for 2 years (or until your passport expires) and allows stays of up to 90 days.
entries.new: ESTA is the online travel authorization for the US Visa Waiver Program. Citizens of VWP countries (including the UK, most of Western Europe, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand) must obtain it before boarding. It costs $40.27 — $40.62 from 16 October 2026 under DHS's fiscal year 2027 adjustment — is valid for 2 years (or until your passport expires) and allows stays of up to 90 days.

entries.field: FAQ: ESTA stay ("border runs" claim not on a page read)
entries.old: Up to 90 days per visit, for tourism, business or transit. The stay cannot be extended, and quick border runs to Canada or Mexico do not reset the 90-day clock.
entries.new: Up to 90 days per visit, for tourism, business or transit. The ESTA site says that if you are admitted under the Visa Waiver Program you may not change or extend your status.

entries.new: The B1/B2 visitor visa application fee is $185. Depending on nationality, a reciprocity issuance fee may also be due when the visa is issued.

entries.old: Uruguay has one of South America's most open entry policies: Mercosur and associate-member nationals arrive on a national ID card, and citizens of the EU, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada and a long list of other countries enter visa-free for 90 days, extendable by another 90.
entries.new: Citizens of the EU, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, most of Latin America and a long list of other countries enter Uruguay visa-free for up to 90 days, and the stay can be extended with the Dirección Nacional de Migración; other nationalities need a visa from a Uruguayan consulate.
entries.note: "One of South America's most open entry policies", the ID-card route and "extendable by another 90" rest on no official page we read; the extension page gives no length.

entries.old: 3 consular pesos (USD 42), charged only if the visa is granted; official and diplomatic passports pay nothing. Consular fees are revised every 1 January and the Foreign Ministry's page was last updated in October 2020, so confirm the amount with the consulate where you apply.
entries.new: 3 consular pesos (USD 42), charged only if the visa is granted; official and diplomatic passports pay nothing. The Foreign Ministry says consular fees change on 1 January each year.
entries.note: Global rule: sentences no official source confirms were deleted; what remains is stated by the cited official page.

entries.old: 3 consular pesos (USD 42), the visa fee the Foreign Ministry publishes, charged only if the visa is granted. Covers meetings, conferences and negotiations but not paid work in Uruguay; the application asks for an invitation letter or hotel booking and proof of funds. Consular fees are revised every 1 January, so confirm the amount with the consulate.
entries.new: 3 consular pesos (USD 42), the visa fee the Foreign Ministry publishes, charged only if the visa is granted. The application asks for an invitation letter or hotel booking and proof of funds.
entries.note: The scope (meetings, not paid work) and the advice to confirm are not on the Foreign Ministry page.

entries.old: Visa-free visitors need a passport valid for the duration of their stay; visa applicants need at least 6 months' validity after arrival. Airlines and onward countries often apply the stricter rule, so six months is the safe margin. Mercosur and associate-member nationals may enter on a valid national identity card instead.
entries.new: The UK government says your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay and have at least one blank page for an entry stamp. Visa applicants need a passport valid for at least 6 months after arrival in Uruguay, according to the Foreign Ministry.
entries.note: Foreign-government advice attributed; the "safe margin" advice and the ID-card claim rest on no official page.

entries.old: Uruguay has no yellow fever risk and does not require a certificate for entry. Vaccination matters only if your trip continues to Brazil, Paraguay or Bolivia, where risk areas and onward requirements do apply.
entries.new: The US CDC says Uruguay does not require yellow fever vaccination for entry.
entries.note: "No yellow fever risk" and the onward-travel sentence are not on the CDC page; the CDC statement is now attributed.

entries.old: No published amount and rarely asked of tourists; visa applicants must show bank statements covering the trip.
entries.new: No official source we could read publishes an amount. Visa applicants must show proof of economic solvency, according to the Foreign Ministry.
entries.note: "Rarely asked of tourists" rests on no page; the Ministry asks for "solvencia económica", not specifically bank statements.

entries.old: Cash or negotiable instruments worth USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared to customs on entry and exit. The rule is applied on the Buquebus ferries from Buenos Aires as well as at airports.
entries.new: Cash, precious metals or other monetary instruments worth USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared to customs on entry and exit.
entries.note: The Buquebus sentence is not on the customs page.

entries.old: The UK government's travel advice says it is illegal for visitors to import fruit, vegetables, animals or dairy products and their derivatives, flammable materials, alkaloids, narcotics or obscene objects, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty. | The UK government's travel advice says registered Uruguayan nationals and long-term residents may grow cannabis or buy it from registered pharmacies, but that it is illegal for tourists to do so.
entries.new: The UK government's travel advice says it is illegal for visitors to import fruit, vegetables, animals or dairy products and their derivatives, flammable materials, alkaloids, narcotics or obscene objects, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
entries.note: The UK advice pages we read do not carry the cannabis statement; Canada's, kept as a tip, does.

entries.old: Uruguay's Ministry of Tourism says non-residents pay no VAT on hotels and other accommodation all year, on showing an identity document issued abroad. A 9-point VAT refund on restaurant bills, car hire and some other services paid with a foreign-issued card ran until 30 April 2026; check whether it has been extended.
entries.new: Uruguay's Ministry of Tourism says non-residents pay no VAT on hotels and other accommodation, on showing an identity document issued abroad. A 9-point VAT refund on restaurant bills, car hire and some other services paid with a foreign-issued card ran until 30 April 2026.
entries.note: "All year" and "check whether it has been extended" are not on the Ministry page.

entries.field: FAQ: do I need a visa
entries.old: Probably not. Uruguay waives visas for a very broad list of nationalities — the EU and EEA, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel, Russia and most of Latin America and the Caribbean — for tourist stays of up to 90 days. Mercosur and associate-member nationals can enter on a national ID card. Everyone else applies for a visa at a Uruguayan consulate.
entries.new: Uruguay waives visas for a broad list of nationalities — including the EU, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel, Russia and most of Latin America and the Caribbean — for tourist stays of up to 90 days. Everyone else applies for a visa at a Uruguayan consulate.
entries.note: The ID-card route rests on no official page we read; "probably not" removed.

entries.old: Ninety days per entry for most visa-free nationalities. The Dirección Nacional de Migración can grant one extension (prórroga) of a further 90 days if you apply before the first period runs out, giving up to 180 days in total.
entries.new: Up to 90 days for visa-free tourist stays. The Dirección Nacional de Migración can extend the stay (prórroga); the request must be made at least 15 days before the permitted stay runs out.
entries.note: The extension page gives no length; "a further 90 days… up to 180 in total" rests on no official page.

entries.old: Yes, if you are a national of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador or Peru. Mercosur and associate-member citizens cross with a valid national identity document — the usual choice for the ferry from Buenos Aires — and stay 90 days. Bring a passport if you are connecting on from outside the bloc.
entries.new: No official source we could read lists which national identity cards Uruguay accepts instead of a passport. The Dirección Nacional de Migración accepts a national identity document or a passport when you apply to extend a stay.
entries.note: The list of ID-card nationalities, the ferry remark and the 90-day stay rest on no official page we read.

entries.old: No. United States passport holders enter visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days, with one 90-day extension available from Uruguayan immigration. There is no reciprocity fee and no advance authorization to buy.
entries.new: No. United States passport holders enter visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days, and the stay can be extended with the Dirección Nacional de Migración.
entries.note: The 90-day extension length, "no reciprocity fee" and "no advance authorization" rest on no official page we read.

entries.old: Yes. Apply to the Dirección Nacional de Migración at least 15 days before your permitted stay runs out, with your passport or national ID card. One extension of up to 90 days is normally granted. The fee is 225.60 indexed units (UI, Uruguay's inflation-linked unit of account, paid in pesos) while your stay is still valid, or 345 UI once it has expired.
entries.new: Yes. Apply to the Dirección Nacional de Migración at least 15 days before your permitted stay runs out, with your passport or national identity document. The fee is 225.60 indexed units (UI) while your stay is still valid, or 345 UI once it has expired.
entries.note: "One extension of up to 90 days is normally granted" is not on the Migration page.

entries.old: No. Uruguay has no yellow fever risk and does not ask arriving travelers for a certificate. It becomes relevant only if your trip continues to Brazil, Paraguay or Bolivia, which have their own risk areas and requirements.
entries.new: No. The US CDC says Uruguay does not require yellow fever vaccination for entry.
entries.note: Global rule: sentences no official source confirms were deleted; what remains is stated by the cited official page.

entries.old: Uruguay is among the safest countries in South America and the tourist areas — Ciudad Vieja by day, Pocitos, Colonia, Punta del Este — are calm. Petty theft and occasional armed robbery do occur in parts of Montevideo, so avoid quiet streets in Ciudad Vieja after dark and the outer barrios, and do not leave anything visible in a parked car.
entries.new: The UK government says street crime happens in Montevideo, including mugging and robbery (sometimes armed), that criminals regularly break into cars left on the street, and that crime rates are generally lower in other parts of Uruguay. The Government of Canada advises a high degree of caution in Montevideo due to crime and says petty crime, muggings and armed robbery are more common in places including the Ciudad Vieja.
entries.note: "Among the safest countries in South America" and "the tourist areas are calm" are not on the cited FCDO page.

entries.old: Uzbekistan admits citizens of about 90 countries and territories — including the whole EU, the UK, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia and New Zealand — visa-free, most of them for 30 days. 44 other nationalities use the inexpensive USD 20 eVisa, and the rest apply at an Uzbek embassy.
entries.new: Uzbekistan admits citizens of about 90 countries and territories — including the whole EU, the UK, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia and New Zealand — visa-free, most of them for 30 days. 44 other nationalities use the USD 20 eVisa, and the rest apply at an Uzbek embassy.

entries.field: FAQ: US citizens (the visa-free list is the Foreign Ministry's, not the eVisa portal's; purpose limit not stated)
entries.old: No. The official eVisa portal lists US citizens as visa-free for up to 30 days, for tourism or business. Longer stays or other purposes need a visa from an Uzbek embassy.
entries.new: No. The Foreign Ministry lists US citizens as visa-free for up to 30 days. For a longer stay, the Ministry says a foreign citizen must obtain one of Uzbekistan's entry visas.

entries.field: FAQ: how the eVisa works ("normally issued" replaced by the portal's stated consideration time)
entries.old: Apply at e-visa.gov.uz with a passport scan and photo. The single-entry eVisa costs USD 20, is normally issued within two working days, and allows a 30-day stay within a 90-day validity window; double-entry and multiple-entry versions cost USD 35 and USD 50.
entries.new: Apply at e-visa.gov.uz with a passport scan and photo. The single-entry eVisa costs USD 20; the portal says applications are considered within two working days, and the eVisa allows a stay of up to 30 days and is valid for entry within 90 days. Double-entry and multiple-entry versions cost USD 35 and USD 50.

entries.field: FAQ: registration (unattributed rules now attributed to the UK Foreign Office)
entries.old: Yes — accommodation must be registered for every night. Hotels and guesthouses do this automatically and give you slips or electronic confirmation; keep them until departure. Staying with friends or in an apartment requires registration through the official Emehmon system, and gaps can lead to fines on exit.
entries.new: Yes. The UK Foreign Office says you must register within 3 days of arrival; hotels register their guests, and private hosts register you with the local OVIR or on the Emehmon electronic system. It says the authorities require a full record of where you have stayed on departure, and that missing or late registration can bring a fine for each day and possible deportation.

entries.field: FAQ: length of visa-free stay ("fresh entry" advice removed; CIS countries named)
entries.old: The standard waiver allows 30 days per visit. Citizens of most CIS countries have more generous bilateral arrangements, and Kyrgyz citizens get 60 days. The eVisa also caps stays at 30 days — longer stays require an embassy visa or a fresh entry.
entries.new: The standard visa-free regime allows up to 30 days from crossing the border. Citizens of Azerbaijan, Georgia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia and Ukraine have a visa-free regime of unlimited duration, and Kyrgyz citizens get 60 days. The eVisa allows stays of up to 30 days; for longer stays the Foreign Ministry says an entry visa is needed.

entries.old: Every night in Uzbekistan must be registered. Hotels and licensed guesthouses do it automatically. Keep the small registration slips (or e-mails) until you leave, as border officers can ask for them; private hosts must register you through the Emehmon portal.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says you must register within 3 days of arrival and that hotels register their guests; private hosts register you through their local OVIR or the Emehmon system. Canada's travel advice says the registration slip may be requested when you leave.

entries.field: Tip: money exchange (unattributed advice now attributed)
entries.old: Change money only through official exchange booths, banks or major hotels. The Government of Canada says buying currency on the black market is illegal and may result in extortion or jail.
entries.new: The UK FCDO advises changing money only through official exchange booths. The Government of Canada says money can be exchanged at official counters at international airports, banks and major hotels, and that buying currency on the black market is illegal and may result in extortion or jail.

entries.field: eVisa fee notes (tariff is published by the Foreign Ministry, not a "government services portal")
entries.old: USD 20 single entry; USD 35 double entry and USD 50 multiple entry, per the government services portal’s consular fee tariff.
entries.new: USD 20 single entry; USD 35 double entry and USD 50 multiple entry, per the Foreign Ministry's consular fee tariff and the eVisa portal.

entries.field: Currency limits (UK figure was presented as Uzbekistan's rule; Canada gives a different threshold)
entries.old: Cash worth USD 10,000 or more must be declared on entry on the written customs declaration — fill in two copies and make sure customs sign and stamp both. You cannot leave Uzbekistan with more foreign currency than you brought in, and undeclared currency may be confiscated.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says cash of USD 10,000 or more must be declared on entry on the written customs declaration, filled in in two copies that customs sign and stamp, that you cannot leave with more foreign currency than you brought in, and that undeclared currency may be confiscated. Canada's travel advice gives the declaration threshold as foreign currency above USD 2,000.

entries.field: Safety text (a "does not advise against travel" claim the page does not make removed; now attributed)
entries.old: The UK government does not advise against travel to any part of Uzbekistan. Pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common in crowded places such as bazaars and on public transport, and terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out. You must carry your passport at all times — police often check.
entries.new: The UK government says pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common in crowded places such as bazaars and on public transport, that terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out, and that you must carry your passport at all times because police often carry out checks.

entries.field: Passport validity (UK figure was presented as Uzbekistan's rule; now attributed)
entries.old: Your passport must be valid for at least 3 months after the date you arrive in Uzbekistan.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for at least 3 months after the date you arrive in Uzbekistan.

entries.old: Vatican City issues no visas of its own. Entry is through Italy, so a Schengen short-stay visa issued for Italy is required.
entries.new: Entry is through Italy, so a Schengen short-stay visa issued for Italy is required.

entries.old: Vatican City is an enclave within Rome that Italian citizens reach from Italy.
entries.new: Vatican City lies on the right bank of the Tiber in Rome, according to the Vatican City State; Italian citizens reach it from Italy.

entries.old: A Schengen short-stay visa issued for Italy is required. The EU suspended its visa facilitation agreement with Russia; fees are higher and processing slower.
entries.new: A Schengen short-stay visa issued for Italy is required.

entries.old: The EU suspended Vanuatu's visa waiver over its citizenship-by-investment scheme; a Schengen visa issued for Italy is required.
entries.new: Vanuatu is on the EU's list of nationalities that need a visa (Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/11), so a Schengen visa issued for Italy is required.
entries.note: The reason (citizenship-by-investment) is not stated in the consolidated regulation read; the listing is.

entries.old: Travelers who need a Schengen visa for Italy must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it.

entries.old: Any onward-travel questions are asked by Italian officers at your point of entry into the Schengen Area.
entries.new: Entry is through Italy, so the Schengen Borders Code applies: the supporting documents border guards may check at your point of entry into the Schengen Area include a return or round-trip ticket.

entries.old: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS authorization to enter the Schengen Area, and therefore to reach Vatican City through Italy. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

entries.old: The UK's advice for Italy also covers Vatican City. entries.old: Official advice is severe. The UK advises against all travel within 80 km of the Colombian border and 40 km of the Brazilian and Guyanese borders, to Zulia state, the Orinoco Mining Arc and the area south of the Orinoco in Delta Amacuro, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the country. The United States rates Venezuela Level 3 (reconsider travel) for crime, kidnapping, terrorism and poor health care, and Level 4 (do not travel) for the Colombian border region, Amazonas, Apure, Táchira and Guárico states, Aragua outside Maracay and rural Bolívar. Violent crime, armed robbery and kidnapping occur; foreigners, including Europeans, have been detained and accused of terrorism, and arrivals can be held for hours or days for questioning. Power, water, fuel and medicine are often short, especially outside Caracas. After the June 2026 earthquakes La Guaira was declared a disaster zone under military control. Consular help is very limited.

For them, the Belize Tourism Board says the passport must be valid for at least 30 days after arrival, provided you return home straight afterwards and are not travelling on to a country that requires 6 months.
