entries.new: Belize's Immigration Department asks visa applicants for a passport valid for more than 6 months, and publishes no minimum for visa-exempt visitors. The UK Foreign Office says your passport must expire more than 3 months after the date you arrive, and that some airlines may refuse boarding if it does not run more than 6 months beyond arrival.
entries.note: The Belize Tourism Board rule is not on any page this entry cites, and '6 months is the safe choice' is our advice; the airline point is now the UK's own wording.

entries.old: BZD 200 (about USD 100) for each 30-day Visitor's Permit Extension, the same for all nationalities. Apply at an Immigration office before your current stamp expires.
entries.new: BZD 200 for each 30-day Visitor's Permit Extension, the same for all nationalities. The extension does not allow employment or business without the Director of Immigration's consent.
entries.note: The USD conversion and 'apply before your stamp expires' are not on the department's page.

entries.old: Travel insurance is not required to enter Belize. The Belize Travel Health Insurance that arriving tourists had to buy during the pandemic became optional in July 2022, when Statutory Instrument No. 100 of 2022 replaced the COVID-19 entry regulations and Cabinet removed all public-health measures at points of entry. Cover for medical emergencies is still sensible.
entries.new: Travel insurance is not required to enter Belize. The Belize Travel Health Insurance that arriving tourists had to buy during the pandemic became optional in July 2022, when Statutory Instrument No. 100 of 2022 replaced the COVID-19 entry regulations and Cabinet removed all public-health measures at points of entry.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: No. Belize's travel health insurance became optional in July 2022, when Statutory Instrument No. 100 of 2022 replaced the COVID-19 entry regulations and Cabinet removed all public-health measures at points of entry. Cover for medical emergencies is still sensible.
entries.new: No. Belize's travel health insurance became optional in July 2022, when Statutory Instrument No. 100 of 2022 replaced the COVID-19 entry regulations and Cabinet removed all public-health measures at points of entry.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Visa applicants must submit a flight itinerary showing arrival in Belize and the return date to their country of origin (or onward departure if transiting). Customs officials may also ask any visitor for a return or onward ticket.
entries.new: Visa applicants must submit a flight itinerary showing arrival in Belize and the return date to their country of origin (or onward departure if transiting). Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask visitors for a return or onward ticket.
entries.note: Attributed to Canada, which states it.

entries.old: Visa applicants must provide an employment letter and bank records showing the last six months of transactions (their sponsor's too, if sponsored). Customs officials may ask any visitor for proof of sufficient funds. No amount is published.
entries.new: Visa applicants must provide an employment letter and bank records showing the last six months of transactions (their sponsor's too, if sponsored). Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask visitors for proof of sufficient funds to cover their stay. No amount is published.
entries.note: Attributed to Canada, which states it.

entries.old: Travelers whose nationality would normally need a Belizean visa are exempt for visits of up to 30 days if they hold a valid multiple-entry US visa or a US permanent residence card. The same exemption covers a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa, and a valid multiple-entry Canadian visa or Canadian permanent residence card. Border officers still decide on entry.
entries.new: Travelers whose nationality would normally need a Belizean visa are exempt for visits of up to 30 days if they hold a valid multiple-entry US visa or a US permanent residence card. The same exemption covers a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa, and a valid multiple-entry Canadian visa or Canadian permanent residence card.
entries.note: 'Border officers still decide on entry' is not on the department's page.

entries.old: If your nationality needs a Belizean visa but you hold a valid multiple-entry US, Canadian or Schengen visa (or a US or Canadian permanent residence card), you are generally allowed in without one for up to 30 days — travel on the passport containing that visa and confirm with a consulate before flying.
entries.new: If your nationality needs a Belizean visa but you hold a valid multiple-entry US, Canadian or Schengen visa (or a US or Canadian permanent residence card), the Immigration Department exempts you from the visa for visits of up to 30 days.
entries.note: 'Generally', 'travel on the passport containing that visa' and 'confirm with a consulate' are not on the department's page.

entries.old: Probably not: US, UK, EU, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand, CARICOM and most Commonwealth passports enter visa-free and are stamped in for up to 30 days. Nationalities that do need a visa apply at a Belizean consulate, or are exempt for visits of up to 30 days if they hold a valid multiple-entry US, Canadian or Schengen visa, or a US or Canadian permanent residence card.
entries.new: US, UK, EU, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand, CARICOM and most Commonwealth passports enter visa-free and are stamped in for up to 30 days. Nationalities that do need a visa apply at a Belizean consulate, or are exempt for visits of up to 30 days if they hold a valid multiple-entry US, Canadian or Schengen visa, or a US or Canadian permanent residence card.
entries.note: Hedge removed.

entries.old: The entry stamp is up to 30 days for everyone, including visa-free visitors. You can extend 30 days at a time at an Immigration office with a Visitor's Permit Extension, which costs BZD 200 (about USD 100) each time.
entries.new: The entry stamp is up to 30 days for everyone, including visa-free visitors. You can extend 30 days at a time at an Immigration office with a Visitor's Permit Extension, which costs BZD 200 each time.
entries.note: Unsourced conversion removed.

entries.old: Generally yes — Belize waives its visa requirement for visits of up to 30 days for travelers holding a valid multiple-entry US visa or a US permanent residence card. A valid multiple-entry Canadian or Schengen visa, or a Canadian permanent residence card, qualifies too. Carry the passport containing the visa and confirm current practice with the Belize Immigration Department before traveling, as admission always remains at the border officer's discretion.
entries.new: Yes. Belize's Immigration Department exempts from its visa requirement, for visits of up to 30 days, travellers holding a valid multiple-entry US visa or a US permanent residence card. A valid multiple-entry Canadian or Schengen visa, or a Canadian permanent residence card, qualifies too.
entries.note: 'Generally', the advice to carry the passport and confirm practice, and 'border officer's discretion' are not on the department's page.

entries.old: Generally, yes. The Government of Canada says US dollars are widely accepted and prices are sometimes given in US dollars, but change for US-dollar payments is frequently given in Belize dollars — so check which currency a quoted price is in.
entries.new: Generally, yes. The Government of Canada says US dollars are widely accepted and prices are sometimes given in US dollars, but change for US-dollar payments is frequently given in Belize dollars.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Generally, yes. The Government of Canada says US dollars are widely accepted and prices are sometimes given in US dollars, but change for US-dollar payments is frequently given in Belize dollars.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says US dollars are widely accepted and prices are sometimes given in US dollars, but change for US-dollar payments is frequently given in Belize dollars.
entries.note: Hedge removed.

entries.old: Belize recognizes Taiwan rather than the People's Republic of China, so applications are handled by consulates outside the mainland and clearance can be slow. A valid multiple-entry US, Canadian or Schengen visa, or a US or Canadian permanent residence card, removes the visa requirement for visits of up to 30 days.
entries.new: A visa from a Belizean consulate is required before travel; the Immigration Department's single-entry fee for nationals of the People's Republic of China is BZD 3,000. A valid multiple-entry US, Canadian or Schengen visa, or a US or Canadian permanent residence card, removes the visa requirement for visits of up to 30 days.
entries.note: 'Belize recognizes Taiwan… clearance can be slow' is on no official page we read.

entries.old: Tourist visa required: apply online for the eVisa (30 USD) or get a visa on arrival (30 USD) at international airports and most land borders.
entries.new: Tourist visa required: apply online for the eVisa (30 USD) or get a visa on arrival (30 USD) at international airports and major land border crossings.
entries.note: Canada's travel advice (the page that states where the visa on arrival is issued) says international airports and major land border crossings, not most land borders.

entries.old: Tourist visa required: apply online for the eVisa (30 USD) or get a visa on arrival (30 USD) at international airports and most land borders. Until 15 October 2026, holders of passports of the People's Republic of China (including Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports) may enter visa-free for up to 14 days per entry under a temporary exemption announced on the e-Visa portal; the e-Arrival card is still required.
entries.new: Tourist visa required: apply online for the eVisa (30 USD) or get a visa on arrival (30 USD) at international airports and major land border crossings. Until 15 October 2026, holders of passports of the People's Republic of China (including Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports) may enter visa-free for up to 14 days per entry under a temporary exemption announced on the e-Visa portal; the e-Arrival card is still required.
entries.note: The temporary exemption is stated on the e-Visa portal's news page (3 June 2026); the rows now cite it.

entries.old: Visa-free entry under ASEAN arrangements (14 days). Confirm the current stay length before travel.
entries.new: Visa-free entry for 14 days with an ordinary passport, under the foreign ministry's list of visa exemptions (ASEAN countries).
entries.note: 'Confirm the current stay length before travel' is advice no official page gives; the stay is on the foreign ministry's exemption list, which the rows now cite.

entries.old: Visa-free entry under ASEAN arrangements (30 days). Confirm the current stay length before travel.
entries.new: Visa-free entry for 30 days with an ordinary passport, under the foreign ministry's list of visa exemptions (ASEAN countries).
entries.note: 'Confirm the current stay length before travel' is advice no official page gives; the stay is on the foreign ministry's exemption list, which the rows now cite.

entries.old: Visa-free entry under ASEAN arrangements — 30 days for Indonesian citizens. Confirm the current stay length before travel.
entries.new: Visa-free entry under ASEAN arrangements — 30 days for Indonesian citizens holding ordinary passports.
entries.note: Advice to confirm the stay removed; the 30 days is on the foreign ministry's exemption list.

entries.old: Visa-free entry under ASEAN arrangements — 30 days for Vietnamese citizens. Confirm the current stay length before travel.
entries.new: Visa-free entry under ASEAN arrangements — 30 days for Vietnamese citizens holding ordinary passports.
entries.note: Advice to confirm the stay removed; the 30 days is on the foreign ministry's exemption list.

entries.old: Visa-free entry under the bilateral exemption for Seychellois citizens. Confirm the current stay length before travel.
entries.new: Visa-free entry for 15 days for Seychellois ordinary passport holders, under the foreign ministry's list of visa exemptions.
entries.note: Advice removed; the 15 days is on the foreign ministry's exemption list.

entries.old: Paid at the border. Available at international airports and major land crossings, but the land crossings with Thailand are currently closed. Canada's travel advice (updated 26 May 2026) says no photo is needed and the fee can be paid by card, though cash may be needed if electronic systems are down; the UK government's older page asks for a photo and payment in US dollars, so carry both.
entries.new: Paid at the border. Canada's travel advice (updated 26 May 2026) says the visa on arrival is issued at international airports and major land border crossings, that the land crossings with Thailand are currently closed, that no photo is needed and that the fee can be paid by card, though cash may be needed if electronic systems are down. The UK Foreign Office says you need to provide a photo and pay in US dollars.
entries.note: 'So carry both' is advice no official page gives; availability now attributed to Canada, which states it.

entries.old: The E-class ordinary visa allows 30 days but, unlike the tourist visa, can be extended long-term in-country (with the appropriate extension class). The usual route for longer stays and work.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says business visas are issued on arrival at Phnom Penh airport, at the immigration department, or in advance by any Cambodian embassy. No official source we could read states how far the E-class visa can be extended.
entries.note: The long-term extension and 'usual route for longer stays and work' are on no official page we read; the e-Visa page gives only USD 35, single entry, 1 month.

entries.old: The UK advises against all but essential travel within 20 km of the land border with Thailand, where landmines and unexploded ordnance also remain; Canada and Australia advise against all travel within 50 km of it, and the land crossings with Thailand are closed. Australia advises a high degree of caution in the rest of the country. Watch for bag-snatching by thieves on motorbikes, and be alert to scams, including organized-crime compounds advertised as easy, well-paid jobs. Stick to marked paths in remote areas.
entries.new: The UK advises against all but essential travel within 20 km of the land border with Thailand, where landmines and unexploded ordnance also remain; Canada and Australia advise against all travel within 50 km of it, and the land crossings with Thailand are closed. Australia advises a high degree of caution in the rest of the country. The UK warns that most thefts are bag snatchings, often by thieves on motorbikes, and that organized crime groups run job scams advertising easy, well-paid work. Mined areas are often unmarked: the UK says not to stray off main routes in rural areas.
entries.note: 'Stick to marked paths' inverted the UK's point (mined areas are often unmarked; do not stray off main routes); theft and scam sentences now attributed to the UK, which states them.

entries.old: Apply for the eVisa only on the official site, evisa.gov.kh.
entries.new: The official eVisa site, run by Cambodia's foreign ministry, is evisa.gov.kh.
entries.note: 'Apply only on the official site' is advice no official page gives; the site's official status is stated on it.

entries.old: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist visa: either the eVisa (30 USD, applied for at evisa.gov.kh) or a visa on arrival (30 USD) at airports and major land borders; the land crossings with Thailand are currently closed. Both allow a 30-day stay, extendable once by 30 days.
entries.new: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist visa: either the eVisa (30 USD, applied for at evisa.gov.kh) or a visa on arrival (30 USD) at airports and major land borders; the land crossings with Thailand are currently closed. Both allow a 30-day stay; Canada's travel advice says a visa may be extended only once.
entries.note: 'By 30 days' is on no official page we read; Canada says a visa may be extended only once.

entries.old: A tourist (T) visa can be extended once by 30 days at the immigration department or through agents. For longer stays, enter on an ordinary (E-class) visa instead. It can be extended in-country for 1, 3, 6 or 12 months.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says you can extend a tourist visa while in Cambodia. Canada's travel advice says visas must be renewed for stays over 30 days and may be extended only once. No official source we could read states the length of an extension or of the ordinary (E-class) visa's extensions.
entries.note: 'At the immigration department or through agents', 'by 30 days' and the 1/3/6/12-month E-class extensions are on no official page we read.

entries.old: Citizens of ASEAN countries enter visa-free: 30 days for Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Laos, Singapore and the Philippines, 14 days for Thailand, Myanmar and Brunei. Maldivian (30 days) and Seychellois (15 days) ordinary passports are also exempt. Nearly everyone else needs the eVisa or a visa on arrival.
entries.new: The foreign ministry's list of visa exemptions gives ordinary passport holders of ASEAN countries visa-free entry: 30 days for Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Laos, Singapore and the Philippines, 14 days for Thailand, Myanmar and Brunei. Maldivian (30 days) and Seychellois (15 days) ordinary passports are also exempt.
entries.note: 'Nearly everyone else needs the eVisa or a visa on arrival' is on no official page; the list is cited by name.

entries.old: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it, but cover is strongly recommended.
entries.new: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. No official source we read requires it of visa-exempt visitors.
entries.note: 'Cover is strongly recommended' is on no official page.

entries.old: Border officers may ask non-EU visitors for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation details.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says that at Danish border control you may need to show a return or onward ticket and prove that you have enough money for your stay.
entries.note: Attributed to the UK; 'accommodation details' is not in its text.

entries.old: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.
entries.new: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Your passport is not stamped; later crossings are quicker because your data is already recorded.
entries.note: The EU page says data can be registered in advance where self-service or an app is available, so 'nothing to submit in advance' was wrong; 'allow extra time' is advice.

entries.old: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.
entries.new: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Crime levels are generally low, but pickpockets and bag-snatchers operate in crowded areas, mainly in Copenhagen: the central station, Nørreport, Strøget, Nyhavn, Christiania and Kastrup Airport. Take extra care in Christiania and Nørrebro late at night. Cyclists often have the right of way, so check cycle lanes before crossing or turning.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says crime levels are generally low, but pickpockets and bag-snatchers operate in crowded areas, mainly in Copenhagen: the central station, Nørreport Station, Strøget, Christiania, Nyhavn and Kongens Nytorv. It advises extra care in Christiania and Nørrebro, particularly late at night, and says cyclists often have the right of way, so check cycle lanes before turning right.
entries.note: Kastrup Airport is not on the UK's list; text attributed to the UK.

entries.old: The 90-day visa-free limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Denmark — days spent in Sweden or Germany draw on the same allowance.
entries.new: For most visa-exempt nationals the 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, Greenland and the Faroe Islands combined. The Danish Immigration Service says citizens of Australia, Canada, Chile, Israel, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Korea and the US may stay in Denmark for 90 days or 3 months regardless of earlier stays in other Schengen countries.
entries.note: The Danish Immigration Service lists ten nationalities whose Denmark allowance runs regardless of other Schengen stays, so 'not just Denmark' was wrong for them.

entries.old: Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, apply only at the official travel-europe.europa.eu site — unofficial sites charge inflated fees for the €20 authorization.
entries.new: ETIAS will cost EUR 20; its official website is travel-europe.europa.eu.
entries.note: 'Unofficial sites charge inflated fees' is on no official page.

entries.old: ETIAS is the EU's travel authorization for visa-exempt visitors. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once mandatory, it will cost €20 (free for under-18s and over-70s) and be valid for 3 years. Check the official travel-europe.europa.eu site for the current status.
entries.new: ETIAS is the EU's travel authorization for visa-exempt visitors. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once mandatory, it will cost €20 (free for under-18s and over-70s) and be valid for 3 years.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Stays over 90 days require a residence permit for a specific purpose — work, study or family — applied for through nyidanmark.dk before travel. The Schengen short-stay allowance itself cannot normally be extended.
entries.new: Stays over 90 days require a residence permit for a specific purpose — work, study or family — applied for through nyidanmark.dk before travel.
entries.note: Hedged and unsourced.

entries.old: A Schengen short-stay visa is required. The EU suspended its visa facilitation agreement with Russia; fees are higher (€90) and processing is slower.
entries.new: A Schengen short-stay visa is required. The EU suspended its visa facilitation agreement with Russia; the standard €90 fee applies.
entries.note: 'Processing is slower' is on no official page.

entries.old: EU citizens can enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without a visa; register if staying over 3 months.
entries.new: EU citizens can enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without a visa.
entries.note: Not on a page read in this pass.

entries.old: Visa-free with a biometric passport: 90 days in any 180-day period. Temporary protection arrangements for those fleeing the war are separate.
entries.new: Visa-free with a biometric passport: 90 days in any 180-day period.
entries.note: Not on a page read in this pass.

entries.old: Djibouti requires nearly every foreign visitor to obtain an eVisa through the official government portal before travel — short-stay eVisas cover up to 14 days and standard ones up to 90 — as visas on arrival are no longer routinely issued.
entries.new: Djibouti's immigration directorate issues eVisas through its official portal, evisa.gouv.dj: a short-stay eVisa covers up to 14 days and a standard one up to 90. The eVisa portal says the eVisa replaces the visa issued at the point of entry; the UK Foreign Office says a tourist visa can still be bought on arrival, paid in cash in US dollars.
entries.note: 'Visas on arrival are no longer routinely issued' is not what either official source says: the portal says the eVisa replaces the visa at the point of entry, and the UK says a tourist visa can still be bought on arrival.

entries.old: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Djibouti.
entries.new: The eVisa portal asks for a passport valid for at least 6 months.
entries.note: The portal does not say 'on arrival'; it lists a passport valid at least 6 months among the application requirements.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers arriving from countries with a risk of yellow fever transmission — relevant if you arrive overland or via much of sub-Saharan Africa.
entries.new: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers arriving from countries with a risk of yellow fever transmission.
entries.note: Gloss removed.

entries.old: No official source we could find states whether travel insurance is required to enter Djibouti. Medical facilities are limited and evacuation is expensive, so cover with medical evacuation is worth having.
entries.new: No official source we could find states whether travel insurance is required to enter Djibouti.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: The UK advises against all travel to the Djibouti–Eritrea border. Elsewhere the main risk is petty crime, so keep valuables, particularly cameras and passports, out of sight, and avoid travelling outside city centres after dark.
entries.new: The UK advises against all travel to the Djibouti–Eritrea border, where there are unmarked landmines. It says there is a risk of petty crime and advises keeping valuables, particularly cameras and passports, out of sight, staying on paved roads and avoiding travel outside city centres after dark.
entries.note: 'Elsewhere the main risk is petty crime' is our ranking; the text now follows the UK's wording.

entries.old: Arrive with your eVisa approval already printed or saved. Visas on arrival have been largely phased out and airlines check for the eVisa at check-in.
entries.new: The eVisa portal says the eVisa replaces the visa issued at the point of entry, and that once approved it is downloaded as a PDF. The UK Foreign Office says a tourist visa can also be bought on arrival, paid in cash in US dollars.
entries.note: 'Largely phased out' and 'airlines check for the eVisa at check-in' are on no official page; the UK still describes a visa on arrival.

entries.old: Almost certainly yes — Djibouti requires nearly every foreign nationality to obtain an eVisa before travel through the official portal evisa.gouv.dj. A short-stay eVisa covers up to 14 days and a standard one up to 90 days.
entries.new: Yes. Djibouti issues eVisas before travel through the official portal evisa.gouv.dj. A short-stay eVisa covers up to 14 days and a standard one up to 90 days.
entries.note: Hedge removed.

entries.old: Do not plan on it. Djibouti has shifted visa issuance to the online eVisa system, and airlines generally require the approval before boarding. Apply on evisa.gouv.dj a few days before departure.
entries.new: The official sources differ. The eVisa portal says the eVisa replaces the visa issued at the point of entry, usually an airport or border crossing; the UK Foreign Office says you can buy a tourist visa when you arrive, paid in cash in US dollars, or apply online before travelling.
entries.note: 'Do not plan on it', 'airlines generally require the approval' and 'apply a few days before' are on no official page, and the UK states a visa on arrival is available.

entries.old: An eVisa obtained before travel on the official portal evisa.gouv.dj is required. A short-stay eVisa covers up to 14 days and the standard one up to 90; visas on arrival are no longer routinely issued.
entries.new: Apply for an eVisa before travel on the official portal evisa.gouv.dj: a short-stay eVisa covers up to 14 days and the standard one up to 90. The eVisa portal says the eVisa replaces the visa issued at the point of entry; the UK Foreign Office says a tourist visa can still be bought on arrival, paid in cash in US dollars.
entries.note: 'Visas on arrival are no longer routinely issued' replaced by what the portal and the UK each say.

entries.old: Insurance is not an entry condition. Canada's travel advice recommends insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays, and says you may have to pay cash immediately for medical treatment.
entries.new: No official source we could read makes insurance an entry condition. Canada's travel advice recommends insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays, and says you may have to pay cash immediately for medical treatment.
entries.note: The government's entry-requirements page does not list insurance; it does not say it is not required.

entries.old: Visitors must show a return or onward ticket and give the address where they are staying; the officer sets the length of stay from those details.
entries.new: The government lists a valid return ticket and a local address among the entry requirements for Dominica.
entries.note: 'The officer sets the length of stay from those details' is not on the page.

entries.old: Cash or travellers' cheques worth XCD 10,000 or more (roughly USD 3,700) must be declared to customs when you bring them in; you receive a certified declaration showing you brought the money with you.
entries.new: Cash or travellers' cheques worth XCD 10,000 or more must be declared to customs when you bring them in; you receive a certified declaration showing you brought the money with you.
entries.note: Unsourced currency conversion removed.

entries.old: Dominica is not the Dominican Republic. They are different countries with different entry rules, so check that flights, insurance and visas name the Commonwealth of Dominica before you book.
entries.new: (removed)
entries.note: 'Check that flights, insurance and visas name the Commonwealth of Dominica' is advice on no official page.

entries.old: No. Dominica is a small English-speaking island in the eastern Caribbean; the Dominican Republic is a much larger Spanish-speaking country sharing Hispaniola with Haiti. Their visa rules are completely separate. Make sure you are reading the right one.
entries.new: No. The Commonwealth of Dominica and the Dominican Republic are different countries with separate entry rules; this page covers the Commonwealth of Dominica.
entries.note: The geography and language descriptions and 'make sure you are reading the right one' are not from an official page.

entries.old: No official source we could read describes a remote-work visa for Dominica, so confirm with Dominica's immigration authorities before planning around one. A normal visitor stamp does not allow you to work locally.
entries.new: No official source we could read describes a remote-work visa for Dominica.
entries.note: The advice to confirm with immigration and 'a visitor stamp does not allow you to work' are on no official page we read.

entries.old: CARICOM nationals move freely within the community — visitors are normally granted a six-month stay on arrival, and skilled nationals with a CARICOM certificate may live and work.
entries.new: CARICOM nationals move freely within the community — visitors are normally granted a six-month stay on arrival.
entries.note: Not stated on the government pages.

entries.old: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Guinea-Bissau.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Guinea-Bissau.
entries.note: Now attributed to the UK, the only official page that states it.

entries.old: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required to enter Guinea-Bissau.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Guinea-Bissau.
entries.note: Now attributed to the UK.

entries.old: Yes. You must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Guinea-Bissau.
entries.new: Yes, according to the UK Foreign Office: you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Guinea-Bissau.

entries.old: Guinea-Bissau suffers from political instability. Avoid demonstrations, large gatherings and sensitive areas such as military installations and government buildings. Pickpocketing and bag and phone snatching are relatively common in Bissau, and landmines remain a risk outside the capital, so stay on paved roads there.
entries.new: The UK says Guinea-Bissau suffers from political instability and advises avoiding sensitive areas such as military installations and government buildings. It says pickpocketing and bag and phone snatching are relatively common in Bissau, and that landmines remain a risk in parts of the country: outside Bissau, take local advice and stay on paved roads.
entries.note: 'Avoid demonstrations, large gatherings' is not in the UK text quoted; the rest is now attributed.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says the Bijagós Islands are reached by chartered air services or by boat, that tour operators organise boat trips, and that pirogues should be avoided because they are unsafe. Build slack into your itinerary.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says the Bijagós Islands are reached by chartered air services or by boat, that tour operators organise boat trips, and that pirogues should be avoided because they are unsafe.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Bring the cash you need: the UK government says credit cards are rarely used and there are not many ATMs, and Canada says there are none. Canada also says local currency may not be imported or exported, while foreign currency must be declared on arrival.
entries.new: The UK government says credit cards are rarely used and there are not many ATMs, and Canada says there are none. Canada also says local currency may not be imported or exported, while foreign currency must be declared on arrival.
entries.note: Inferred advice removed.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says to exercise a high degree of caution because of high crime rates and weak state infrastructure, and that the army seized power on 26 November 2025. Petty crime is common at the airport, in markets and at public gatherings, and demonstrations can turn violent. Check your government's travel advice before booking.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says to exercise a high degree of caution because of high crime rates and weak state infrastructure, that the army seized power on 26 November 2025, that petty crime, including pickpocketing, is common at the airport, in markets and at public gatherings, and that even peaceful demonstrations can turn violent.
entries.note: 'Check your government's advice' removed; the petty-crime and demonstration sentences are now attributed to Canada, which states them.

entries.old: Effectively no. The UK government says Guinea-Bissau is a cash-based economy where credit cards are rarely used and there are not many ATMs, and Canada says there are no ATMs at all. Bring the cash you need and declare foreign currency on arrival.
entries.new: The UK government says Guinea-Bissau is a cash-based economy where credit cards are rarely used and there are not many ATMs, and Canada says there are no ATMs at all. Canada also says foreign currency must be declared on arrival.
entries.note: 'Effectively no' and 'bring the cash you need' are our words, not a source's.

entries.old: India runs one of the world's largest eVisa programs: citizens of around 170 countries can apply online for tourist eVisas valid 30 days, 1 year or 5 years, starting at 25 USD. Applications go exclusively through the official indianvisaonline.gov.in portal.
entries.new: Citizens of the 175 countries and territories on India's e-Visa list can apply online for tourist eVisas valid 30 days, 1 year or 5 years, starting at 25 USD. The e-Visa portal's FAQ says indianvisaonline.gov.in is the only official website to apply.
entries.note: 'One of the world's largest eVisa programs' is on no official page; 'around 170' corrected to the 175 entries of the portal's eligibility list.

entries.old: Reduced to 10 USD for applications between April and June. Fees differ for some nationalities, and some pay nothing. The portal shows your exact fee.
entries.new: 10 USD from April to June, according to the portal's fee table. Fees differ for some nationalities, and some pay nothing. A bank charge of 3% is added to the fee.
entries.note: The table's column is 'April to June', not 'applications between April and June'; 'the portal shows your exact fee' replaced by what the table states (3% bank charge).

entries.old: Multiple entry, valid for one year (365 days) from the date of arrival, for treatment at recognized Indian hospitals; up to two e-Medical Attendant visas per patient. Like every e-Visa it cannot be extended or converted. The portal's FAQ still gives 60 days from first arrival, beside the older e-Conference category.
entries.new: The e-Visa instructions give the e-Medical Visa multiple entries and one year (365 days) from the date of arrival; up to two e-Medical Attendant visas are granted per e-Medical Visa. Like every e-Visa it cannot be extended or converted. The portal's FAQ still gives 60 days from first arrival.
entries.note: 'At recognized Indian hospitals' and the e-Conference aside are not on the portal's pages.

entries.old: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival and have at least 2 blank pages. The e-Visa instructions put the six months at the time of applying, while the same page's FAQ and the UK Foreign Office count them from arrival — the stricter reading, used here.
entries.new: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months and have at least 2 blank pages. India's e-Visa instructions count the six months from the time of applying; the UK Foreign Office counts them from the date of arrival.
entries.note: The portal's FAQ (Q1) also counts six months at the time of application, not from arrival; 'the stricter reading, used here' removed.

entries.old: Travellers arriving by air or sea within 6 days of being in, or transiting through, a yellow fever endemic country (India notifies 30 in Africa and 13 in South America) must carry a valid yellow fever certificate (ICVP). Without one you can be quarantined for up to 6 days — India enforces this strictly. Infants under six months are exempt.
entries.new: Travellers arriving by air or sea from, or after transiting, a yellow fever endemic country (India notifies 30 in Africa and 13 in South America) must carry a valid yellow fever certificate (ICVP). Without one, the Bureau of Immigration says you will be kept in quarantine for up to 6 days. Infants below six months are excluded.
entries.note: 'India enforces this strictly' is on no official page; wording now follows the Bureau of Immigration's health-regulation page.

entries.old: You must have sufficient money to support yourself during the stay; no fixed amount is published, but immigration may ask.
entries.new: The e-Visa instructions say travellers should have sufficient money to spend during their stay in India. No official source we could read states an amount.
entries.note: 'Immigration may ask' is on no official page.

entries.old: eVisa holders must enter through one of the designated airports or seaports (all major international airports qualify); exit is allowed through any authorized immigration checkpoint.
entries.new: eVisa holders may enter only through the designated airports and seaports listed on the e-Visa portal (36 international airports on its checkpoint list); they may depart from any Indian immigration checkpoint.
entries.note: 'All major international airports qualify' is not what the portal says: entry is only through the listed airports and seaports.

entries.old: https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/india
entries.new: https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/india/entry-requirements
entries.note: The payments sentence quotes the UK, so the source now points at the UK page that states it.

entries.old: Most visits are trouble-free, but petty crime, traffic and scams around tourist sites warrant increased caution. Women travelers should take particular care, especially at night. The UK advises against all travel within 10 km of the Pakistan border and to Jammu and Kashmir (except travel by air to and within the city of Jammu), and against all but essential travel to Manipur.
entries.new: The UK warns that scammers, pickpockets and ticket touts target foreign nationals in tourist areas, and that female travellers often experience verbal and physical harassment. The UK advises against all travel within 10 km of the Pakistan border and to Jammu and Kashmir (except travel by air to and within the city of Jammu), and against all but essential travel to Manipur.
entries.note: 'Most visits are trouble-free' and 'traffic' are not on the UK page; the scam and harassment sentences now say what the UK says.

entries.old: Apply only at indianvisaonline.gov.in — look-alike sites charge large markups and some are outright scams.
entries.new: The e-Visa portal's FAQ says indianvisaonline.gov.in is the only official website for the e-Visa, and that no intermediary or travel agent is needed.
entries.note: 'Look-alike sites charge large markups and some are outright scams' is not on the portal.

entries.old: Carry a printed copy of your eVisa approval (ETA) — airlines and immigration ask for it.
entries.new: The e-Visa portal says to print your Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) and present it at the immigration checkpoint, where the eVisa is stamped in your passport.
entries.note: 'Airlines ask for it' is on no official page.

entries.old: The 30-day e-Tourist Visa has a standard fee of 25 USD (10 USD for April–June arrivals), the 1-year version 40 USD, and the 5-year version 200 USD. Fees differ for a few nationalities. The official portal shows your exact fee before payment.
entries.new: The 30-day e-Tourist Visa has a standard fee of 25 USD (10 USD from April to June), the 1-year version 40 USD, and the 5-year version 200 USD. Fees differ for a few nationalities, and a 3% bank charge is added; the portal's fee table lists each country's fee.

entries.old: Most eVisas are approved within 1–4 business days. Apply at least 4 days before your flight; you cannot use the eVisa scheme more than twice per calendar year for the 30-day version.
entries.new: No official source we could read states how long an eVisa takes to process. The portal says e-Tourist and e-Business applications may be made at least 4 days before arrival and up to 120 days ahead, and that the fee must be paid at least 4 days before travel.
entries.note: 'Most eVisas are approved within 1–4 business days' and the twice-a-year limit on the 30-day eVisa are not on the portal.

entries.old: Only conditionally: a yellow fever certificate if you arrive from a risk country (strictly enforced — quarantine applies without it), and a polio vaccination certificate if arriving from a polio-affected country. No vaccinations are required when flying directly from Europe, the Americas or most of Asia.
entries.new: Only conditionally: a yellow fever certificate if you arrive from or transit through a yellow fever endemic country (without one you can be quarantined for up to 6 days), and a polio vaccination certificate if arriving from a polio-affected country.
entries.note: 'Strictly enforced' is on no official page, and 'no vaccinations when flying from the Americas' was wrong: India lists 13 South American endemic countries.

entries.old: Tourist eVisas cannot be extended. For longer stays, use the 1-year or 5-year multiple-entry eVisa (max 90 days per visit for most nationalities) or a regular embassy visa.
entries.new: No. The e-Visa portal says e-Visas are non-extendable and non-convertible. The 1-year and 5-year e-Tourist Visas allow multiple entries, with a total stay of no more than 180 days in a calendar year.
entries.note: 'Max 90 days per visit for most nationalities' is not on the portal, which gives 180 days per calendar year.

entries.old: Not on the eVisa eligibility list. Apply for a regular visa through an Indian mission; confirm current eligibility on the official portal.
entries.new: Not on the eVisa eligibility list. Apply for a regular visa through an Indian mission.
entries.note: Advice to confirm eligibility removed.

entries.old: eVisa fees for US citizens differ from the standard tariff. Check the fee shown in the official portal for your nationality.
entries.new: Eligible for the Indian eVisa. The portal's fee table lists 25 USD for 30 days (10 USD from April to June), 40 USD for 1 year and 160 USD for 5 years for US citizens.
entries.note: Replaced 'check the fee in the portal' with the fees the portal's table states.

entries.old: eVisa fees for British citizens differ from the standard tariff. Check the fee shown in the official portal for your nationality.
entries.new: Eligible for the Indian eVisa. The portal's fee table lists 25 USD for 30 days (10 USD from April to June), 40 USD for 1 year and 484 USD for 5 years for UK citizens.
entries.note: Replaced 'check the fee in the portal' with the fees the portal's table states.

entries.old: Turkish citizens are not currently on the eVisa eligibility list and apply through the Indian mission. Confirm current eligibility on the official portal.
entries.new: Turkish citizens are not on the eVisa eligibility list and apply through an Indian mission.
entries.note: Advice to confirm eligibility removed.

entries.old: Nigerian citizens are not currently on the eVisa eligibility list and apply through the Indian mission. Confirm current eligibility on the official portal.
entries.new: Nigerian citizens are not on the eVisa eligibility list and apply through an Indian mission.
entries.note: Advice to confirm eligibility removed.

entries.old: Chinese citizens are not on the eVisa eligibility list. Tourist visas for them resumed in 2025 and are applied for through Indian missions; confirm current eligibility on the official portal.
entries.new: Chinese citizens are not on the eVisa eligibility list and apply through an Indian mission.
entries.note: 'Tourist visas resumed in 2025' and the advice to confirm eligibility are on no official page we read.

entries.old: Pakistani citizens are not eligible for eVisa; visas are issued restrictively through Indian missions and processing can take months.
entries.new: Pakistani citizens, and foreigners of Pakistani origin, are not eligible for the eVisa; the portal says they may apply for a regular visa at an Indian mission.
entries.note: 'Issued restrictively' and 'processing can take months' are on no official page we read.

entries.old: No visa needed: under the 1950 India–Nepal treaty the border is open, and Nepali citizens may enter, live and work in India with an accepted identity document. No stay limit.
entries.new: No visa needed: the Bureau of Immigration says citizens of Nepal arriving from Nepal by land or air need neither a passport nor an Indian visa, only a government-approved identity document with a photograph. Arriving from a third country they need a passport, and from China, Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan a passport and an Indian visa.
entries.note: 'Live and work', 'no stay limit' and the 1950 treaty are not on the Bureau of Immigration page, which the row now cites.

entries.old: No visa needed: under the India–Bhutan friendship arrangements the border is open, and Bhutanese citizens may enter, live and work in India with an accepted identity document. No stay limit.
entries.new: No visa needed: the Bureau of Immigration says citizens of Bhutan arriving from Bhutan by land or air need neither a passport nor an Indian visa, only a government-approved identity document with a photograph. Arriving from a third country they need a passport, and from China, Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan a passport and an Indian visa.
entries.note: 'Live and work', 'no stay limit' and the 1950 treaty are not on the Bureau of Immigration page, which the row now cites.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days under the India–Maldives bilateral agreement.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days for business, medical treatment or tourism; the Bureau of Immigration counts all stays in India in the 6 months before arrival toward the 90 days.
entries.note: The Bureau of Immigration page states the 90 days and its conditions; 'bilateral agreement' is not on it.

entries.old: Paid online when you apply. The UK FCDO gives the fee as USD 160 and says the visa is valid for 60 days; Iraq's own e-Visa portal (evisa.iq) says it is valid for 30 days and can be single or multiple entry. We show the shorter 30 days. Apply at least 24 hours before you travel (FCDO).
entries.new: Paid online when you apply. The UK FCDO gives the fee as USD 160 and says the visa is valid for 60 days; Iraq's own e-Visa portal (evisa.iq) says it is valid for 30 days and can be single or multiple entry. Apply at least 24 hours before you travel (FCDO).
entries.note: 'We show the shorter 30 days' is an editorial choice, not a source; both figures stay attributed.

entries.old: The FCDO advises against all travel to large parts of Iraq — including Kirkuk, Ninawa and Salah al-Din provinces, western Anbar and Sadr City — and against all but essential travel to the rest, including Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region. It reports Iranian strikes in Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region, since 8 July 2026. Terrorism, kidnapping and sudden unrest remain real risks; if you go, travel with an experienced local operator.
entries.new: The FCDO advises against all travel to large parts of Iraq — including Kirkuk, Ninawa and Salah al-Din provinces, western Anbar and Sadr City — and against all but essential travel to the rest, including Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region. It reports Iranian strikes in Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region, since 8 July 2026. It says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Iraq and that there is a high threat of kidnapping throughout the country.
entries.note: 'Travel with an experienced local operator' is not on the UK page; the terrorism and kidnap sentence now says what the UK says.

entries.old: The Kurdistan Region (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah) issues its own e-Visa, online or on arrival for citizens on its Country List A, but it is valid in the Kurdistan Region ONLY. Canada's travel advice says travel to other regions of Iraq needs a separate Iraqi visa; decide which you need before you fly.
entries.new: The Kurdistan Region (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah) issues its own e-Visa, online or on arrival for citizens on its Country List A, but it is valid in the Kurdistan Region ONLY. Canada's travel advice says travel to other regions of Iraq needs a separate Iraqi visa.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says Iraq's economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs that accept international cards are hard to find, so bring enough cash; Australia's Smartraveller says US dollars and euros are the easiest to exchange. The e-Visa itself is paid online when you apply.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says Iraq's economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs that accept international cards are hard to find; Australia's Smartraveller says US dollars and euros are the easiest to exchange. The e-Visa itself is paid online when you apply.
entries.note: 'So bring enough cash' is our inference, not Canada's advice.

entries.old: No. Canada and Australia advise against all travel to Iraq, and the UK advises against all travel to large parts of the country, including Kirkuk, Ninawa and Salah al-Din provinces, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest. Missile, drone and rocket attacks have struck locations in Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region. Check your government's advice before considering a trip.
entries.new: No. Canada and Australia advise against all travel to Iraq, and the UK advises against all travel to large parts of the country, including Kirkuk, Ninawa and Salah al-Din provinces, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest. Missile, drone and rocket attacks have struck locations in Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Apply online for Iraq's e-Visa before you travel: the Interior Ministry's e-Visa portal lists Gulf Cooperation Council citizens among the 44 nationalities that can apply directly (USD 160; valid 30 days per Iraq's portal). GCC citizens were in the past issued visas on arrival; Iraq does not say whether that still applies. A Kurdistan Region visa is valid in the Kurdistan Region only.
entries.new: Apply online for Iraq's e-Visa before you travel: the Interior Ministry's e-Visa portal lists Gulf Cooperation Council citizens among the 44 nationalities that can apply directly (USD 160; valid 30 days per Iraq's portal). A Kurdistan Region visa is valid in the Kurdistan Region only.
entries.note: The past visa-on-arrival practice is on no official page we read.

entries.new: null
entries.note: PICA's visa-requirements table lists these Commonwealth nationalities as 'NO visa required' with no period (unlike the 30/90-day entries it gives others); no official page we read gives 90 days for them. Same treatment as the existing BD and MZ rows.

entries.old: Commonwealth citizens are admitted visa-free for up to 90 days; the free C5 immigration and customs form, online or on paper, is still mandatory.
entries.new: No visa is needed, per PICA's visa-requirements table, which does not state a period; the Immigration Officer decides the length of stay on arrival. The C5 immigration and customs form, online or on paper, is still mandatory.
entries.note: 'Up to 90 days' is not in PICA's table for these Commonwealth nationalities.

entries.new: null
entries.note: PICA's table gives these Commonwealth members 'NO visa required' with no period; Australia's Smartraveller says Australians need no visa for tourist stays of less than 6 months, which contradicts 90.

entries.old: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days; every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.
entries.new: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days, per PICA's visa-requirements table; every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.

entries.old: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days; every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.

entries.old: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days; every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.
entries.new: No visa is needed, per PICA's visa-requirements table, which does not state a period; Australia's Smartraveller says Australians need no visa for tourist stays of less than 6 months. Every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form.

entries.old: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days; every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.
entries.new: Visa-free; Canada's travel advice says tourists need no visa for stays of up to 90 days. Every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.

entries.old: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days; every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.
entries.new: Visa-free; the UK Foreign Office says you will usually be granted entry for up to 90 days. Every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.

entries.old: A visitor's visa must be obtained from a Jamaican mission or honorary consulate before traveling. There is no visa on arrival and no eVisa.
entries.new: A visitor's visa must be obtained from a Jamaican mission or honorary consulate before traveling.
entries.note: Not stated on PICA's table or the embassy page.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 30 days under the mutual visa-exemption agreement signed with China. Confirm the current terms with a Jamaican mission before booking.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 30 days, for tourism only, per PICA's visa-requirements table.
entries.note: The 'mutual visa-exemption agreement' and the advice to confirm are not on PICA's table, which says tourism only.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days under a bilateral waiver. Confirm the current allowance with a Jamaican mission before a long stay.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism, business and cultural exchanges, per PICA's visa-requirements table.
entries.note: 'Bilateral waiver' and the advice to confirm are not on PICA's table.

entries.old: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days under Jamaica's waiver for Latin American passports; complete the online C5 form before departure.
entries.new: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days per PICA's visa-requirements table; complete the online C5 form before departure.
entries.note: No 'waiver for Latin American passports' is named on PICA's table.

entries.old: Jamaica requires a passport valid for the whole of your intended stay rather than a fixed six months. Airlines and many home governments still advise six months' validity, so travel with six months where you can.
entries.new: Jamaica's Embassy in Washington says your travel document should have at least six months' validity. The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay and have 2 blank pages for entry and exit stamps.
entries.note: Jamaica's own embassy (rank 3) says six months' validity, so 'rather than a fixed six months' was wrong; the airline advice is on no official page. Rule set to 6 months; the UK page is kept as the conflict.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you are arriving from, or have recently transited, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — mainly parts of tropical Africa and South America, and also Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean. Travelers coming directly from Europe or North America do not need one to enter Jamaica.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.
entries.note: The list of regions and 'travellers from Europe or North America do not need one' are not on the UK page.

entries.old: All arriving passengers must present a completed and signed Immigration/Customs C5 form, either filled in online before travel or on paper. It is free, so any site charging a fee for a Jamaican "travel authorization" is not official — if you are unsure, check with your airline or PICA.
entries.new: PICA says all arriving travellers must present a completed and signed Immigration/Customs C5 form, either online or a physical form. The UK Foreign Office says to complete it online where possible before you arrive.
entries.note: The 'travel authorization' warning and 'check with your airline' are on no official page.

entries.old: Crime and homicide rates in Jamaica are high, but gang violence and shootings mostly occur in inner-city areas, including parts of Kingston, Spanish Town and Montego Bay, and tourist areas are not usually affected. Most attacks on tourists are robberies. Hotels and resorts are generally well guarded, and some visitors have been followed and robbed on the way from the airport to private accommodation.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says crime and homicide rates in Jamaica are high, but gang violence and shootings mostly occur in inner-city areas and tourist areas are not usually affected; it advises particular caution in Kingston, Spanish Town, Savanna-la-Mar and parts of Montego Bay. It says the motive for most attacks on tourists is robbery, most hotels and resorts are well guarded, and British nationals have been tracked and robbed travelling from the airport to private accommodation.
entries.note: Now attributed to the UK, which states it; the areas follow the UK's list.

entries.old: Complete the free Immigration/Customs C5 form at enterjamaica.gov.jm before you fly and save the QR code. Sites charging a fee for a "Jamaica travel authorization" are not official — that authorization was discontinued after the pandemic and no longer exists.
entries.new: Complete the Immigration/Customs C5 form at enterjamaica.gov.jm, the C5 portal run by PICA and Jamaica Customs; the UK Foreign Office says to complete it online where possible before you arrive.
entries.note: 'Save the QR code' and the discontinued 'travel authorization' are on no official page we read.

entries.old: The Government of Canada says entering Jamaica with a firearm or even a single round of ammunition is a serious crime. Empty and check every bag before you travel.
entries.new: The Government of Canada says entering Jamaica with a firearm or even a single round of ammunition is a serious crime.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says smoking marijuana is illegal in Jamaica, with a fine for possessing up to 2 ounces and severe penalties for attempting to export narcotics. The Government of Canada says departing visitors are thoroughly screened for drugs. Do not attempt to leave with any.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says smoking marijuana is illegal in Jamaica, with a fine for possessing up to 2 ounces and severe penalties for attempting to export narcotics. The Government of Canada says departing visitors are thoroughly screened for drugs.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says arrival and departure taxes are usually included in the cost of your ticket; if unsure, check with your carrier.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says arrival and departure taxes are usually included in the cost of your ticket, and that your carrier can advise you if you are unsure.

entries.old: Probably not. Jamaica is visa-free for citizens of the US, Canada, the UK, most EU and Schengen countries, Japan, South Korea, much of Latin America and most Commonwealth countries, and CARICOM nationals get six months. The period depends on the passport: PICA's table gives six months to US citizens, 90 days to, among others, Germany, the Netherlands, the Nordic countries, Brazil, Mexico and South Korea, and 30 days to France, Spain, Portugal, Japan and most of Latin America. Some nationalities, such as Armenia, Georgia and Uzbekistan, can get a visa at the port of entry for US$100; others need a visitor's visa from a Jamaican high commission or embassy before traveling. There is no eVisa.

The officer writes the actual period on your stamp and may grant less if your return ticket is sooner. Extensions are handled by PICA and must be applied for before your stamp expires; a visitor may stay at most 12 months in total as a Commonwealth citizen, or 6 months otherwise.

entries.old: The Maldives grants a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival to every nationality except Israeli passport holders, who are barred from entry, provided you have a confirmed hotel booking, sufficient funds and an onward ticket. Every traveler must also submit the free Imuga Traveller Declaration online within 96 hours before arrival, and the stay can be extended in-country through the Imuga portal.
entries.new: Maldives Immigration grants tourists a visa on arrival without pre-approval, provided they have confirmed return tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking and sufficient funds; since 15 April 2025 entry is not granted on Israeli passports. The UK and Canada say the visa is for 30 days, and Australia says it is free. Every traveller must also submit the free Imuga Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before arrival, and the stay can be extended in-country through the Imuga portal.
entries.note: Maldives Immigration's page states neither the 30 days nor that the visa is free; both are now attributed to the governments that state them (UK and Canada; Australia).

entries.old: Free of charge for every nationality admitted (Israeli passport holders are barred). Granted at the border for up to 30 days, subject to a confirmed accommodation booking, sufficient funds and an onward or return ticket.
entries.new: Australia's Smartraveller says the tourist visa on arrival is free; the UK Foreign Office and Canada say it is granted for 30 days. Maldives Immigration lists the conditions: confirmed return tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility and sufficient funds, or a sponsorship it has approved. Entry is not granted on Israeli passports.
entries.note: Free and 30 days now attributed; the conditions are Maldives Immigration's wording.

entries.old: Your passport (or travel document) must be machine-readable and valid for at least 1 month on arrival, according to Maldives Immigration; the UK Foreign Office gives the same 1-month rule. Canada's travel advice asks for 6 months from your date of entry, so check with your airline.
entries.new: Your passport (or travel document) must be machine-readable and valid for at least 1 month on arrival, according to Maldives Immigration; the UK Foreign Office gives the same 1-month rule. Canada's travel advice asks for 6 months from your date of entry.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: A confirmed onward or return ticket is one of the conditions of the visa on arrival — airlines and immigration officers check it.
entries.new: Confirmed return journey tickets are one of the entry requirements Maldives Immigration lists for tourists.
entries.note: 'Airlines and immigration officers check it' is on no official page.

entries.old: The Imuga Traveller Declaration is free at imuga.immigration.gov.mv and must be submitted within 96 hours before your flight for arrival; the Imuga home page lists departure too. Ignore third-party sites that charge for it.
entries.new: The Imuga Traveller Declaration is free at imuga.immigration.gov.mv and must be submitted within 96 hours before your flight for arrival; the Imuga home page lists departure too. Maldives Immigration advises against other websites that may charge a fee.

entries.old: No advance visa for any passport that is admitted. Every nationality except Israel receives a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival — Israeli passport holders are barred from entry — provided you have a confirmed accommodation booking, means to cover your stay, an onward or return ticket and a submitted Imuga declaration.
entries.new: No advance visa: Maldives Immigration grants tourists a visa on arrival without pre-approval, provided you have confirmed return tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking, sufficient funds and a submitted Imuga declaration. Entry is not granted on Israeli passports. The UK and Canada say the visa is for 30 days; Australia says it is free.

entries.old: Free 30-day tourist visa granted on arrival. You need a confirmed booking, funds for your stay, an onward ticket and the Imuga declaration submitted within 96 hours before arrival.
entries.new: Tourist visa granted on arrival without pre-approval (30 days according to the UK and Canada; free according to Australia). You need confirmed return tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking, sufficient funds and the Imuga declaration submitted within 96 hours before arrival.
entries.note: Free and 30 days are not on Maldives Immigration's page; now attributed.

entries.old: Israeli passport holders are barred from entering the Maldives under the entry ban announced in 2024 and signed into law in 2025. The ban applies to travel on an Israeli passport — dual nationals may be able to enter on another passport.
entries.new: Maldives Immigration says that from 15 April 2025 entry to the Maldives is not granted on Israeli passports.
entries.note: 'Announced in 2024 and signed into law in 2025' and 'dual nationals may be able to enter on another passport' are on no official page we read.

entries.old: For stays over 90 days: work, study and other long-stay purposes, usually alongside a residence-permit application. Confirm the current fee and requirements with Identità or the Maltese mission before applying.
entries.new: For stays over 90 days, for work, study and other long-stay purposes. Identità's Central Visa Unit charges its fees under Fee Ordinance L.N. 287 of 2020.
entries.note: 'Usually alongside a residence-permit application' and the advice to confirm are removed; the fee page cites L.N. 287 of 2020.

entries.old: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it but border officers may ask about cover.
entries.new: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. No official source we read requires it of visa-exempt visitors.
entries.note: 'Border officers may ask about cover' is on no official page.

entries.old: Border officers may ask non-EU visitors for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation details.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says that at Maltese border control you may need to show a return or onward ticket.
entries.note: Attributed to the UK; 'accommodation details' is not in its text.

entries.old: Malta's commonly used reference is around €48 per person per day for the stay; border officers assess sufficiency case by case alongside accommodation and return bookings. Confirm the current guideline with the Maltese authorities.
entries.new: The European Commission's table of reference amounts set by national authorities lists EUR 48 per person per day for Malta.
entries.note: 'Commonly used… around', 'case by case alongside bookings' and the advice to confirm are removed; the Commission's table states EUR 48.

entries.old: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.
entries.new: Non-EU travellers are registered biometrically (photo and/or fingerprints) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders, and their passports are no longer stamped. Later crossings are quicker because the data is already recorded.
entries.note: The EU page allows some data to be registered in advance where self-service or an app exists; 'allow extra time' is advice.

entries.old: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.
entries.new: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Malta is very safe with low violent crime. Watch for pickpocketing in Valletta and on crowded buses, and take the usual care in the Paceville nightlife district late at night.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says crime against tourists is rare, but there have been incidents including pickpocketing, notably on crowded buses between Valletta and St Julian's in summer, and that criminals have drugged people in some bars and gentlemen's clubs in the Paceville district.
entries.note: 'Very safe' is not the UK's wording; the pickpocketing and Paceville warnings now say what the UK says.

entries.old: Traffic drives on the left. The Government of Canada describes Malta's roads as narrow, winding, congested and sometimes poorly maintained, and the UK Foreign Office says local driving standards are poor — as a pedestrian, look right first.
entries.new: Traffic drives on the left. The Government of Canada describes Malta's roads as narrow, winding, congested and sometimes poorly maintained, and the UK Foreign Office says local driving standards are poor.
entries.note: 'Look right first' is not on the UK or Canadian page.

entries.old: Apply for ETIAS only at the official travel-europe.europa.eu site once it becomes mandatory.
entries.new: The official ETIAS website is travel-europe.europa.eu; the EU says ETIAS is not yet in operation.
entries.note: Advice restated as the official page states it.

entries.old: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11, allowing up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries. National long-stay (Type D) visas cost around €100. Confirm with the Maltese mission.
entries.new: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11, allowing up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries. A national long-stay (Type D) visa costs €100.
entries.note: Hedge and advice removed; the figure follows the visa type's fee field.

entries.old: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers across the Schengen Area is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once mandatory, the €20 online authorization will be required before boarding. Check the official EU website for the current status.
entries.new: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers across the Schengen Area is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The EU gives the application fee as €20.
entries.note: 'Required before boarding' and the advice are not on the EU page.

entries.old: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area, so time spent in Italy or any other Schengen country counts toward the same limit. EU and EFTA citizens can stay indefinitely but should register if settling for more than 3 months.
entries.new: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area, so time spent in Italy or any other Schengen country counts toward the same limit.
entries.note: Not on a page read in this pass.

entries.old: A Schengen short-stay visa is required. The EU suspended its visa facilitation agreement with Russia; fees are higher (€90) and processing is slower.
entries.new: A Schengen short-stay visa is required. The EU suspended its visa facilitation agreement with Russia; the standard €90 fee applies.
entries.note: 'Processing is slower' is on no official page.

entries.old: EU citizens can enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without a visa; register if staying over 3 months.
entries.new: EU citizens can enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without a visa.
entries.note: Not on a page read in this pass.

entries.old: Visa-free with a biometric passport: 90 days in any 180-day period. Temporary protection arrangements for those fleeing the war are separate.
entries.new: Visa-free with a biometric passport: 90 days in any 180-day period.
entries.note: Not on a page read in this pass.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Andorran citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. Andorran citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. EU citizens can also enter with a national ID card for short stays of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. EU citizens can also enter with a national ID card for short stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Icelandic citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. Icelandic citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.
