entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. Liechtenstein citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Monegasque citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. Monegasque citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Norwegian citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. Norwegian citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. San Marino citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. San Marino citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Swiss citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. Swiss citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Holy See citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days. Holy See citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card for stays of up to 30 days.
entries.note: The Decree on Visa Regime gives 'up to 90 days' without a 180-day reference period; the 90/180 rule on the MFA page is for visa C.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days; the UK Foreign Office says up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
entries.note: 180-day period attributed to the UK, which states it.

entries.old: Your passport must be valid for at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave Montenegro and have been issued less than 10 years before you enter. If you need a visa, the passport must be valid at least 3 months beyond the visa's validity.
entries.new: Montenegro's foreign ministry says a foreign travel document is valid for entry if it was issued within the last ten years and will not expire until at least three months after your planned departure from Montenegro. If you need a visa, the passport must be valid at least three months longer than the visa.
entries.note: Montenegro's own foreign ministry page states the rule; the field now cites it instead of the UK page.

entries.old: Not a condition of entry for visa-free visitors, though visa applicants must show travel health insurance for the stay. EU EHIC cards are not valid in Montenegro, so private cover is strongly recommended.
entries.new: Not a condition of entry for visa-free visitors, though visa applicants must show travel health insurance for the stay.
entries.note: EHIC claim and the recommendation are on no official page we read.

entries.old: Montenegro is generally safe for visitors, with low violent crime against tourists. Watch for pickpocketing and car break-ins at busy coastal resorts in summer, and take care on narrow mountain roads.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office advises being wary of pickpockets in tourist hot spots, beaches, airports and on public transport and not leaving luggage in a parked vehicle. It says incidents of violent crime between organised criminal groups can affect others close by, and that hikers have got lost in the mountains after leaving marked paths.
entries.note: 'Generally safe', 'low violent crime against tourists', 'car break-ins at coastal resorts in summer' and 'narrow mountain roads' are not on the UK page.

entries.old: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors must register with the local tourism office or police within 24 hours of arrival, and that you may be fined, detained or face a court appearance if you do not. If you stay in private accommodation, check that your host has done it.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors must register with the local tourism office or police within 24 hours of arrival, and that you may be fined, detained or face a court appearance if you do not. If you stay in private accommodation, the UK says to make sure you complete the registration yourself.
entries.note: The UK says to complete it yourself in private accommodation, not to check the host did it.

entries.old: Montenegro uses the euro although it is not an EU member: the European Central Bank lists it among the countries that use the euro without a formal arrangement. No currency exchange is needed if you arrive from the euro area.
entries.new: Montenegro uses the euro although it is not an EU member: the European Central Bank lists it among the countries that use the euro without a formal arrangement.
entries.note: Inference removed.

entries.old: US passport holders can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so this allowance is separate from your Schengen 90/180 days.
entries.new: US passport holders can stay up to 90 days without a visa, under Montenegro's Decree on Visa Regime.
entries.note: 'In any 180-day period' and the Schengen comparison are not on the decree or MFA page.

entries.old: Not until 31 October 2026: Russian citizens can enter visa-free for up to 30 days until then. From 1 November 2026, as Montenegro aligns its visa policy with the EU's, they need a visa, which can be applied for at VFS Global visa application centres, including in Russia.
entries.new: Not until 31 October 2026: Montenegro's Decree on Visa Regime lets Russian citizens enter visa-free for up to 30 days until then. After that date the exemption lapses and a visa is required.
entries.note: 'As Montenegro aligns its visa policy with the EU's' and the VFS Global centres are on no official page we read.

entries.old: Yes — EU citizens can enter with a national ID card for short stays of up to 30 days, and citizens of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Serbia can use their ID card for up to 90 days under the Western Balkans freedom-of-movement agreement. For a full 90-day stay as an EU citizen, or to be safe at all crossings, carry a passport.
entries.new: Yes — EU citizens can enter with a national ID card for short stays of up to 30 days, and citizens of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Serbia can use their ID card for up to 90 days under the Western Balkans freedom-of-movement agreement. With a passport, EU citizens can stay up to 90 days.
entries.note: 'To be safe at all crossings' removed; the MFA gives 30 days on an ID card, 90 on a passport.

entries.old: Your passport should be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned stay in North Macedonia. Keep a comfortable margin and confirm with the embassy if your passport is close to expiry.
entries.new: Your passport should be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned stay in North Macedonia.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: Not a condition of entry for visa-free visitors, though visa applicants must show travel health insurance. EU EHIC cards are not valid in North Macedonia, so private cover is strongly recommended.
entries.new: Visa applicants must show adequate travel medical insurance. No official source we read makes insurance a condition of entry for visa-free visitors.
entries.note: The EHIC claim and 'private cover is strongly recommended' are on no official page we read.

entries.old: Non-residents must declare foreign cash and cheques worth €10,000 or more on entry; smaller sums can be declared voluntarily. On departure a non-resident may not take out more foreign cash than was declared on entry, so declare any sizeable amount when you arrive.
entries.new: Non-residents must declare foreign cash and cheques worth €10,000 or more on entry; smaller sums can be declared voluntarily. On departure a non-resident may not take out more foreign cash than was declared on entry.
entries.note: Inferred advice removed.

entries.old: Carry denars in cash: Canada says the economy is mostly cash-based and cards are accepted only in some larger establishments. Change money only at banks or official exchanges, not with street dealers (UK government).
entries.new: Canada says the economy is mostly cash-based and cards are accepted only in some larger establishments. The UK government says to change money only through banks or official exchanges, not through street dealers.
entries.note: 'Carry denars in cash' is our inference.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says smoke haze and air pollution can be extremely hazardous, usually worst in winter because of coal and wood heating, and Australia's Smartraveller names Skopje. Travellers with breathing conditions should check air-quality levels.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says smoke haze and air pollution can be extremely hazardous, usually worst in winter because of coal and wood heating, and Australia's Smartraveller names Skopje. It advises talking to your doctor before you travel if you have a breathing condition.
entries.note: Smartraveller's advice is to talk to a doctor, not to check air-quality levels.

entries.old: Yes — holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen (type C) visa can enter without a North Macedonian visa and stay up to 15 days per visit, provided the Schengen visa remains valid at least five days beyond the stay. Confirm the current terms with an embassy before travel.
entries.new: Yes — holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen (type C) visa can enter without a North Macedonian visa and stay up to 15 days per visit, provided the Schengen visa remains valid at least five days beyond the stay.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: US passport holders can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. North Macedonia is outside the Schengen Area, so this does not use up any of your Schengen days.
entries.new: US passport holders can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa.
entries.note: Not on a page read in this pass.

entries.old: The Macedonian denar (MKD). Canada's travel advice says the economy is mostly cash-based, with credit cards accepted in some larger establishments and ATMs in urban centres, so carry denar cash. Australia's Smartraveller says the denar cannot be changed outside North Macedonia.
entries.new: The Macedonian denar (MKD). Canada's travel advice says the economy is mostly cash-based, with credit cards accepted in some larger establishments and ATMs in urban centres. Australia's Smartraveller says the denar cannot be changed outside North Macedonia.
entries.note: Inferred advice removed.

entries.old: EU citizens can enter with a valid biometric national ID card for short visits of up to 15 days; for longer stays (up to the full 90 days) travel with a passport.
entries.new: Yes. The Foreign Ministry says nationals of EU member states and Schengen signatories do not need a visa and may enter with a valid national identity card.
entries.note: The 15-day limit on ID-card entry and the passport advice are not on the ministry's page.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. EU citizens can also enter with a biometric national ID card for visits of up to 15 days.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. EU citizens can also enter with a valid national ID card.
entries.note: The 15-day ID-card limit is not on the ministry's page.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 90 days — neighboring Western Balkan citizens can also enter with a national ID card for short stays.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 90 days.
entries.note: Not on a page read in this pass.

entries.old: Samoa is one of the most open countries in the world: visitors of every nationality are issued a free 90-day entry permit on arrival, with no visa and no online authorization to arrange, provided you hold onward travel and somewhere to stay.
entries.new: Samoa Immigration says visitors can apply on arrival, using the arrival card, for a 90-day Visitor Permit, provided they hold a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the stay, confirmed onward tickets, visas for their next destination, sufficient funds and a confirmed address in Samoa. The UK government says the permit is free.
entries.note: 'One of the most open countries in the world' is not an official statement; 'free' is the UK's word, now attributed.

entries.old: Samoa's Ministry of Health has no active travel advisories or health-related travel restrictions in place, and it publishes no measles vaccination requirement for visitors. After the 2019 measles epidemic, being up to date with MMR vaccination is sensible.
entries.new: Samoa's Ministry of Health has no active travel advisories or health-related travel restrictions in place, and it publishes no measles vaccination requirement for visitors.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: The free 90-day entry permit is granted only if you have a return or onward ticket, a passport valid at least 6 months after you leave Samoa, and a visa or permit for the country you travel on to.
entries.new: Samoa Immigration grants the 90-day Visitor Permit only to travellers with confirmed onward or return tickets, a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the intended stay, and visas for their next country of destination.
entries.note: 'Free' is not on Samoa Immigration's page; the conditions follow its wording.

entries.old: A paper arrival card and a combined customs, biosecurity and health declaration are handed out on the inbound flight. Declare all food, plant and animal products — quarantine officers inspect bags and fines apply for undeclared items.
entries.new: Samoa Immigration says arrival and declaration cards are provided by the airline or shipping agent, or by immigration officers at the arrival booths. The UK government says you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
entries.note: 'Handed out on the inbound flight', 'combined customs, biosecurity and health declaration' and 'quarantine officers inspect bags and fines apply' are not on the pages read.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says the level of serious crime is low and petty theft is uncommon and opportunistic. Tides can produce powerful currents in lagoons and waves break directly onto reefs, so take local advice before swimming or surfing. Stray dogs are common in Apia and many villages, and roads are poorly lit at night.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says the level of serious crime is low and petty theft is uncommon and opportunistic. It says tides can produce powerful currents in lagoons and waves break directly onto reefs, so take local advice before swimming or surfing, and that stray dogs are common in Apia and many villages.
entries.note: 'Roads are poorly lit at night' is not on the UK page.

entries.old: Canada's travel advice says ATMs are mostly in and around Apia, with one on Savai'i and none elsewhere, so carry enough tālā before leaving Apia.
entries.new: Canada's travel advice says ATMs are mostly in and around Apia, with one on Savai'i and none elsewhere.
entries.note: Inferred advice removed.

entries.old: No. Samoa gives citizens of every country a free visitor entry permit on arrival, valid for up to 90 days. There is nothing to apply for in advance — just arrive with a passport valid six months, a confirmed onward ticket and details of where you are staying.
entries.new: No. Samoa Immigration says visitors can apply on arrival, using the arrival card, for a 90-day Visitor Permit; they need a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the stay, confirmed onward tickets, visas for their next destination, sufficient funds and a confirmed address in Samoa. The UK government says the permit is free.
entries.note: 'Citizens of every country' and 'free' replaced by what Samoa Immigration and the UK each state.

entries.old: The entry permit is issued for up to 90 days. If you want to stay longer, the Immigration Division in Apia can extend it: apply before the permit expires, with an onward ticket and evidence of funds. No current fee is published online, so ask the office.
entries.new: The Visitor Permit is issued for up to 90 days. To stay longer, Samoa Immigration says you apply on the temporary residence form, with a copy of an onward ticket, evidence of sufficient funds and details of your accommodation. No current fee is published online.
entries.note: 'Apply before the permit expires' and 'ask the office' are not on the page; the extension uses the temporary residence form.

entries.old: Only a yellow fever certificate, and only if you arrive from or have transited a yellow fever risk country. Samoa's Ministry of Health has no health-related travel restrictions in place, and after the 2019 measles epidemic being up to date with MMR vaccination is sensible. The UK government's travel advice lists dengue and Zika among the health risks, so take precautions against mosquito bites.
entries.new: Only a yellow fever certificate, and only if you arrive from a yellow fever risk country, according to the UK government. Samoa's Ministry of Health has no health-related travel restrictions in place. The UK government lists dengue and Zika among the health risks and advises taking precautions against mosquito bites.
entries.note: 'MMR is sensible' is our advice; the mosquito advice is the UK's and is attributed.

entries.old: A free visitor entry permit valid for up to 90 days is issued on arrival to citizens of every country, provided you hold a passport valid six months, a confirmed onward ticket and accommodation details.
entries.new: Samoa Immigration issues a 90-day Visitor Permit on arrival, using the arrival card, to travellers with a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the stay, confirmed onward tickets, sufficient funds and a confirmed address in Samoa.
entries.note: 'Free' and 'citizens of every country' are not Samoa Immigration's wording.

entries.old: Sierra Leone requires proof of yellow fever vaccination from all arriving travelers. The yellow card is checked by port health officers at Lungi airport and land borders.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Sierra Leone.
entries.note: 'Checked by port health officers at Lungi airport and land borders' is on no official page; the rule is attributed to the UK.

entries.old: No official Sierra Leonean source states an insurance requirement for visitors. Hospital care is very limited, so cover including medical evacuation is advisable.
entries.new: No official Sierra Leonean source states an insurance requirement for visitors. The UK Foreign Office says hospitals, medical facilities and services in Sierra Leone are severely limited.
entries.note: 'Cover including medical evacuation is advisable' is our advice.

entries.old: No official Sierra Leonean source we could read states a cash declaration threshold. Declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to duty, and check with customs before carrying large sums.
entries.new: No official Sierra Leonean source we could read states a cash declaration threshold.
entries.note: Advice removed.

entries.old: If you plan to get the visa on arrival, bring the USD 80 fee in US dollar cash, or apply ahead on the official e-Visa portal, evisa.sl.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says the visa on arrival costs USD 80, paid in cash in US dollars. The official e-Visa portal is evisa.sl.

entries.old: The Government of Canada says the rainy season runs from May to November, with seasonal flooding, mudslides and landslides that can make roads impassable — build slack into any wet-season itinerary.

entries.old: Not an entry requirement: WHO's country list and CDC both state Somalia does not require proof of yellow fever vaccination. entries.old: Malaria is present throughout Somalia all year, with risk lower and seasonal in the north and higher in the centre and south, including Mogadishu. Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

entries.old: Most travelers do not. entries.old: Malaria is transmitted throughout Vanuatu, mainly P. vivax, and the CDC recommends prescription malaria prevention for all travelers. Talk to a travel clinic before you go, and use repellent everywhere against dengue too.

entries.note: 'Use repellent everywhere against dengue' is not on the CDC's Vanuatu page; the doctor advice is the CDC's own.

entries.old: Cash above the declaration threshold set by Vanuatu Customs must be reported on arrival and departure. The country's financial-center status means these rules are enforced, so check the current amount before traveling with large sums.

entries.old: Vanuatu is welcoming with low levels of violent crime; petty theft in Port Vila and occasional unrest are the main concerns. Natural hazards are the bigger factor: a cyclone season that normally runs from November to May, frequent earthquakes, and active volcanoes on Tanna, Ambrym and other islands.
entries.new: The UK Foreign Office says the risk of crime is generally low, but there have been burglaries accompanied by violence and some street crime and attacks on foreign nationals, including tourists at nightclubs and bars in Port Vila. It says Vanuatu is in an active seismic region where volcanic eruptions, earthquakes and tsunamis are possible, and that the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May.
entries.note: 'Welcoming', 'occasional unrest' and 'petty theft' are not the UK's words; it reports violent burglaries and attacks on tourists in Port Vila.

entries.old: The UK FCDO says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May, though cyclones can happen at any time of year, bringing strong winds, heavy rain, flooding, landslides and road closures. Book flexibly and check your insurance.
entries.new: The UK FCDO says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May, though cyclones can happen at any time of year, bringing strong winds, heavy rain, flooding, landslides and road closures.

entries.old: Yemen requires an embassy visa obtained in advance for virtually every nationality — there is no eVisa or visa on arrival — and mainland tourist visas are rarely issued while the armed conflict continues. The US State Department warns that companies outside Yemen have sold trips to the island of Socotra with unofficial, invalid visas; only the Republic of Yemen government can issue a valid one.
entries.new: Yemen requires a visa obtained in advance from a Yemeni diplomatic mission: Canada's travel advice says Yemeni authorities do not issue visas at ports of entry, and the Embassy of Yemen in Washington, which requires an invitation letter from Yemen's Department of Immigration for every application, says it is not issuing tourist visas at this time.

entries.field: FAQ: Can I extend my 90-day stay
entries.old: Under Decree 9,199/2017 (art. 20), the Federal Police can extend a visit visa's stay by up to 90 days, as long as the total stay does not exceed 180 days in each migratory year. The request must be made before the original stay expires, and extensions are available only to nationals of countries that give Brazilians reciprocal treatment. The foreign ministry's visa table caps some nationalities, for example Germans and Italians, at 90 days in every 180.
entries.new: Under Decree 9,199/2017 (art. 20), the Federal Police can extend a visit visa's stay by up to 90 days, as long as the total stay does not exceed 180 days in each migratory year. The request must be made before the original stay expires, and extensions are available only to nationals of countries that give Brazilians reciprocal treatment. Article 23 says the same rule may be applied to nationals of visa-exempt countries. The foreign ministry's visa table caps some nationalities, for example Germans and Italians, at 90 days in every 180.

entries.field: FAQ: can Russian citizens enter Lithuania
entries.old: Russian citizens need a Schengen short-stay visa (Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, Annex I). No official source we could read states Lithuania's current entry restrictions for Russian citizens.
entries.new: Russian citizens need a Schengen short-stay visa (Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, Annex I). Lithuania's Foreign Ministry says that under Law No XIV-1888 its visa authorities abroad have suspended accepting Schengen visa applications from Russian and Belarusian citizens, except where the Ministry mediates the application, for example for family members of Lithuanian or EU citizens or for trips that cannot be postponed. The European Commission says that since 7 November 2025 Russian nationals no longer receive multiple-entry visas.
